Ohio vs Akron prediction, pick against the spread and over/under: I'm on Akron Zips +12.5 and Over 50.5 at DraftKings, with my final at Ohio Bobcats 32, Akron Zips 21. Tuesday night MAC football lands at InfoCision Stadium at 7:00 PM ET on Election Day, and the Zips are throwing a Taco Tuesday theme night for a team that has won once all fall.

Penny Trautman drove up from the Athens brick streets with a thermos and a grin. "Ohio Bobcats are 6-2 and 4-0 in the MAC," she says. "Nick Poulos threw for 266 yards against Eastern Michigan, and Dom Dorwart caught four balls for 125. We lay our wins down one brick at a time."

Hollister "Zip" Grubbs has his tire gauge out at the tailgate. "We're 1-7, Penny, I know. But Jordan Gant ran 28 times for 162 yards and two scores at Kent State. Rubber that's been stretched that far snaps back."

Here is the case for the points. Ohio has won its last four by 3, 17, 41 and 4, and two of those were 13-10 at Kent State and 24-20 over Eastern Michigan. Victor Rosa leads the ground game with 364 yards, and this offense is happy to shorten the night. Akron loses big to good teams, but it played Eastern Michigan to 23-25. My final has Ohio by 11, inside the 12.5.

The worry is Brayden Roggow. He has 9 interceptions on the year, including 4 in the 14-34 loss at Miami (OH). A Bobcats defense led by Michael Molnar, with 5 sacks and 70 tackles, can turn mistakes into a runaway.

On the over/under, Ohio scores 29.6 a game and Akron gives up 32.8. The Zips score 19.0 against an Ohio defense allowing 21.9. The open at DraftKings was 49.5, and it has moved up to 50.5. My 32-21 adds up to 53.

The room is with me on the side. The Formula has Ohio 31-20 and lands on Akron Zips +12.5 and the Over without backing either hard. Next Man Up has Ohio 33-22, takes Akron +12.5, and likes the Over. In The Trenches likes Akron +12.5, reads sides only and has no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "Thirty-three to twenty-two. Eleven points, Zip. Save me a taco."

The Formula: "Eleven again. Still short of the 12.5."

Penny taps a brick she carried up from Athens for luck. Hollister checks the tread on his sneakers and heads for the taco table before the gates fill.

display.fanatic_story:
Ohio Bobcats vs Akron Zips prediction for Tuesday, November 3: Taco Tuesday at InfoCision Stadium, and Penny Trautman of Athens has brought her own hot sauce. The gates open at 6:00 PM in Akron, daylight saving time just ended, and Hollister "Zip" Grubbs swears the extra hour of sleep has his Zips ready to bounce.

It is Election Day in the Rubber City, so the morning belongs to the polls and the Akron Zoo is open free from 11 to 4. By the time the sun goes down, though, the only vote anybody in the parking lot cares about is the one taken on the field under the lights.

"I voted early, I ate early, and I'm sitting early," Penny says, settling into the visitors' side with a brick wrapped in a green scarf. "You know what this is, Zip? This is a Bobcats team that's 6-2 and 4-0 in the MAC. We drove up from the hills to keep building."

Hollister has a notebook full of tread diagrams. "Penny, I have measured every tire in this lot. The wear pattern says one thing. Akron is 1-7, sure, but we played Eastern Michigan to 23-25. We're not flat. We're just low on air."

"Low on air," Penny says, "is a polite way to say you've lost seven of eight."

"And you lost to South Alabama 36-41," Hollister fires back. "I keep notes. Rubber remembers."

The Bobcats arrive with a defense that has stopped arguing with anybody. Michael Molnar sits at 70 tackles and 5 sacks, and he plays like a man who smelled the tacos and wants the opposing offense to miss dinner. Ohio has given up 21.9 points a game all season. Over the last four weeks, the Bobcats beat Kent State 13-10, Central Michigan 31-14, Sacramento State 48-7 and Eastern Michigan 24-20.

"Every one of those was a brick in the wall," Penny says. "Some bricks are pretty. Some are just heavy."

On offense, Nick Poulos has thrown for 781 yards with 6 touchdowns, and he was sharp in that last game against Eastern Michigan, 19 of 29 for 266 yards. Dom Dorwart caught four for 125 that day, and Riley Neer leads the team with 37 catches for 497 yards. Victor Rosa carries the ground game with 364 yards and 5 touchdowns.

"Rosa runs like Athens streets look," Penny says. "Bumpy, old and impossible to knock over."

Hollister nods slowly, then grins. "Fine. Now let me talk about Jordan Gant."

He has earned the floor. Gant ran 28 times for 162 yards and two touchdowns at Kent State, and he owns 618 yards on 127 carries this fall. When the Zips trust him, they look like a different team.

"Gant is vulcanized," Hollister says. "Heat-treated. Stronger under pressure. That's polymer science, Penny. Look it up."

Brayden Roggow is the bigger question. He has thrown for 1,343 yards and 7 touchdowns, but also 9 interceptions, and the four he threw at Miami (OH) still sting. Marcel Williams has 34 catches for 375 yards, and Kyan Mason went for 129 at Kent State. When Roggow keeps the ball out of trouble, Akron can move it.

"If he hands Molnar a gift, we're opening presents early," Penny says.

"If he hits Mason down the far hash," Hollister says, "you'll be tapping that brick so hard it turns to gravel."

Donelius Johnson anchors the Akron defense with 71 tackles, and Cyrus Durham has 2.5 sacks. They will need every one of them against a Bobcats team scoring 29.6 points a game.

The history is not kind to the home crowd. In nine meetings from 2016 to 2024, Ohio won 8 and Akron won 1, the 37-34 game in 2017. The 2024 meeting ended 30-10 for the Bobcats.

"Rubber remembers 2017," Hollister says, tapping his notebook. "BOING."

"Brick remembers the other eight," Penny says, and she offers him a taco anyway, because that's how folks from the hills do it.

Here is how it shakes out. Ohio's defense keeps Roggow honest, Poulos finds Neer and Dorwart for the big plays, and Rosa keeps the chains moving. Akron does not fold. Gant runs hard all night, the Zips hit a couple of shots, and the home crowd gets something to holler about in the fourth quarter. It just isn't enough to swing it.

Penny leaves with her brick. Hollister leaves with a fresh page of tread math and a promise that the Zips will bounce back. Both leave full of tacos.

My call: Ohio Bobcats 32, Akron Zips 21.

Buffalo vs Miami (OH) prediction, pick against the spread and over/under: I'm laying Miami (OH) RedHawks −6.5 and taking Over 44.5 at DraftKings, with my final at Miami (OH) RedHawks 29, Buffalo Bulls 22. Oxford spends Election Day with Party at the Polls under the Bell Tower on High Street, and by 8:00 PM ET the crowd walks past the Cradle of Coaches statues at the south gate of Yager Stadium for a game between two 5-3 teams.

Kendra Woolcott gives the weather report first, the way Western New York does. "Whatever the sky does in Oxford, it isn't lake effect," she says. "Messiah Burch ran 33 times for 184 yards and three scores against Bowling Green. He has 845 yards. We've won three in a row."

Cordelia Van Doren straightens her scarf beside the bronze Bo Schembechler. "So have we, Kendra. Massachusetts, Akron, Central Michigan. And a quiz for you: who won this game in 2025? We did, 37-20."

Here is why I lay it. Miami has won six of the nine meetings since 2016 in the CFBD file, and the RedHawks score 27.0 a game to Buffalo's 22.6. Buffalo has been living on the wire, winning 25-18 in overtime against Massachusetts and 31-28 over Robert Morris. Maleek Huggins has 431 receiving yards, and Roosevelt Andrews III has 4.5 sacks up front. My final has Miami by 7, just past the 6.5.

The quarterback question cuts both ways. Caleb Heavner has taken the most throws in each of Miami's last four games, and he threw 2 interceptions at Central Michigan. David McComb leads the team with 1,121 yards. I'm pricing Heavner, and it still comes out Miami.

For Buffalo, Jason Wright has 987 yards with 7 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and Chance Morrow has 41 catches for 480 yards. If Burch controls the game, the Bulls hang around.

On the over/under, the open at DraftKings was 45.5 and it now sits at 44.5. Miami allows 25.8 and Buffalo allows 25.4, and the 2025 meeting cleared this number by itself. My 29-22 adds up to 51.

The room splits on the side. Next Man Up has Miami 30-22, lays the −6.5 and likes the Over. The Formula has Miami 28-23, takes Buffalo +6.5 and likes the Over. display.fanatic_story:
Buffalo Bulls vs Miami (OH) RedHawks prediction for Tuesday, November 3: Oxford votes all day at the Party at the Polls under the Bell Tower, then votes again at Yager Stadium. Kendra Woolcott drove in from Western New York with a cooler of wings, and Cordelia Van Doren is waiting at the south gate with a trivia card and a smile that means trouble.

The Bell Tower party at 501 E. High Street runs from 11 in the morning until 7:30 at night, and across campus a pianist named Sean Chen takes the stage at 7:30 too. Cordelia has made her choice. She'll take the band, the bricks and the bronze.

"Every visitor walks past my coaches first," she says, gesturing at the 11 bronze statues outside the stadium. "Paul Brown. Weeb Ewbank. Ara Parseghian. Bo Schembechler. John Harbaugh. Sean McVay. Kendra, name one Buffalo statue that tall."

"Name one Oxford wing that's worth the drive," Kendra says, cracking open the cooler. "I'll wait. Weather report, by the way: whatever the sky does tonight, it's not lake effect, so it's not a problem."

Both teams walk in at 5-3, and both sit 3-1 in the MAC. Neither one has lost since early October. Buffalo beat Toledo 23-8, Massachusetts 25-18 in overtime and Bowling Green 31-24. Miami beat Massachusetts 20-19, Akron 34-14 and Central Michigan 28-27.

"We win ugly and we like it," Kendra says. "Ugly travels."

"We win close and we like it," Cordelia says. "Close is a family tradition. Ask the statues."

The Bulls run through Messiah Burch, and there is no polite way to say how much. He carried 33 times for 184 yards and three touchdowns against Bowling Green and has 845 yards on 151 carries. Jason Wright has thrown for 987 yards with 7 touchdowns, and Chance Morrow is the one he looks for, with 41 catches for 480 yards and 6 scores.

"Burch is a snowplow," Kendra says. "You hear him before you see him, and then the road's clear."

Cordelia does not flinch. "Our defense has met snowplows. Roosevelt Andrews III has 4.5 sacks, and Malcolm McCain has 59 tackles. We've been clearing roads in Oxford since before your stadium had a parking lot."

That is a trivia ambush, and Kendra knows it. "You don't know when our parking lot opened."

"No," Cordelia admits. "But you hesitated."

For Miami, the question under center is a two-name story. David McComb leads the team with 1,121 yards and 7 touchdowns, and he threw for 334 at Cincinnati. Caleb Heavner has taken the most throws in each of the last four games, and he went 18 of 33 for 221 yards at Central Michigan, adding 58 on the ground and a touchdown run. Maleek Huggins caught seven balls for 122 yards that day and leads the RedHawks with 431 receiving yards.

"Whoever throws it, Huggins catches it," Cordelia says. "That's not a scheme. That's manners."

Buffalo's defense has its own anchor in SaVeon Brown, with 67 tackles, and Sedrick Vessah has 2 sacks off the corner. The Bulls have given up 25.4 points a game, and Miami has given up 25.8. Nobody in this matchup has been shy about letting the other side score.

"So this is a shootout," Kendra says.

"This is a conversation," Cordelia says. "With scoreboards."

The history tilts her way. In nine meetings from 2016 to 2025, Miami won 6 and Buffalo won 3. The last one, in 2025, ended Miami 37, Buffalo 20. Buffalo's best night in the stretch was a 51-42 win in 2018, and Kendra brings it up before anyone can stop her.

"Fifty-one," she says. "Write that on a statue."

"Even legends lost once," Cordelia says, "and I can tell you which ones."

Here's the shape of it. Burch gets his carries and keeps Buffalo in it through three quarters. Wright finds Morrow for a big score. Miami answers with Huggins over the top, and the RedHawks defense makes one stop late when Buffalo needs a drive. The south gate crowd heads home past the Bell Tower, and Cordelia adds one more gold mark to her chart.

Kendra packs up the cooler. "Just another lake-effect Tuesday," she says, and grins anyway.

My call: Miami (OH) RedHawks 29, Buffalo Bulls 22.

Ball State vs UMass prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Wednesday night in Amherst: I'm on Massachusetts Minutemen −3.5 and Over 49.5, with a final of Massachusetts Minutemen 30, Ball State Cardinals 22. McGuirk Alumni Stadium opens its MAC slate on a Wednesday night built around Salute to Service and Faculty & Staff Appreciation, so the bleachers will be full of professors grading film instead of midterms.

Abner Kettleworth, the Pioneer Valley farmer who grinds tape between harvests, has the case for the hosts. "We dropped four in a row, 14-38 to Eastern Michigan, 19-20 to Miami (OH), 18-25 in overtime at Buffalo and 16-35 at UConn. Fine. But we still score 26.5 a game and allow 21.1. Ball State gives up 35.2. You don't need a roll call to see who brought more men."

Gus Ponder drove in from Muncie with his punt chart rolled up like a diploma. "We won two straight, Abner. Bowling Green 32-31 in overtime, then Sacramento State 34-17. TJ Horton has 425 yards and 9 touchdowns on the ground. Garfield hates Mondays. Good thing this is a Wednesday."

The side begins with the quarterbacks. William Watson III has thrown 8 touchdowns against 2 interceptions. Keldric Luster has 9 touchdowns but 6 interceptions, and the hosts bring a front with William DePaepe at 3 sacks and Timmy Hinspeter running down 72 tackles. Both teams played Sacramento State. UMass won 35-6 on the road. Ball State won 34-17 at home. That gap is the margin I want, and my final has UMass by 8, clear of the 3.5.

On the over/under, Ball State's defense is the reason. The Cardinals surrendered 56 to Ohio State, 51 to Liberty and 45 to Northwestern, and even the Kent State and Toledo nights went 26 and 39 against them. DraftKings opened 48.5 and moved to 49.5. My 30-22 lands at 52.

The room splits on the side. The Formula has Massachusetts 30-23 and likes both the Minutemen −3.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has Massachusetts 31-21 and likes the same two. In The Trenches reads sides only, has no score this week and likes Ball State Cardinals +3.5, so the ground game has Gus smiling. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "Thirty-one to twenty-one, Trenches. Bring a sweater to Amherst."

In The Trenches: "Bring a punt chart. Gus did."

Ball State Cardinals vs UMass Minutemen prediction for Wednesday night, November 4, at McGuirk Alumni Stadium: it's Salute to Service and Faculty & Staff Appreciation night in Amherst, and Abner Kettleworth is already saluting anyone in a uniform or a tweed jacket. Gus Ponder rolled in from Muncie with a whiteboard under one arm and a Garfield tie in his glovebox, just in case.

Wednesday football in the Pioneer Valley is its own animal. University Drive closes to southbound traffic at 2:30 in the afternoon, kids 12 and under get in for $5, and the folks who teach organic chemistry all day are going to spend the night yelling at third-down calls. Abner calls it the best faculty meeting of the year.

"You know what I love about tonight, Gus?" Abner says, adjusting his specs. "The professors grade us, we grade them back. One if by run, two if by throw. And Ball State had better bring both lanterns."

Gus pats his whiteboard. "Abner, I brought a punt chart, a thermos and a joke. Why did the Cardinal sit on the scoreboard? He heard the Minutemen were short on fans up high." He waits. Nothing. "Tough crowd. Jim Davis went to Ball State, you know. Garfield hates Mondays. Lucky for me, it's a Wednesday."

The history is short and even. These two have met four times, and the series sits 2-2. UMass won the first one 26-10 in 1984. Ball State won the last one 20-10 back in 2015 in Muncie. Abner remembers the first. Gus remembers the last. Neither of them will admit to remembering the other.

"Here's my worry," Abner says, and the deadpan cracks just a hair. "We've dropped four in a row. Eastern Michigan rolled us 38-14 right here. Miami (OH) beat us 20-19. Buffalo got us 25-18 in overtime. UConn won 35-16. If I plant one more tree for a loss, the Valley is going to be a forest."

"And I've got the opposite problem," Gus says. "We finally remembered how to win. Bowling Green, 32-31 in overtime. Sacramento State, 34-17. Two in a row, Abner. In Muncie we call that a parade."

The Minutemen have more than hope, though, and Abner knows every name on the roster card. William Watson III has thrown for 1,025 yards with 8 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. He went 19 of 22 for 197 yards and 3 touchdowns in the opener at Rutgers, a 37-21 win that Abner still replays at the kitchen table. T.Y. Harding leads the receivers with 28 catches for 327 yards. Elijah Faulkner carries it on the ground with 376 yards.

"Watson doesn't give the ball away," Abner says. "He treats it like heirloom seed."

On the other side of the field, the Massachusetts defense has a heartbeat named Timmy Hinspeter, who has 72 tackles, and a front with William DePaepe and his 3 sacks. That group held Sacred Heart to 10 and Stonehill to 14 and went to Sacramento State and allowed 6.

Gus is not backing down. Keldric Luster has thrown for 1,300 yards with 9 touchdowns, and when he gets hot he can make a defense look silly. He was 27 of 32 for 256 yards and 3 touchdowns against Stony Brook. TJ Horton is the battering ram in the backfield, 425 yards and 9 touchdowns, and Donovan Hamilton leads the receivers with 310 yards. Kaleb Stewart anchors the Cardinals defense with 37 tackles and 2.5 sacks.

"Horton runs like Garfield going after lasagna," Gus says. "Straight ahead, no apologies, and you are not getting it back."

Abner nods slowly. "Fair. But your defense has given up 56 to Ohio State, 51 to Liberty and 45 to Northwestern. Those are big schools. We are not a big school. We are a stubborn school."

"Stubborn," Gus says, "is my whole punt chart."

Here's the part that makes this one fun. Both teams played Sacramento State this year. The Minutemen won 35-6 out in California. The Cardinals won 34-17 at home. Abner has that written on an index card in his pocket and keeps patting it like it's a pocket watch.

So here is how it plays out under the lights in Amherst. Watson keeps the ball clean, Harding wins on third down, and Faulkner grinds the clock. Ball State hangs around because Horton is real and Luster can hurt you, and Gus gets at least two reasons to stand up and wave the whiteboard. But the Minutemen defense makes one more play when it counts, the veterans in the crowd get a proper Wednesday win to cheer, and the faculty go home with a good grade for the home side.

Abner rings his tiny colonial bell. Gus loosens the Garfield tie and says it sounds like a Monday after all.

My call: Massachusetts Minutemen 30, Ball State Cardinals 22.

Toledo Rockets vs Sacramento State Hornets prediction for Wednesday, November 4: it's Senior Day, Native American Heritage Day and the final game of the year at Hornet Stadium, and Mateo Villaseñor has the whole menu planned. Rocco Szczepanski flew in from the Glass City to tell him the Rockets brought their own engine and a full tank of gas.

This is the first time these two programs have ever met, and it's the first time Sacramento State has ever played a Wednesday MAC night at home. The Hornets will recognize 27 seniors before kickoff. They will wear brand-new uniforms created in consultation with the Wilton Rancheria tribe. And when it's over, there are fireworks scheduled over the stadium for 916 Community night.

"You hear that, Rocco?" Mateo says, tying on an apron over his green and gold. "Fireworks. My mother is coming. My uncle is coming. The guy who sells me tomatoes is coming. Nobody is leaving this kitchen hungry."

Rocco cracks his knuckles. "Mateo, I grew up three streets from the Jeep plant. I grade offenses in horsepower. And the Toledo offense right now? That's four hundred horses and a racing stripe. You're cooking on a camp stove."

"A camp stove that just roasted Kent State 31-10," Mateo fires back. "Five turnovers, Rocco. Five. Fata Puloka forced two fumbles. Miles Bailey jumped on two more. We held the ball for nearly 35 minutes. That is slow food. That is a braise."

He is not wrong, and Rocco knows it. That was the first MAC win in Hornets history and their first win over an FBS team since the move up. Isaiah Ene ran for 107 yards and two touchdowns that night, and he leads the team with 410 yards on the season. Matt Coleman is the top receiver with 41 catches for 492 yards and 5 touchdowns. Boogsie Silvera roams the back of the defense with 71 tackles, and he hits like he's tenderizing a steak.

"Silvera is my secret ingredient," Mateo says. "You don't see him, you just taste him."

Rocco just smiles and lists parts. John Alan Richter has thrown for 2,244 yards with 17 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. He threw for 429 yards in the overtime win over Temple and 391 against Western Michigan. CJ Miller has 609 yards and 7 touchdowns, and he carried it 33 times for 183 yards in that 45-38 win over the Broncos. Adjatay Dabbs is the deep threat, with 592 yards and 7 touchdowns.

"Then there's Andrew Zock," Rocco says. "Eight sacks. That's not a defensive end, that's a tow truck. He shows up and your quarterback goes for a ride."

"Jackson Sharman has been sacked before," Mateo says. "He gets up. He has thrown for 1,363 yards and 8 touchdowns this season. He's a short-order cook. He keeps the tickets moving."

The scoreboards are not kind to the Hornets this fall, and Mateo will tell you so himself. Fresno State beat them 49-3. Ohio won 48-7 here. Massachusetts came in and won 35-6. Ball State took a 34-17 win in Muncie. The record sits at 2-7, and the kitchen has had some long nights.

"Back to the kitchen," Mateo says, the way he does after every loss. "But Kent State was the night the sauce came together. You don't forget that recipe."

Toledo has its own scars. Buffalo beat the Rockets 23-8 in the Glass Bowl. Michigan State won 30-20 in the opener. Rocco calls those engine trouble and moves on, because 6-2 is 6-2, and the Rockets have scored at least 34 in seven of their last eight games.

"And here's the thing about the schedule," Rocco says, lowering his voice. "We last played October 24. Rested. Tuned. You played Friday night and turn around five days later. I'm not saying that's unfair. I'm saying our engine has been sitting in the garage cooling."

Mateo shrugs. "Seniors don't get tired on Senior Day."

So here is how it shakes out under the California sky. Richter finds Dabbs early, Miller grinds out the middle, and Zock makes Sharman's night a little too exciting. The Rockets build a real cushion by the second half. But the Hornets do not fold on their seniors. Ene keeps churning, Coleman makes a couple of grabs that bring the home crowd to its feet, and Silvera makes one of those hits the seniors will talk about at reunions. Toledo wins comfortably, and the fireworks still go off for Sacramento State.

Rocco does his burnout gesture in the aisle. Mateo gives a chef's kiss to his seniors anyway.

My call: Toledo Rockets 38, Sacramento State Hornets 18.

Imogen Tremblay showed up with a spreadsheet titled "Fan Challenge" and a bag of canned soup, because this rivalry now keeps score off the field too.

Here's the deal. The two schools are competing in a Fan Challenge that awards points for the most food donated to the MAC's annual Canned Food Drive, for social media support, for tickets donated to Detroit-area youth and first responders, and for a chef cook-off between the two universities. On game day, fans score points for wearing their colors and cheering loud. General admission in the end zones costs $20. Eastern Michigan is the home team this year. Central Michigan gets that title in 2027.

"Ope, sorry, Imogen," Brynn says, clearly not sorry. "Did you say home team? Ford Field is our home away from home. We've played here 11 times. Six bowl games. Four MAC title games. I could find the Chippewas tunnel blindfolded."

Imogen pushes up her glasses. "Brynn, I'm from Ypsilanti. I have spent my entire life being the little sibling of Ann Arbor. I am not about to be the little sibling of Mount Pleasant. I donated eleven cans of chickpeas. The spreadsheet is very green."

This series has been going since November 1, 1902, and it's the longest-running rivalry in the MAC at 103 games. Central Michigan leads it 65-32-6. Over the last ten meetings, the Chippewas won six and the Eagles won four. Last year Central won 24-13. The year before, Eastern won a wild one 38-34.

"Thirty-eight to thirty-four," Imogen says, closing her eyes like she's at a concert. "I have that game framed."

"I have last year framed," Brynn says. "Bigger frame."

Then the arguing gets serious, because these two know their rosters like the back of their hands.

Brynn goes first. Angel Flores is the engine of the Central Michigan offense, and he does it with his legs. He has run for 618 yards and 4 touchdowns, which makes him the team's leading rusher as a quarterback. When the Chippewas needed to throw against Miami (OH), Jadyn Glasser went 18 of 31 for 221 yards, and Langston Lewis caught 10 balls for 163 yards in a one-point loss. Mayson Hitchens leads the defense with 62 tackles, and Jaxon Cherry has 3 sacks.

"Lewis against Miami was a snowmobile on fresh powder," Brynn says. "Nobody was catching him."

"Except the scoreboard," Imogen says. "Twenty-eight to twenty-seven."

Brynn retreats briefly to her imaginary deer camp.

Imogen takes the floor. Noah Kim has thrown for 1,678 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 4 interceptions. Joshua Long is the go-to tight end with 42 catches for 383 yards. Amareon Blue leads the ground game with 405 yards. And then there is Quincy Byas, who has 5 sacks and plays like he's personally offended by quarterbacks. Zach Mowchan backs him up with 58 tackles.

"Byas is the green cell," Imogen says. "Every spreadsheet needs one."

The two common opponents make this even tighter. Both beat Akron, Central by 41-17 and Eastern by 25-23. Both lost at Ohio, Central 31-14 and Eastern 24-20. Eastern has the better league mark at 3-2, while Central is 1-3. Central has dropped three straight, the last one that 28-27 heartbreaker. Eastern has dropped two straight too.

"So we're both hungry," Brynn says.

"We're both bringing canned food," Imogen says. "Literally hungry is the theme."

Here's how it plays out under the roof downtown. It is close all night. Kim moves the Eagles with Long working the middle, and Byas gets home at least once to make the Eastern section shake. Flores keeps the Chippewas alive on the ground, Lewis wins a big third down, and the defense led by Hitchens gets one critical stop late. The whole building is loud enough to win a few Fan Challenge points for both sides. In the end, a single point separates them, and the food drive is the real winner.

UTSA Roadrunners vs Florida Atlantic Owls prediction for Thursday, November 5: it is Night Market night in downtown Boca Raton, and Kaia Brightwater has already walked Sanborn Square twice. Marisol Ybarra came in from San Antonio with a Fiesta medal on her cap and a 7-1 team behind her, and the two of them are settling this one before the Owls ever leave the tunnel.

The market runs from six to nine on Thursday evening, with local makers, music, sweet treats and a free BocaConnect shuttle hauling people downtown. Kaia knows every table. She knows the dark chocolate guy, the jam lady and the vanilla booth. She also knows Florida Atlantic football scores in bunches, and she wants Marisol to hear it twice.

"Thirty-seven point eight a game," Kaia says, holding up a jar of jam like a trophy. "That's us. That's Caden Veltkamp. Two thousand five hundred thirty-six yards and 23 touchdown throws, and he's not done."

Marisol nibbles a sample of chocolate and smiles. "Mija, I love a big offense. I married one. But UTSA is 4-0 in the American. We beat Tulane 42-19 on their own field. Owen McCown does not panic. He reads the field like a parade route. Left at the Alamo, right at the river, and he never drops the float."

Here is the thing Kaia will not say out loud: Florida Atlantic gives up 35.8 points a game. Army hung 56 on the Owls in October. North Texas went for 48 last week, even with Veltkamp throwing for 452 yards and five touchdowns and Easton Messer catching 16 balls for 189 yards.

"Sixteen catches," Kaia says. "Sixteen. Easton Messer is a wave that does not stop breaking. Seventy-four catches, 898 yards, nine touchdowns. Find me a Roadrunner who can keep up with that."

Marisol does not even look up. "Brandon Tucker has 56 tackles. Owen Pewee has four sacks. And we have Will Henderson III, who ran for 102 yards at Tulane and has 664 on the year. When we get the lead, Kaia, we hand the ball to Will and you watch your offense sit on the bench eating jam."

That is the whole fight. UTSA has won five in a row, and most of them were tight. Sixteen to fourteen at Rice. Thirty-eight to thirty-four over Navy. The Roadrunners do not blow people out on the road very often. They just keep running until the other side runs out of road.

"You guys squeak," Kaia says. "That's your whole personality. Squeak, squeak, beep beep."

"And you guys swim," Marisol says. "Beautifully. Right up until the fourth quarter, when you notice the tide went out."

Florida Atlantic has its own proof. The Owls beat Navy 38-30 in September with Veltkamp going 27 of 32 for 386 yards and five touchdowns. They beat Rice 51-49. When the Owls get going in their own building, the stadium gets loud and the ocean breeze feels like it is pushing the ball downfield.

The history is split right down the middle. Florida Atlantic won 40-26 in 2019 and 24-3 in 2020. UTSA won 36-10 in 2023 and 38-24 in 2024. Two apiece in the recent meetings, so nobody gets to brag at the jam table.

"Two and two," Marisol says. "Tonight breaks the tie."

"Tonight," Kaia says, "breaks your heart."

McCown is the steady hand. He has 1,751 yards with 10 touchdowns and only four interceptions, and he threw for 359 yards against Navy when the Roadrunners needed all of them. DJ Allen Jr. leads the receivers with 347 yards. Florida Atlantic needs Joseph Sipp Jr., who leads the Owls with 57 tackles and two sacks, to get into McCown's face early.

Here is how it shakes out. Veltkamp and Messer give the Boca crowd plenty to scream about, and the Owls keep the game within reach all night. UTSA answers every punch, Henderson grinds the fourth quarter, and McCown makes the late throw that matters. The Owls hang around right to the end. The Roadrunners just do what they have done for five straight games and finish.

Kaia buys one more square of dark chocolate on the way out of the square. Marisol buys the jam, because a Roadrunner always brings something home from the road.

My call: UTSA Roadrunners 38, Florida Atlantic Owls 32.

display.fanatic_story:
James Madison Dukes vs Southern Miss Golden Eagles prediction for Thursday, November 5: Hattiesburg has a photography show hanging on Pearl Street, and Lila Shenandoah walked through it before dinner. Dee Broussard met her at the door, because if a Duke is going to spend a day on the Southern Miss campus, a Golden Eagle is going to give the tour.

The exhibit is called Two Photographers: Don Norris and Betty Press, at the Gallery of Art and Design in the George Hurst Building. Frozen moments, every one of them. Dee thinks that is exactly how James Madison should be remembered after Thursday night: a nice picture of a team that used to be rolling.

"Look at this one," Dee says, pointing at a print. "That's the Dukes in October. Pretty. In the past."

Lila laughs, the cheer-captain laugh that carries to the top row. "Dee, we're 7-2. We're first in the Sun Belt East. We beat Wagner 87-3. Our defense gives up 18.9 points a game. You want a photograph? Frame the scoreboard."

Dee has an answer ready. "Two straight overtime losses, Lila. App State got you 34-31. Troy got you 24-21 in your own house. You've been staring at overtime coin flips for two weeks."

That one lands, and Lila knows it. Camden Coleman has been the steady hand all fall, with 1,742 yards, 16 touchdown throws and only four interceptions. But he threw two against Troy, and the Dukes needed Seth Cromwell's 135 rushing yards just to get to extra time.

"Camden's fine," Lila says. "And George Pettaway is better than fine. Eight hundred twenty-four yards. Eight touchdowns. He runs like the Blue Ridge, all climb and no quit."

Southern Miss has its own snapshot to show off. The Golden Eagles won their last two, 35-31 over Louisiana and 35-21 at UL Monroe, and Steven Robinson carried 21 times for 151 yards in Monroe. He has 728 yards and nine touchdowns on the year. Mario Sanders leads the receivers with 44 catches for 600 yards, and Landry Lyddy has thrown for 1,326.

"Robinson is the whole show," Dee says. "You can hang him in this gallery. Title it 'Gone.'"

The defense in Hattiesburg is the question. Southern Miss gives up 31.0 points a game, and Auburn and UConn both ran away from the Golden Eagles in September. Mathis Haygood leads the team with 70 tackles and has been everywhere, but the Eagles need Jameer Lewis and his four sacks to get after Coleman early.

"If Jameer gets home twice," Dee says, "Lila does her cheers in a whisper."

"If Jameer gets home twice," Lila says, "Nakian Jackson gets home three times. Sixty-six tackles, Dee. He's going to be in Lyddy's backfield so often your kids will think he's family."

The history is short and it belongs to the Dukes. James Madison beat Southern Miss 32-15 in 2024, the only regular-season meeting in recent years.

"One photograph," Dee says. "One. I don't hang a whole wall on one picture."

"You should," Lila says. "It's a good one."

Friday night, the Mannoni Performing Arts Center opens Natasha, Pierre and the Great Comet of 1812. Dee says Thursday will be its own comet, the Golden Eagles flying across the sky. Lila says comets burn up when they get too close.

Here is how it shakes out. Robinson makes the home crowd loud early, and Southern Miss stays in it longer than anyone in Harrisonburg wants. But Coleman cleans it up, Pettaway wears down the Golden Eagles in the second half, and the James Madison defense gets the stops it needs. The Dukes break their two-game skid without needing another overtime.

Dee says she will be back at the gallery next week to choose a new print. Lila says she already has one: the final scoreboard.

My call: James Madison Dukes 36, Southern Miss Golden Eagles 23.

"And you lost," Ruthanne says.

"By three. 27-30. On the road. Up there in the cold." Tatum waves a hand. "Kevin comes home, Kevin gets warm, Kevin cooks."

SMU has cooked plenty in Dallas this fall. The Mustangs beat UC Davis 56-10, Missouri State 34-24, Boston College 25-16 and California 59-20 at home. Kendrick Raphael has 692 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Yamir Knight leads the receivers with 523 yards.

Ruthanne answers with the thing Virginia Tech always answers with: defense and patience. Aycen Stevens has eight sacks this year, and she says he gets off the ball like a drum major hitting the first beat.

"Eight," she says. "Kevin Jennings is going to meet Aycen Stevens enough times Friday that they'll exchange Christmas cards."

"Two interceptions," Ruthanne says. "In eight games. Our quarterback treats the football like a family heirloom."

South Florida Bulls vs East Carolina Pirates prediction for Friday, November 6: downtown Greenville throws its First Friday ArtWalk that night, from 5 to 8, with a free Emerald Express trolley rolling past the galleries about every 20 minutes. Bart Quidley plans to ride it straight from the art to the stadium. Reina Valdés-Kowalski plans to ride it straight from the stadium back to the art, because she says that will be the only pretty thing the Pirates fans see all night.

Bart has tailgated in the same patch of Pitt County grass for so long his uncles mark it with a lawn chair in August. He meets Reina at the ECU Proctor Yongue House, where the porch show is called Pirates on the Porch: Wild Friends.

"Wild Friends," he says. "That's what we call visiting teams. We're wild and you're our friend until kickoff."

Reina laughs. She drove up from Tampa with sunscreen she will not need and a Bulls sweatshirt she will. "Bart, we're 6-2. We give up 14.5 points a game. We held Kent State to two points. Two. We beat UAB 30-10 last week. My defense doesn't make friends."

Bart has the memory card ready. "Three straight, Reina. Last three meetings. 44-24. 29-14. 48-28. We eat the Bulls."

That stings, and Reina knows the rest of the history too. South Florida won the four before that, including a 61-31 blowout in 2017. Across those seven meetings, South Florida has four wins and East Carolina has three.

"Old news," she says. "You want old news, go to the holiday show."

There is one, as it happens. The 25th annual Down East Holiday Show runs in Greenville that week, with more than 180 small businesses selling everything from candles to Christmas ornaments. Bart says the Pirates will be gift-wrapping a win for the home crowd. Reina says she will buy a souvenir to remember the night ECU fans went quiet.

East Carolina comes in at 4-4, and Bart admits it has been a bumpy ride. The Pirates lost two straight in overtime in October, 17-30 at UAB and 34-41 at Memphis, before beating Temple 17-9. TJ Engleman Jr. carried 16 times for 107 yards in that win and has 689 yards on the year. DJ Johnson Jr. leads the defense with 56 tackles.

"Engleman runs like a farm truck with no brakes," Bart says. "And when he gets going, the whole stadium gets going."

Reina is worried about her own offense, and she says so. Michael Van Buren Jr. has thrown for 1,273 yards, but Luke Kromenhoek ran the show against UAB, carrying 15 times for 92 yards. D.J. Crowther has 578 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, and C.J. Hicks has five sacks on defense.

"Whoever's throwing," she says, "we run it and we hit you. That's the South Florida way this year."

"Your way scored 13 against Temple," Bart says.

"And you scored 17 against Temple and needed a lawn chair to celebrate."

The quarterback in purple is the question for Bart. Mitch Griffis has 753 passing yards, four touchdown throws and five interceptions. Ray Ray Joseph Jr. leads the Pirates with 303 receiving yards. If Griffis gives Reina's defense extra chances, the Bulls do not need much offense.

Here is how it shakes out. Engleman makes the home crowd loud, and East Carolina has the lead late in a game that never gets loose. But the South Florida defense makes one more stop than the Pirates do, Crowther punches one in, and the Bulls sneak out of Greenville by a single point.

Reina rides the trolley back downtown to see the art. Bart rides it too, quietly, and says the paintings look better when you lose.

My call: South Florida Bulls 23, East Carolina Pirates 22.

New Mexico Lobos vs Nevada Wolf Pack prediction for Friday, November 6: the Reno Public Market has Margret's Funk Band playing for free that night from 7 to 10, and Paloma Begaye-Ortiz has already decided that is where she will warm up. Ridge Corbell tells her funk is fine, but the only music in Reno that matters is the noise at Mackay Stadium.

Paloma pilots hot-air balloons over Albuquerque, so she talks about everything in terms of altitude. "We're 7-1, Ridge. Number 22 in the country. First in the Mountain West. We are flying so high you need binoculars."

Ridge patrols the slopes at Tahoe and has pulled a lot of overconfident people out of the snow. "Balloons come down, Paloma. Usually in somebody's field."

New Mexico has plenty to brag about. The Lobos give up 11.9 points a game. Darren Agu has six sacks. Mercury Swaim has 50 tackles. Scottre Humphrey has 11 rushing touchdowns, and Kiefer Sibley ran for 102 yards in a 21-16 win at San Jose State last week.

"Mercury Swaim," Paloma says. "Even his name is fast."

Ridge goes right at the quarterback. Toa Fa'avae threw three interceptions at San Jose State, and he has seven on the year against only six touchdown throws. The Lobos have scored 21 points in each of their last three wins.

"Your quarterback throws to my guys like he's handing out lift tickets," Ridge says. "EJ Smith has 85 tackles. He's going to find Toa."

Paloma waves it off. "Toa doesn't need to throw. We run. We hit. We win. Ask Hawai'i. Ask North Dakota State."

Nevada's year has been rough, and Ridge admits it. The Wolf Pack are 3-5 and were shut out 0-27 at UCLA last week. Carter Jones leads the team with 654 passing yards, and Gary Givens III leads the receivers with 305. Dylan LaBarbera has four and a half sacks.

"We beat San Jose State 28-13 the week before," Ridge says. "Same team you squeaked past. We can play with anybody at Mackay."

The history gives him something to hold on to. Since 2016, Nevada has won three of the five meetings, including 34-24 in 2023. New Mexico won the last one 24-22 last year.

"Two points," Paloma says. "Close, but we went home happy."

"Close is all we need Friday," Ridge says.

The cold is part of Ridge's case. He swears the Lobos have never felt a Reno November, and he expects them to be stiff by the second quarter. Paloma tells him balloon pilots get up before dawn in the desert cold all fall. Cold doesn't scare her. Wind does, and she says the Wolf Pack aren't strong enough to make any.

Paloma has a few more numbers for the drive home. New Mexico beat UTEP 61-7 and Mercyhurst 70-7, and the only loss came 6-14 at Oklahoma in September.

"Six points at Oklahoma," Ridge says. "Your offense went for a balloon ride and forgot to come down."

"And we still only gave up 14 to the Sooners," Paloma says. "Ask your guys how they did against Montana State."

Ridge winces. Nevada lost 7-20 at home to Montana State and 33-36 in overtime to Air Force. But the Wolf Pack opened the year with a 49-14 win over Western Kentucky, and Ridge swears that team still lives somewhere inside Mackay.

Here is how it shakes out. Nevada's defense hangs around early, and Fa'avae gives Ridge a scare or two. But the New Mexico run game wears the Wolf Pack down, the Lobos' defense keeps Nevada out of the end zone when it counts, and New Mexico pulls away in the second half to stay on top of the Mountain West.

Paloma heads back downtown to catch the last of the funk band. Ridge goes with her, because a ski patroller knows when to call it a night.

My call: New Mexico Lobos 28, Nevada Wolf Pack 17.

TCU Horned Frogs vs Arizona Wildcats prediction for Friday, November 6: downtown Tucson is throwing the Greek Festival in Jácome Plaza that weekend, and Inez Paloverde has a plan. She is taking Ryder Galloway to Papou's Cafe for Greek coffee and loukoumades, the little honey-soaked doughnuts, before the late kickoff. She says it is Tucson hospitality. Ryder says it is a sugar trap.

Ryder grew up around the Fort Worth Stockyards and now works in finance downtown. He still wears the boots. Inez plays piccolo in the Arizona band and swears it never really gets cold in the desert, even in November.

"Ryder," she says, "you're going to love it here. Warm night, sweet food, and a Wildcats win."

"I'll take two out of three," Ryder says. "And I'm not picky about which two."

Arizona has given Inez plenty to play for. The Wildcats are 6-2 and ranked No. 24. Noah Fifita has 2,481 passing yards, 19 touchdown throws and only four interceptions. Isaiah Mizell caught seven balls for 182 yards at Texas Tech last week. Arizona scores 34.9 points a game and beat Iowa State 39-3 two weeks ago.

"Noah throws the ball like I play piccolo," Inez says. "High, sharp and right on the note."

Ryder points to the loss. "And you still lost 26-34 in Lubbock. Fifita threw for 417 and you lost."

TCU does not win pretty, and Ryder doesn't care. The Frogs are 4-4, but they give up just 14.1 points a game. They beat Kansas 22-16 last week and Baylor 17-6 in October, and their four losses came by five, eight, seven and four.

"We count every point twice in Fort Worth," Ryder says. "Koron Hayward has five and a half sacks. Jamel Johnson has 50 tackles. Nobody runs away from us."

Jaden Craig has been steady, with 2,207 yards, 11 touchdown throws and six interceptions. He ran for 87 yards against Kansas and trusts Kari Ashley, the tight end, who has 38 catches for 560 yards.

"Kari Ashley is a tight end who runs like a calf at a rodeo," Ryder says. "You'll see."

Inez answers with defense of her own. Chase Kennedy has six sacks and Taye Brown has 47 tackles. "Your quarterback is going to meet Chase so many times Friday he'll want to sit at Yia Yia's House with the grandmas."

The festival has a spot called Yia Yia's House, and a Kids Zone too. Ryder says he might hide in the Kids Zone if the Wildcats get rolling early.

The history is short. The only recent meeting was in 2024, and TCU won it 49-28.

"Forty-nine," Ryder says. "On you."

"That was a different Arizona," Inez says. "This one is ranked."

The two teams have one more common thread, and both of them want to talk about it. Arizona went to Morgantown and beat West Virginia 52-31. TCU lost 20-24 to the same Mountaineers at home two weeks later.

"Fifty-two," Inez says, holding up her piccolo like a pointer. "You scored twenty."

"And BYU beat you by 11 in Provo," Ryder says. "BYU beat us by seven. Same Cougars."

Inez shrugs. Kedrick Reescano has seven rushing touchdowns, and she says he is the closer when the Wildcats get near the end zone. Ryder says the Frogs have closed doors on better.

Here is how it shakes out. The TCU defense hangs in, Craig makes some plays with his legs, and the Frogs keep it close into the second half. But Fifita finds Mizell for the big plays, Kennedy gets after Craig, and Arizona pulls away just enough in the fourth quarter to send the home crowd out happy.

Inez buys Ryder a second plate of loukoumades to soften the blow. Ryder eats them anyway and says Tucson is all right, for a desert.

My call: Arizona Wildcats 26, TCU Horned Frogs 17.

Texas vs Missouri prediction for Saturday in Columbia, from two people who have been arguing about this game since the schedule came out. Caroline Whitfield bleeds burnt orange and has never once lowered her voice in a stadium. Delphine Arceneaux-Moss has followed Mizzou from the press box and the student section and will tell you which one has better coffee.

Delphine: Saturday morning, the Columbia Farmers Market sets up its winter market at 1769 West Ash. Local growers, local bakers, local folks who have watched a lot of visiting teams leave town quiet. I want every Texas fan in Columbia to go. Buy something from a farmer. Learn something about patience, because you are going to need it at Faurot Field.

Caro: Patience is a word people use when they are about to lose. I will go to the market. I will buy whatever is in season. I will wear burnt orange in the produce aisle and nobody will say a thing, because we are 6-2 and ranked No. 10 and everybody in Columbia knows it.

Delphine: You are 6-2 with two losses by three points each. Oklahoma 27, Texas 24. Florida 27, Texas 24. Same score twice. That is not a football team, that is a recurring dream.

Caro: And you lost to Florida, too? Oh wait, no. You beat Florida 45-17. Then you went to Oxford and scored 3 points. Three. I have seen higher numbers on a thermometer in Austin in January.

Delphine: Ole Miss was a bad night. We answered it. We went to Arkansas and won 34-10, and Jamal Roberts carried it 23 times for 138 yards. He has 1,005 yards this year and 9 touchdowns. He runs like the field owes him money.

Caro: Roberts is a real back. I will give you that one, free of charge, like a free sample. But you have not seen Colin Simmons up close. He has 10.5 sacks. Your quarterback is going to spend Saturday looking over his shoulder like somebody is following him home from the library.

Delphine: Speaking of the library, the Columbia Public Library is holding a Local Authors Open House Saturday. You should go. Ask somebody to write a happy ending for a team that keeps losing by three.

Caro: Clever. Here is my happy ending. Arch Manning has 1,727 yards and 15 touchdown throws. Last week against Mississippi State he went 16 of 20 for 220 yards and 3 touchdowns, and Texas won 31-3. Emmett Mosley caught 4 balls for 98 yards. That is a quarterback who is finding his rhythm in November, which is the month that matters.

Delphine: Austin Simmons has 1,952 yards, 16 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. Two. Your guy has 7. If we are comparing who protects the football, I will take the man who treats it like a family recipe.

Caro: Seven interceptions is a number I will own. He also has eight more touchdowns than interceptions. And Texas scores 30.8 a game while giving up 17.1. You score 31.5 and give up 18.4. Basically identical, except one of us has a defense that makes quarterbacks nervous.

Delphine: Daeden Hopkins has 7 sacks for us. Nicholas Rodriguez has 84 tackles. You think the Texas rush gets to show up and our front just watches? We beat Texas A&M 27-6. Ask the Aggies how much fun it was.

Caro: I would never ask the Aggies anything. That is one thing Texas and Missouri agree on.

Delphine: Finally, common ground. Here is my other point. Your team has to travel north for a game in November. You will get off the plane, feel the wind, and wonder why Columbia smells like woodsmoke and cider.

Caro: It smells like a road win, and I am going to enjoy every bite of it. The Longhorns are bringing Ryan Wingo, who has 470 receiving yards, and Raleek Brown, who has 452 on the ground. Nobody in your secondary has seen speed like Wingo's since the last time a Texas team came through.

Delphine: Fine. Here is what happens. The market closes, the tailgates fill up, Faurot Field gets loud, and Roberts runs downhill for four quarters. Mizzou keeps it close all day.

Caro: Close, yes. I will agree with close. Simmons gets to your quarterback when it matters, Manning finds Wingo for the play everybody talks about on Sunday, and the Saturday market crowd waves goodbye to the burnt orange as we drive south.

Delphine: You are buying souvenirs at the market before you leave, aren't you.

Caro: Two bags. One for me and one for the trophy case.

My call: Texas Longhorns 25, Missouri Tigers 21.

BYU vs Utah prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium: on Friday night, downtown Salt Lake City has Alex Boyé's The King of New York at the Eccles Theater on Main Street, a show built on faith, history and pioneer stories. Saturday at noon ET, a few blocks up the hill, the history gets louder. No. 7 BYU at 7-1, No. 3 Utah at 8-0, and a market that has run hard one way.

DraftKings opened Utah −3 with the over/under at 51.5. It is now Utah −5.5 and 47.5. Money came in on the Utes and against the points at the same time. I am with the first move and against the second. My side is Utah Utes −5.5, and my number is Over 47.5.

First, the part BYU fans will throw back at me: BYU won the last two meetings, 22-21 in 2024 and 24-21 in 2025. Two one-score games, both decided late. In the seven meetings since 2016, Utah won 4 and BYU won 3. Fine. This Utah team is different. It scores 38.9 a game and allows 15.9, and Devon Dampier has 1,876 yards, 18 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Last week at Cincinnati he went 22 of 29 for 260 and 3 scores in a 49-25 win, with Hunter Andrews catching 5 for 112 and 2 touchdowns. Wayshawn Parker has 726 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns.

BYU is no pushover. Bear Bachmeier has 1,750 yards with 12 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and Legend Glasker has 585 receiving yards. The Cougars beat Notre Dame 28-24 and Arizona State 27-20, and their only loss was 31-39 in overtime at UCF. They score 32.4 and allow 18.8. They will find points. I just think Utah finds more of them, and a game where both teams clear 20 gets over 47.5 quickly.

Now the room, because this one splits. The Formula has Utah 29-24 and takes BYU +5.5 with the Over. Next Man Up has Utah 32-21 and likes Utah −5.5 and the Over, which is basically my ticket with a bigger margin. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. In The Trenches calls the front-line matchup split and gives no side. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula crew will tell you five points is a lot to lay in a rivalry that has been a coin flip. I will tell you they projected Utah to win by five and then took the points anyway. Pick a lane.

Utah Utes 30, BYU Cougars 22 is my score. The Utes control the clock with Parker, Dampier finds a big play to Pegan or Andrews, and BYU spends the fourth quarter chasing.

Utah Utes 30, BYU Cougars 22. Utah Utes cover the 5.5. Over 47.5.

display.fanatic_story:
BYU vs Utah prediction for Saturday at Rice-Eccles, from two people who cannot share a car ride without it turning into a debate. Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi guides hikers up the trails above Provo and points out the Y on the mountain to anybody who will listen. Aspen Mortensen raced downhill for years and still takes every corner like there is a clock on it.

Aspen: Friday night, downtown, the Eccles Theater on Main Street has Alex Boyé and The King of New York. Faith, history, pioneer stories, all set to hip-hop. You should come up early, Bryce. It will be the last time all weekend somebody in Salt Lake tells a story where BYU comes out on top.

Bryce: The story where BYU comes out on top is the last two years. Twenty-two to twenty-one in 2024. Twenty-four to twenty-one in 2025. I do not need a musical for that. I have the scores memorized and set to my own soundtrack.

Aspen: A one-point game and a three-point game. You are framing a pair of photo finishes like they were blowouts. We are 8-0. We are No. 3 in the country. We score 38.9 points a game. You could drive down from Provo, get lost on the way, and still miss fewer points than your defense will.

Bryce: You scored 21 both of the last two years. Same number twice, both losses. Your team has a ceiling and it is painted crimson.

Aspen: Devon Dampier has 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns. Last week at Cincinnati he went 22 of 29 for 260 and 3 scores. Hunter Andrews caught 5 balls for 112 yards and 2 touchdowns, and we won 49-25. That is not a ceiling. That is a ski lift.

Bryce: Bear Bachmeier has 1,750 yards, 12 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. He has thrown three fewer interceptions than your guy. When I take people hiking, the first rule is do not take risks you do not need to take. Bear follows the trail. Dampier jumps off ledges and hopes there is snow.

Aspen: There is always snow up here, Bryce. That is the point. And Wayshawn Parker has 726 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns. He runs like he is late for the Disney On Ice show at the Delta Center this weekend. Find Your Hero, it is called. Your secondary is going to be looking for one all afternoon.

Bryce: Our secondary will be fine. We beat Notre Dame 28-24. We beat Arizona State 27-20 last week. Our only loss came in overtime at UCF, 39-31, and I still say that one was a road trip that went a little long.

Aspen: A little long. That is how you describe losing to UCF. We went to Colorado and won 27-24. We beat Arkansas 43-10. We held Utah State to zero. Zero. Your mountain has a letter on it, ours has a scoreboard.

Bryce: Legend Glasker has 585 receiving yards. You know what a legend is? Somebody people talk about for generations. Nobody is writing songs about Braden Pegan.

Aspen: Braden Pegan has 505 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns. Glasker has 4. If you want to talk about legends, talk about touchdowns, because that is what people remember on the drive home.

Bryce: The drive home is going to be long for you if this is close in the fourth quarter. The last two years it was. BYU knows how to win these. Utah knows how to explain them.

Aspen: Here is what I know. We score 38.9 and allow 15.9. You score 32.4 and allow 18.8. Both numbers point the same direction, and it is uphill toward Rice-Eccles. The crowd is going to be loud, the air is going to be cold, and every one of those red sweaters in the stands has been waiting two years for this.

Bryce: You have been waiting since 2024. We have been enjoying it since 2024. That is a different kind of waiting.

Aspen: Enjoy it on the hike back down. Dampier hits a big one early, Parker grinds the clock in the second half, and Bachmeier spends the fourth quarter throwing into a crowd of red jerseys.

Bryce: Fine. I will come up Friday, watch the show, and stay for the game. If Utah wins, I will buy dinner. If BYU wins, you have to hike the Y with me in November.

Aspen: Deal. Bring a jacket. You will want something to hide the blue.

My call: Utah Utes 30, BYU Cougars 22.

Iowa State vs Baylor prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at McLane Stadium: this is Baylor Homecoming, the whole of Waco is wearing green and gold, and the Waco Downtown Farmers Market on Bridge Street will be open a few hours before the noon ET kickoff. Iowa State comes in at 4-4. Baylor is 5-3. The market has not moved an inch.

DraftKings opened Baylor −9.5 with the over/under at 50.5 and it is still sitting at Baylor −9.5 and 50.5. Nobody blinked. I am laying it. My side is Baylor Bears −9.5, and my number is Over 50.5.

The Baylor case is defense and a quarterback who just found his range. The Bears allow 15.2 points a game, and their three losses came 16-17 to Auburn, 6-17 to TCU and 24-25 at Kansas. Nobody has blown them out. DJ Lagway has 1,671 yards with 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and last week at UCF he went 16 of 25 for 319 and 4 scores in a 41-9 win. Gavin Freeman has 63 catches for 792 yards and caught 5 for 114 in that game.

Iowa State is a weird team to price. It beat Oklahoma State 51-49 last week, with Jaylen Raynor throwing for 309 and 3 touchdowns, Aiden Flora carrying 29 times for 221, and Jamal Polite Jr. catching 6 for 171. A week earlier it lost 3-39 at Arizona. The Cyclones score 29.0 and allow 27.2. Flora has 937 yards and 8 touchdowns, and he is the reason I think Iowa State scores enough to push this over 50.5 even in a loss.

The series argues against me. Iowa State won 43-21 in 2024 and holds a 5-4 lead in the nine meetings since 2016. But that Baylor defense was not this one.

Here is the room. The Formula has Baylor 31-21 and takes Baylor −9.5 with the Over, the exact score I landed on. Next Man Up has Baylor 32-21 and likes Baylor −9.5 and the Over. In The Trenches likes Iowa State +9.5 off the trench matchup, and it is the lone voice in the room for the Cyclones. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Trenches crew thinks the Cyclones' front can keep this inside ten. I think the Trenches crew has never tried to block a homecoming crowd that has been tailgating since the farmers market opened.

Baylor Bears 31, Iowa State Cyclones 21 is my final. Lagway and Freeman hit two shots, the Baylor defense gets Raynor into long downs, and Flora gets his yards with the score already decided.

display.fanatic_story:
Iowa State vs Baylor prediction for Saturday in Waco, and it is Baylor Homecoming, so one of the two people below has been planning her outfit for a month. Twyla Hemmingsen studied meteorology at Iowa State and treats every football game like a storm system. Magnolia Whitlock, Maggie to everyone in Waco, designs living rooms for a living and has opinions about every shade of green.

Maggie: Homecoming weekend, Twyla. McLane Stadium, Saturday, noon Eastern. Before that, the Waco Downtown Farmers Market on Bridge Street. I will walk you through it. You will buy something local, you will compliment the gold trim on my jacket, and then you will watch your team lose in front of every Baylor alum who ever lived.

Twyla: Let me give you the forecast. Cyclones moving south, gusting at 51 points. That is what we scored last week against Oklahoma State. Fifty-one to forty-nine. Jaylen Raynor threw for 309 yards and 3 touchdowns. Aiden Flora ran it 29 times for 221 yards. Jamal Polite Jr. caught 6 balls for 171. Pack an umbrella.

Maggie: You also allowed 49 points. In my business we call that a house with a beautiful front door and no back wall. And the week before that, you went to Arizona and scored 3 points. Three. I have seen more points on a throw pillow.

Twyla: Arizona was a weather event. Every storm has a calm spot. We came out of it and scored 51.

Maggie: Baylor allows 15.2 points a game. Fifteen. Our defense is the kind of room you walk into and immediately lower your voice. We went to UCF last week and won 41-9. DJ Lagway threw for 319 yards and 4 touchdowns on 16 completions. Gavin Freeman caught 5 balls for 114.

Twyla: Freeman is very good. Sixty-three catches, 792 yards. I will grant you that the way a forecaster grants you a sunny afternoon, with an asterisk. But Flora has 937 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, and nobody in Waco has had to tackle him yet.

Maggie: Nobody in Waco has had to tackle anybody. Our three losses came by one point to Auburn, 17-16, by eleven to TCU and by one at Kansas, 25-24. We have not been blown out once. You lost to Arizona by thirty-six.

Twyla: And in 2024 we beat you 43-21. Forty-three. That is not a weather event, that is climate.

Maggie: 2024 was a different decade in football years. Iowa State is 4-4. Baylor is 5-3. And this is homecoming. You do not come into somebody's house on homecoming weekend and talk about two years ago. That is like showing up to a dinner party and complaining about the last owners' wallpaper.

Twyla: The last owners won five of the nine meetings since 2016. I checked. Iowa State 5, Baylor 4. The wallpaper is ours.

Clemson vs Syracuse prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at the JMA Wireless Dome: at noon ET, the CNY Veterans Parade steps off at Chevy Court on the State Fairgrounds, and at the same hour Clemson and Syracuse kick off a few miles away under the roof. Clemson is 5-3. Syracuse is 4-4. Neither looks like the program its fans grew up with, and that is exactly why I like the home team.

DraftKings opened Clemson −1.5 with the over/under at 49.5, and it has not moved. I am taking the points. My side is Syracuse Orange +1.5, and my number is Over 49.5.

The Clemson case for most of the season has been defense, and that defense has holes. The Tigers allow 21.6 and score only 23.2, and they lost 10-51 at LSU, 13-41 to Miami and 16-20 to Virginia Tech. Tait Reynolds has 1,285 throwing yards with 3 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Last week at Florida State he threw for 189 and 2 scores and ran 14 times for 85 and another touchdown in a 36-24 win. Gideon Davidson has 528 rushing yards, and Will Heldt has 7 sacks.

Syracuse has the better offense. The Orange score 31.4 a game and allow 26.4. Umari Hatcher has 60 catches for 952 yards and 8 touchdowns, which is a monster season for any receiver in the conference. Steve Angeli has 1,187 yards and was the quarterback with the most attempts in the last two wins, 31-30 in overtime at North Carolina and 30-27 over SMU. Keyshawn Johnson has 6 sacks.

The series is lopsided. Clemson won 7 of the 9 meetings since 2016. But the last one went Syracuse's way, 34-21 in 2025.

display.fanatic_story:
Clemson vs Syracuse prediction for Saturday at the Dome, from two people who have never agreed on a single thing including the weather. Dixie-Lynn Pruitt spun a flag as captain of the Tiger Band color guard and still salutes when she hears the fight song in a grocery store. Nico Calabrese grew up in the Salt City, shovels lake-effect snow for fun and thinks anybody who complains about cold is from somewhere else.

Nico: Saturday at noon, the CNY Veterans Parade steps off at Chevy Court on the State Fairgrounds. More than 90 veterans and military organizations. Astronaut Jeanette Epps is speaking that morning. An astronaut, Dixie-Lynn. That is the kind of person who comes to Syracuse on a Saturday. And at the same hour, Clemson is going to find out what it feels like to be inside the loudest building in the state.

Dixie-Lynn: An astronaut. That is wonderful, but it is the only thing in Syracuse this weekend that is going to go up. Clemson has been coming up here for years and you know how it usually goes. Seven wins in nine meetings since 2016.

Nico: Not the last one, though. We won the last one, 34-21, in 2025. You remember that one? I do. I have the program framed next to my snow shovel.

Dixie-Lynn: Two wins in nine. Frame them both. You will need something to look at in February. Clemson is 5-3. We just went to Tallahassee and won 36-24. Tait Reynolds threw 2 touchdowns and ran for another one. He went 14 times for 85 yards. That is a quarterback who will run through your parade.

Nico: Reynolds has 3 touchdown throws all season. Three. Umari Hatcher has 8 touchdown catches by himself. He has 60 catches for 952 yards. Hatcher has caught more touchdowns than your quarterback has thrown, and it is not close.

Dixie-Lynn: That is a mean thing to say about a team that is 5-3.

Nico: It is a fact about a team that is 5-3. Here is another one. You lost 51-10 at LSU. You lost 41-13 to Miami. You lost to Virginia Tech, 20-16. Your defense gives up 21.6 a game and your offense only scores 23.2. That is a team hanging off a cliff by its fingernails.

Dixie-Lynn: Will Heldt has 7 sacks. Seven. Your quarterback is going to spend the afternoon on his back, looking up at that roof and wondering why he did not stay in the parade.

Nico: Keyshawn Johnson has 6 sacks for us, and he does not care what color your flags are. Steve Angeli has 1,187 yards and he has been the guy for the last two wins. We beat North Carolina 31-30 in overtime and SMU 30-27. Close games, every week, and we keep finding a way.

Dixie-Lynn: You also lost to California and Virginia and Pittsburgh and Louisville. That is a lot of finding a way out the door.

Nico: We are 4-4 and we score 31.4 a game. You are 5-3 and you score 23.2. If points were snowfall, you would be the city that gets a dusting and closes the schools. We get four feet and go to work.

Dixie-Lynn: Gideon Davidson has 528 rushing yards and 5 touchdowns. He is going to run right at your front all day and wear it out. In South Carolina we call that a long, slow Sunday dinner. By the time dessert comes out, everybody is too full to move.

Nico: In Syracuse we call that the first quarter. By the third quarter Hatcher is behind your secondary and the Dome is shaking. Then everybody goes out to the Fairgrounds and thanks a veteran, because that is the kind of Saturday this is.

Dixie-Lynn: I will give you that part. It is a good weekend to be in Central New York. Thank the veterans, cheer for the band, and then watch Clemson leave town with a win.

Nico: One point. That is what this comes down to. One play, one drive, one throw to Hatcher with a minute left. I have seen this movie and I like the ending.

Dixie-Lynn: I have seen it too. It ends with my flag waving in your end zone.

Nico: Bring a hat. The flag is going to need it on the walk to the car.

My call: Syracuse Orange 26, Clemson Tigers 25.

Kickoff is noon ET. The Seminoles are 3-5. The Eagles are 4-4. Neither record is the reason anybody bought a ticket.

McKenzie is the whole show in Chestnut Hill: 1,450 throwing yards and 638 rushing yards. When he is held in check, there is no plan B.

display.fanatic_story:
Florida State vs Boston College prediction for Saturday in Chestnut Hill, and if you have a free afternoon, these two will fill it. Gianna Ravello grew up in Tallahassee with a Seminole spear painted on her bedroom wall. Siobhan Dunleavy won a national debate title at Boston College and has not lost an argument at a dinner table since.

Siobhan: Saturday is Veterans and Military Appreciation Day at Alumni Stadium. Noon Eastern. It is a good day to be in Chestnut Hill and a good day to say thank you. It is also the first time Florida State has come up here since 2023, so I would like to welcome you back to New England, where November is a season and not a rumor.

Gianna: Thank you. I brought a coat. I also brought the history. Florida State is 16-6 all-time against Boston College. Nine and three at Alumni Stadium. We have won three straight road games in this series. I have been to your house before. I know where the good chair is.

Siobhan: History is what you reach for when your present is 3-5. Let me introduce a counterargument. You are 3-5.

Gianna: And you are 4-4 and last week you scored 2 points at Duke. Two. That is a safety, not a football game. I have seen more scoring at a church bake sale.

Siobhan: Duke was a bad day. Two weeks ago we went to Georgia Tech and won 49-27. Mason McKenzie runs this team on his own legs. He has 1,450 throwing yards and 638 more on the ground. He is our quarterback, our running back and our closing argument.

Gianna: Respectfully, if one man is your quarterback and your leading rusher, your team is a one-person debate club. Ashton Daniels has 1,968 throwing yards and 14 touchdowns. Ousmane Kromah has 609 rushing yards. Duce Robinson has 438 receiving. We have a whole cast.

Siobhan: Your whole cast has 11 interceptions. Daniels threw 3 last week against Clemson and you lost 36-24. A cast is only as good as the person who keeps dropping the script.

Gianna: He also threw for 350 yards against Clemson. Micahi Danzy caught 4 balls for 108. We moved the ball all day. We just gave it away a few times. That is fixable. Two points is not fixable.

Siobhan: Point of order. Anthony Palano has 69 tackles for us. Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks. Our defense will be in Daniels' face, and a quarterback with 11 interceptions in a cold stadium in November is a quarterback who will give us gifts.

Gianna: Rylan Kennedy has 6 sacks for us. He is going to chase McKenzie around that field like a man trying to catch the last train out of Boston. And your offense scores 21.6 a game. Ours scores 30.6. The math is not a debate.

Siobhan: The math also says you allow 28.9 a game. That is not a defense, that is a revolving door with a logo on it. You lost to Louisville 44-20. You lost to Alabama 50-36. You gave up 43 to Miami in overtime.

Gianna: Those are good teams. Boston College is not Alabama. No disrespect. Alumni Stadium is a fine building and the people are very nice, and I am sure the veterans being honored on Saturday will see a good game. I am just telling you who wins it.

Siobhan: The last time Florida State came here, in 2023, you won 31-29 and needed every last snap. The year after, we went to Tallahassee and beat you 28-13. That one still stings, doesn't it?

Gianna: It stings like a cold wind off the reservoir. Which is to say, I will put on a scarf and move on. This is a different year. Kromah runs downhill, Daniels hits a couple of shots to Robinson and Danzy, and your crowd gets very quiet around the third quarter.

Siobhan: My closing argument. McKenzie makes plays with his legs, the defense gets two takeaways off Daniels, and Boston College keeps this a game into the fourth quarter. We honor the veterans, we sing loud, and we make you earn every yard of the trip.

Gianna: My rebuttal. Nice speech. Florida State by eight. Then I buy you a chowder.

Siobhan: I accept the chowder. I reject the premise.

My call: Florida State Seminoles 31, Boston College Eagles 23.

display.fanatic_story:
North Carolina vs UConn prediction for Saturday in East Hartford, from two people who would argue about which way the river runs. Ainsley Pemberton grew up in Chapel Hill and refers to the color of the sky as Carolina blue without irony. Jo Ferrante ran the point for a high school team outside Hartford, still plays every possession like it is a fast break, and has never once been told to slow down.

Jo: Saturday is Youth and Junior Husky Club Day at Pratt & Whitney Stadium. Noon kickoff. Kids everywhere. Face paint, little jerseys, the works. And North Carolina is going to have to play in front of a stadium full of future Huskies who have never heard of the Tar Heels.

Ainsley: They have heard of us, Jo. Every child in America has heard of North Carolina. We have the sky named after us.

Jo: The sky is blue everywhere. You did not invent it. You just painted a ram on it. And here is the thing those kids do know. The last time these two teams played, in December of 2024, UConn won 27-14. Tell them about the sky after that.

Ainsley: That was two years ago. This is a different North Carolina. Billy Edwards Jr. went 28 of 34 for 341 yards and 4 touchdowns against Miami last week. He has 1,872 yards and 15 touchdowns this season. He threw the ball like a man who had somewhere to be.

Jo: And you lost. Thirty-eight to thirty-five. You lost to Syracuse in overtime, 31-30. You lost to Notre Dame. You lost at Clemson. You are 4-4, Ainsley. Same as us. The only difference is that we have Kalieb Osborne and he has thrown 2 interceptions all year.

Ainsley: Two. Fine. Edwards has 5. That is not a crisis, that is a rounding error.

Jo: Osborne has 1,857 yards and 14 touchdowns. He plays the position like a point guard on a fast break. Eyes up, ball out, nobody touches it. And Cyncir Bowers has 571 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. You are going to see a lot of him going right past your linebackers.

Ainsley: Derek McDonald has 82 tackles. He will be waiting. And Xavier Lewis has 7 sacks. Your point guard is going to find out what it feels like to get run over on the way to the rim.

Jo: We score 34.4 a game. You score 25.8. We went to Southern Miss and won 48-20. We went to Temple and won 34-20. We beat UMass 35-16. When this offense gets going, the scoreboard operator needs a nap.

Ainsley: You also lost to Maryland 38-14. At home. Maryland, Jo. A team with two wins. I do not want to bring it up in front of the children, but there it is.

Jo: Fair. That was September. September is preseason in Connecticut. We are a November team. And speaking of losing to Syracuse, we did that too, 42-41 in overtime. So the two of us have that in common. One overtime loss each to the same team, and we both have to live with it.

Ainsley: Finally, something we agree on. Syracuse is the villain of this story.

Jo: Syracuse is the villain of every story. But this is East Hartford, and on Saturday the villain is wearing powder blue. Jordan Shipp has 587 receiving yards. Good player. I would like to see him get open in the cold with a stadium full of kids screaming.

Ainsley: He will. North Carolina plays close games. Five of our eight games have come down to a touchdown or less. We are used to the pressure. Your kids can scream all they want.

Jo: Here is how it goes. Osborne keeps it moving, Bowers gets into the end zone, and UConn is right there in the fourth quarter with the ball and a chance.

Ainsley: And here is how it actually goes. Edwards finds Shipp twice, Lewis gets home on a third down, and North Carolina leaves Connecticut with a win and a few new fans in the stands.

Jo: New fans. You are going to try to recruit the Junior Husky Club.

Ainsley: I am going to hand out Carolina blue face paint at the gate.

Jo: Security is going to love you.

Ainsley: Everybody loves me. It is the sky thing.

My call: North Carolina Tar Heels 30, UConn Huskies 24.

UCLA vs Minnesota prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Huntington Bank Stadium: on the same Saturday UCLA plays in Minneapolis, The Museum of Russian Art opens Painting Snow, an exhibition of winter landscapes, and lets anybody in for free if they show up in a winter hat. The Bruins are 8-0 and No. 5. Minnesota is 5-3. Kickoff is noon ET, and I suggest the visitors bring hats.

DraftKings opened UCLA −6.5 with the over/under at 42.5. It sits at UCLA −6 and 39.5. A half point toward the home team and three points off the points. I will take the home team. My side is Minnesota Golden Gophers +6, and my number is Over 39.5.

UCLA is unbeaten, and the defense is the reason. The Bruins allow 13.4 a game and score 33.5. Wayne Knight has 680 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. But the quarterback picture has shifted. Nico Iamaleava leads the team with 982 throwing yards, and Ty Dieffenbach has had the most attempts in each of the last three games, including 16 of 30 for 178 in a 27-0 win over Nevada. The Bruins won 17-15 at Oregon and 17-7 over Wisconsin. They grind.

Minnesota plays in close games and does not panic. The Gophers lost 16-23 in overtime at Indiana last week, beat Iowa 13-10 and beat Michigan 20-14. Drake Lindsey has 1,592 yards with 10 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Javon Tracy has 460 receiving yards. The Gophers score 25.2 and allow 20.5. They also beat UCLA 21-17 in 2024, the only meeting in the stretch I can check.

Why the Over at 39.5? Because UCLA scores 33.5, Minnesota scores 25.2, and the number dropped to a level where two field goals in the fourth quarter get you there.

The room agrees with me on both halves, which makes me a little nervous. The Formula has UCLA 26-21 and takes Minnesota +6 with the Over. Next Man Up has UCLA 25-20 and takes Minnesota +6 with the Over, which is my score to the point. In The Trenches calls the trench matchup split and offers no side. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

When Next Man Up and I land on the same score, one of us is about to be very smart and the other is about to find out the hard way that copying is not research. I was here first.

UCLA Bruins 25, Minnesota Golden Gophers 20 is my final. Knight runs well, the UCLA defense bends without breaking, and Lindsey keeps Minnesota inside a touchdown into the final minutes.
