display.fanatic_story:
UCLA vs Minnesota prediction for Saturday in Minneapolis, from two people who agree on nothing except that the other one dresses wrong for the weather. Kenzie Rhee produced short films at UCLA and still frames every argument like a trailer. Tor Engebretsen spends most of the winter on a frozen lake in a shack with a hole in the floor and considers that a vacation.

Tor: Saturday morning, The Museum of Russian Art opens a show called Painting Snow. Forty paintings of winter. Wear a winter hat and you get in free. I want every UCLA fan in town to go. Study the paintings. That is what the afternoon is going to look like at Huntington Bank Stadium.

Kenzie: Okay, cold open. A team from Los Angeles walks into Minneapolis. It is 8-0. It is ranked No. 5 in the country. It has given up 13.4 points a game. Cut to the home crowd, in hats, realizing they are about to watch the best defense they have seen all year.

Tor: Cut to the scoreboard in 2024. Minnesota 21, UCLA 17. I remember that one. I remember it the way I remember a walleye that was this big. Every year it gets a little bigger.

Kenzie: You are counting a two-year-old game against an unbeaten team. That is not a story, Tor. That is a flashback, and flashbacks slow down the movie. We beat Oregon on the road, 17-15. We beat Wisconsin 17-7. We beat Nevada 27-0 last week.

Tor: Seventeen points against Oregon. Seventeen against Wisconsin. Your offense makes its movies on a budget. And you have two quarterbacks. Nico Iamaleava has 982 yards, but Ty Dieffenbach has thrown the most in each of the last three games. When you have to tell people which quarterback is in your movie, the audience gets confused.

Kenzie: The audience is watching Wayne Knight. He has 680 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns. Twelve. He is the lead. He is in every scene. And Sammy Omosigho has 5.5 sacks. He is the villain, and the villain gets your quarterback.

Tor: Drake Lindsey can take a hit. He has 1,592 yards and 10 touchdowns. Javon Tracy has 460 receiving yards. We beat Michigan 20-14. We beat Iowa 13-10. We went to Indiana last week and lost in overtime, 23-16. We know how to play in a close game. You have not been in one since Oregon.

Kenzie: We have not been in one because nobody can score on us. That is not a weakness. That is the premise.

Tor: The premise changes when it gets cold. You know what the Gophers hockey team is doing this weekend? Playing Wisconsin in a Gold Out. Whole town in gold. Football Saturday, hockey Saturday night, and in between people go to the museum to look at paintings of snow because they cannot get enough of it.

Kenzie: That is the most Minnesota sentence anybody has ever said.

Tor: Thank you. I practice it on the ice.

Kenzie: Here is my pitch. UCLA scores 33.5 a game. Minnesota scores 25.2. The Bruins allow 13.4. Minnesota allows 20.5. On paper that is a comfortable win. On film, it is a road team in November that does not love the cold and a home team with nothing to lose.

Tor: That is the first honest thing you have said all day. Nothing to lose is the best way to play. We are 5-3, we have a home crowd, and we have Maverick Baranowski with 60 tackles waiting for Knight at the hole like a pike under the ice.

Kenzie: A pike. You are comparing your linebacker to a fish.

Tor: To a very patient fish with a lot of teeth. And TJ Bush Jr. has 5 sacks. He is a fish too. Everybody on our defense is a fish.

Kenzie: Final scene. Knight runs for a touchdown, the defense holds in the fourth quarter, and UCLA flies home 9-0 with snow on its shoes.

Tor: My final scene. Minnesota hangs around, Lindsey finds Tracy late, and the crowd in winter hats goes home hoping until the very last snap.

Kenzie: Hoping is not winning.

Tor: In Minnesota, it is a lifestyle.

My call: UCLA Bruins 25, Minnesota Golden Gophers 20.

Tulsa vs Tulane prediction for Saturday in New Orleans, from two people who have been loudly disagreeing since the schedule came out. Wiley Pettibone is from Tulsa, works in the oil patch and describes every big play as a gusher. Twan Ducros-Labat plays trumpet in a brass band uptown and has no use for quiet Saturdays, or quiet anything.

Twan: Saturday, City Park, Beignet Fest. All day. Every kind of beignet you can think of and a few you cannot. Amanda Shaw is playing. The Imagination Movers are playing. And the whole thing raises money for local autism programs. You come to New Orleans, Wiley, you eat a beignet, you do something good, and then you go to Yulman Stadium and watch Tulane win.

Wiley: I will eat the beignet. I will do the good deed. I will even listen to your band. But I am telling you right now, Tulsa is bringing a gusher. Baylor Hayes has 1,343 yards and only 2 interceptions. He does not give the ball away. He drills, he finds oil, he moves to the next well.

Twan: He also lost to Army at home. Thirty-eight to thirty-five. And that was the last game you played, two weeks ago. You have been sitting at home since October 23 thinking about it.

Wiley: We have been resting. There is a difference. Two weeks off, fresh legs, and Oran Singleton Jr. with 535 receiving yards running past your secondary like a pipeline leak. Fast, messy, and expensive to clean up.

Twan: That is the worst compliment I have ever heard a man give his own team.

Wiley: In Tulsa it is the highest one there is.

Twan: Here is a better one. Trace Johnson went 28 of 36 for 284 yards at Charlotte last week and we won 38-31 in overtime. Johnnie Daniels ran 13 times for 99 yards and 2 touchdowns. Our offense found a groove. You can hear it, like a horn section hitting the chorus together for the first time.

Wiley: Your offense scores 22.5 a game. That is not a horn section. That is a kazoo.

Twan: And your defense gives up 24.4 a game. You lost at Arkansas 34-6. You lost to North Texas in overtime, 45-44. You lost at Navy. You lost to Army. That is two service academies, Wiley. Your team is very respectful toward the military.

Wiley: Kyran Duhon has 6 sacks. Chris Thompson Jr. has 81 tackles. Your quarterback is going to feel both of them before the band gets through its first song.

Twan: Dickson Agu has 78 tackles for us. Makai Williams has 4 sacks. And the thing you are not saying is the history. Tulane won 31-14 last year. We won 24-22 the year before that. Six of the last nine meetings since 2016 are ours.

Wiley: Six of nine. Three for us. That is not a rout, that is a rivalry.

Twan: It is a rivalry where one side keeps winning. In New Orleans we call that a tradition. You do the same thing every year until it becomes a parade.

Wiley: We beat Oklahoma State 24-10 to open the season. Big win. Oil country. Everybody in Tulsa was proud. And we score 29.8 a game. If this turns into a shootout, I like where we sit.

Twan: It is not going to be a shootout. It is going to be Daniels running into the pile, three yards, four yards, the clock running, the crowd singing, and Hayes standing on the far side of the field watching it happen.

Wiley: Hayes will get his chances. He always does. One gusher in the fourth quarter and this whole thing changes.

Twan: Then the band plays louder. That is what we do. When the other team scores, we play louder. When we score, we play louder still. By the end of the day you will not be able to hear yourself think.

Wiley: I will not need to think. I will need another beignet.

Twan: That I can arrange. Bring powdered sugar money and a sense of humor. You are going to need both on the drive back to Oklahoma.

My call: Tulane Green Wave 25, Tulsa Golden Hurricane 23.

Duke vs NC State prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Carter-Finley Stadium: NC State has made it Military Appreciation day, kickoff is 12:30 PM ET, and the Raleigh Food Truck Rodeo will have Fayetteville Street packed downtown for anybody who wants to eat their way through the afternoon before or after. Duke is the better team. I am not arguing that. The Blue Devils score 32.0 and allow 14.2, and Nate Sheppard has 972 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns, including 5 scores in a 47-2 win over Boston College last week. Walker Eget has 1,641 yards with 9 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. But Duke's two losses came 25-28 at Georgia Tech and 20-24 to North Carolina, and it won 19-16 at Virginia. On the road against a decent team, Duke has been in one-score games.

NC State's offense is real. The Wolfpack score 32.1 a game, a hair more than Duke. CJ Bailey has 1,955 yards with 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, and Keenan Jackson has 456 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns. Last week Davion Gause ran 19 times for 104 in a 31-10 win over California. The problem is defense. NC State allows 25.9, and that is why I like Over 50.5 more than I like the Wolfpack to win outright.

The series has gone Duke's way. Duke won 45-33 in 2025 and 29-19 in 2024, and took 3 of the 4 meetings since 2016 that I can check.

Here is the room. The Formula has Duke 29-23 and takes Duke −4.5 with the Over. Next Man Up has Duke 28-27 and likes NC State +4.5 with the Over. In The Trenches calls the trench matchup split and gives no side. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. display.fanatic_story:
Duke vs NC State prediction for Saturday in Raleigh, from two men who park next to each other at Carter-Finley and have not agreed on anything in the history of that parking lot. Harrison Wexley-Moore IV went to Duke, as did his father, as did his father, and he will remind you of that before you can say hello. Ruff Pegram went to NC State, runs the grill in the next spot over and has been feeding Harrison for years out of what he calls Christian charity.

Ruff: Saturday is Military Appreciation at Carter-Finley. Kickoff at 12:30. Downtown, the Food Truck Rodeo is on Fayetteville Street, free, with every truck in the Triangle. But nobody in their right mind leaves my grill for a food truck. Harrison, you have eaten my brisket for six years.

Harrison: I have tolerated your brisket for six years. As a courtesy. A gentleman never refuses food from a neighbor, even one wearing that much red.

Ruff: And a gentleman says thank you. Here is your thank you. NC State has a running back named Duke. Jayden Scott. Wears number 1. Everybody calls him Duke. So on Saturday, there will be exactly one Duke on that field worth watching, and he is ours.

Harrison: That is the single most NC State thing I have ever heard. You could not beat us, so you named a running back after us.

Ruff: We did not name him. We just took the name. Like we take your lunch most years.

Harrison: Most years? We won 45-33 last year. We won 29-19 the year before that. We won 24-3 in 2023. Three. You scored three points, Ruff. I have seen more points on the scoreboard at a tennis match.

Ruff: You know what tennis has? Love. Which is what you will have for our offense when CJ Bailey throws for a few hundred yards. He has 1,955 yards and 13 touchdowns. Keenan Jackson has 456 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns. We score 32.1 a game. Duke scores 32.0. We score more than you do, Harrison. Write that down in your family Bible.

Harrison: By one-tenth of a point. And we allow 14.2. You allow 25.9. Our defense is a private club. Yours is a public park.

Ruff: Fair. But you went to Georgia Tech and lost 28-25. You lost to North Carolina 24-20. You beat Virginia 19-16 and needed every bit of it. On the road, your private club turns into a tent.

Harrison: Nate Sheppard has 972 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns. He scored 5 of them last week against Boston College. Five. We won 47-2. Boston College scored a safety. That is the only way anybody gets two points against us.

Ruff: Boston College is not NC State. We beat Louisville 31-28. We beat California last week 31-10. Davion Gause ran 19 times for 104 yards. He runs like a man late for the food trucks.

Harrison: Walker Eget has 1,641 yards and only 3 interceptions. He does not make mistakes. He has the composure of a man who has been to a lot of formal dinners.

Ruff: And Popo Aguirre has 76 tackles. He has the composure of a man who has never been invited to one and does not care. He is going to put Eget in the grass.

Harrison: Kevin O'Connor has 4.5 sacks for us. Your quarterback is going to see a lot of blue.

Ruff: It is a Saturday in November in Raleigh. Everybody sees a lot of blue. It is called the sky. We also see red, and that is what it is going to look like when the crowd stands up in the fourth quarter.

Harrison: I will grant you the crowd. Carter-Finley is loud. It is also a stadium where Duke has won three of the last four.

Ruff: And we won the one before that, 31-20. I remember it. I remember everything. That is what grilling teaches you. Patience and memory.

Harrison: Here is my prediction. Sheppard scores twice, Eget does not turn it over, and Duke wins a close one.

Ruff: Close is all I need. Bailey throws, Duke Scott runs, the real Duke, and the Wolfpack are right there with the ball at the end.

Harrison: And afterward?

Ruff: Afterward, you eat my brisket and say thank you, win or lose. It is Military Appreciation day. We can all be decent for one afternoon.

Harrison: For one afternoon. Then I go back to being right.

My call: Duke Blue Devils 28, NC State Wolfpack 25.

Maryland vs Purdue prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Ross-Ade Stadium: it is Purdue Homecoming, kickoff is 12:30 PM ET, and the College of Agriculture and Vet Med alumni will be tailgating on Memorial Mall before the game. Maryland is 2-6 and has lost every Big Ten game it has played. Purdue is 3-5. Somebody has to win, and I know who.

DraftKings opened Purdue −7 with the over/under at 57.5. It is now Purdue −6.5 and still 57.5. Half a point of drift toward Maryland, the total parked. My side is Purdue Boilermakers −6.5, and my number is Over 57.5.

Begin with Ryan Browne. He has 1,964 yards with 11 touchdowns and 5 interceptions, and before a rough 10 of 29 for 142 at Penn State last week he threw for 378 at UCLA and 329 against Wake Forest. Fame Ijeboi has 588 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns, and Asaad Waseem has 652 receiving yards. Purdue scores 29.5 a game, and at home it beat Minnesota 41-13.

Maryland's problem is that it stopped stopping people. The Terrapins allow 31.6 a game. They lost 3-54 to UCLA, 23-48 at Nebraska and 16-45 at Ohio State. Malik Washington has 1,805 yards and 9 touchdowns, but also 7 interceptions, and Chris Durr Jr. has 58 catches for 638 yards. The closest Big Ten game was last week, 17-20 against Illinois. Purdue went to Illinois and won 24-17.

Purdue's defense is not good either, allowing 32.1 a game. That is the case for Over 57.5. Two defenses giving up more than 31 a game, two quarterbacks who can throw, and a Homecoming crowd that wants points.

The series is close in recent memory. Purdue won 31-29 in 2022 and 40-14 in 2019. Maryland won 50-7 in 2016.

The cards agree more than usual. The Formula has Purdue 34-26 and takes Purdue −6.5 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has Purdue 36-26 and likes Purdue −6.5 with the Over. In The Trenches calls the trench matchup split and offers no side. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

When The Formula and Next Man Up agree on the side and the Over, I do not go looking for reasons to argue. Purdue at home against a team that has not won a Big Ten game is the cleanest spot on the board.

Purdue Boilermakers 35, Maryland Terrapins 26 is my final. Browne bounces back, Ijeboi scores twice, and Washington throws enough to push it over 57.5 in the fourth quarter.

Purdue Boilermakers 35, Maryland Terrapins 26. Purdue Boilermakers cover the 6.5. Over 57.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Maryland vs Purdue prediction for Saturday in West Lafayette, from two people who should never have been seated together at a wedding, and were, and have been texting each other insults ever since. Abby Chesapeake is from Annapolis, has cracked crabs since she could hold a mallet, and judges every situation by whether it would be improved with Old Bay. Barnaby Wolcott-Reese is a Purdue engineer who builds scale replicas of the Boilermaker Special in his garage and cannot stop making engineering puns, even when begged.

Barnaby: Saturday is Homecoming at Ross-Ade. Kickoff at 12:30. And before that, the Ag and Vet Med alumni tailgate on the south end of Memorial Mall, ten to noon, catered by Shoup's Country Foods. Abby, it is a full Indiana table. Pork, corn, the works. You are going to love it.

Abby: I am going to try it. Whether I love it depends on whether anybody brought a crab.

Barnaby: There are no crabs in Indiana.

Abby: That explains a lot about Indiana.

Barnaby: What it explains is that we have other priorities. Like football. Ryan Browne has 1,964 yards and 11 touchdowns. He has torque. He has thrust. He is a precision instrument.

Abby: He went 10 of 29 at Penn State last week.

Barnaby: Every engine has a rough cycle. You recalibrate. Six weeks before that he threw for 378 at UCLA. That is the real output.

Abby: You lost that game 52-38.

Barnaby: And you lost to UCLA 54-3. If we are comparing our results against the Bruins, I am comfortable with mine.

Abby: That was a bad day. Malik Washington threw 4 interceptions. We do not talk about it in Maryland. It is like a crab with no meat in it. You crack it, you look, you set it aside, and you move on.

Barnaby: You have been setting aside a lot of crabs this year. Two wins and six losses. Zero and five in the Big Ten.

Abby: We beat UConn 38-14 on the road. Washington went 34 of 41 for 347. When he is right, he is right. And Chris Durr Jr. has 58 catches for 638 yards. He catches everything. He is a crab trap. Whatever comes near him, it is staying.

Barnaby: Asaad Waseem has 652 receiving yards for us. More yards. Fewer catches. That is called efficiency. That is an engineering term.

Abby: That is a word you made up to feel better about fewer catches.

Barnaby: Fame Ijeboi has 588 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns. He is a piston. Up and down the field, all afternoon, no rest. We beat Minnesota 41-13 at home. We beat Illinois 24-17 on the road. The same Illinois that beat you last week.

Abby: Illinois beat us 20-17. Three points. We were right there. That is the most encouraging loss I have had all year.

Barnaby: The most encouraging loss. That should be on a Maryland shirt.

Abby: Your defense gives up 32.1 a game. That should be on a Purdue shirt. Ours gives up 31.6. So we are better at defense, Barnaby. By half a point. Write it on the garage wall next to your train.

Barnaby: It is not a train. It is a replica of the Boilermaker Special. It runs. It has a horn. It is a working locomotive in miniature.

Abby: So it is a train.

Barnaby: It is an engineering achievement.

Abby: Does it carry crabs?

Barnaby: It could, theoretically. Load capacity is not the issue. The issue is that there are no crabs in Indiana.

Abby: There will be on Saturday. I am bringing a cooler.

Barnaby: Here is the history. Purdue won 31-29 in 2022. Purdue won 40-14 in 2019. Maryland won 50-7 in 2016, which I do not acknowledge because I was not yet emotionally invested.

Abby: Fifty to seven. Say it with me.

Barnaby: I will not. Here is my prediction. Browne rebounds, Ijeboi scores twice, the defense holds just long enough, and Homecoming ends with a win. It is simple mechanics. Force applied, result achieved.

Abby: Here is mine. Washington throws for plenty, Durr catches everything, and we make it close enough that you sweat through your engineering shirt.

Barnaby: You will lose.

Abby: Probably. But I will lose with Old Bay on my fingers, and you will win with pork on yours. We both know who had the better afternoon.

My call: Purdue Boilermakers 35, Maryland Terrapins 26.

Arkansas vs Auburn prediction, spread and over/under for Saturday: I have Arkansas Razorbacks +10.5 and Under 50.5, with Auburn Tigers 29, Arkansas Razorbacks 19 as my final. Kickoff is 12:45 PM ET at Jordan-Hare Stadium, and Auburn has made this its Military Appreciation game, with the Tigers dressed in navy.

Bubba Fayette-Dorsey calls the Hogs before he says hello. "Woo Pig. We're 3-5, fine. We still beat Auburn 24-14 in 2024, and Chris Marshall has 633 receiving yards. KJ Jackson just needs one clean afternoon."

Lacey Bellamy smiles like she already knows the ending. "Bubba, we won 33-24 last year. Byrum Brown has 484 rushing yards and 7 rushing touchdowns, Elijah Melendez has 63 tackles and 4 sacks, and y'all scored 10 against Missouri."

Here is why I take the points. Auburn has dropped two in a row, 17-38 to LSU and 15-45 at Ole Miss, and it scores 24.1 a game. That is not an offense that pulls away from anybody. Brown has 9 touchdown throws and 7 interceptions, and he threw 3 interceptions in the opener against Baylor. Arkansas is worse, scoring 19.6 a game and losing 10-34 to Missouri, but my 29-19 is a 10-point Auburn win, inside the 10.5. DraftKings opened Auburn −12.5, so the market has already drifted toward the Hogs.

The risk is the history. Auburn won 8 of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025, including 48-10 in 2023. Arkansas also lost 10-43 at Utah and 17-45 to Georgia this fall. If Jackson turns it over early, a 10-point game can become 20 in a hurry.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 50.5 and it has held. Arkansas allows 27.6 a game and Auburn allows 26.8, which looks like points on paper. But neither offense has shown it lately: 10 points for Arkansas against Missouri, 15 for Auburn at Ole Miss. My 29 and 19 make 48, two and a half under 50.5.

The room splits on the side. The Formula has Auburn 29-20 and takes Arkansas +10.5 with the Under. Next Man Up has Auburn 29-18, takes the Tigers −10.5, and likes the Under. display.fanatic_story:
Arkansas Razorbacks vs Auburn Tigers prediction for Saturday, November 7: Auburn has made this its Military Appreciation game, the Tigers are wearing navy, and Bubba Fayette-Dorsey drove down from the Ozarks with a cooler, a red hat and a speech he has been practicing since Monday.

Lacey Bellamy met him on the Plains with a tray of biscuits and a look that said she had heard the speech before.

"Woo Pig Sooie," Bubba announced to the parking lot, to the trees, to anybody within a hundred yards. "We are here. We are hungry. We are 3-5 and we do not care."

"You should care a little," Lacey said. "Y'all scored 10 points against Missouri."

That landed, and Bubba knew it. Arkansas has had a long fall. The Hogs beat North Alabama, Tulsa and Vanderbilt, and then lost to Utah 10-43, to Georgia 17-45, to Texas A&M 7-34, to Tennessee 17-24 and to Missouri 10-34. They score 19.6 points a game and give up 27.6. Bubba teaches science to grade-schoolers in the Ozarks, and he will tell you that numbers do not lie. He will also tell you that he does not have to like them.

"KJ Jackson has thrown for 1,673 yards," he said. "Chris Marshall has 633 receiving yards. That is a real receiver. And we beat y'all 24-14 in 2024, right in front of everybody."

"And we beat y'all 33-24 last year," Lacey said, handing him a biscuit like a peace offering. "Eat. You're going to need your strength."

Auburn has its own bruises. The Tigers opened 4-2 and then ran into LSU and Ole Miss. LSU won 38-17 at Jordan-Hare. Ole Miss won 45-15 in Oxford. Auburn is 4-4, it scores 24.1 a game and it gives up 26.8. Lacey was a sorority president on this campus, and she runs a tailgate the way she ran chapter meetings: on time, with a plan, and with no patience for sad talk.

"We beat Georgia 27-24 in Athens," she said. "Nobody gets to tell me this team is done."

Bubba could not argue with that one either.

Her case starts with Byrum Brown. He has thrown for 1,560 yards and run for 484 more, with 7 rushing touchdowns. When the throws are not there, he puts his head down and goes. Behind him on defense, Elijah Melendez has 63 tackles and 4 sacks. Lacey calls him the hall monitor, because nobody gets down the hall without permission, and she is very proud of that joke.

Bubba's case is simpler. Arkansas has to protect Jackson, let him find Marshall and keep the game close enough that Auburn begins to feel the last two weeks. Ja'Quavion Smith has 53 tackles for the Hogs, and Quincy Rhodes Jr. has 3 sacks. If they can get Brown on the ground early, Bubba thinks the crowd gets nervous.

"Your crowd will be loud early," he said. "And quiet by halftime."

"Our crowd is going to be standing for the veterans," Lacey said, and she meant it. "Then it will be loud all day."

That part they agree on. Military Appreciation Day on the Plains is the kind of afternoon that makes even a visiting Hog take his hat off. Bubba already promised he would stand for the salute. He also promised to call the Hogs right after, which Lacey has decided to allow, once.

Here is how it shakes out. Brown makes enough plays with his legs to keep Auburn in front, and Melendez makes Jackson uncomfortable all afternoon. But Arkansas does not fold. Marshall gets loose a couple of times, the Hogs kick a field goal or two, and Auburn never quite gets the runaway Lacey wants. The Tigers snap the two-game skid. Bubba drives home with a full stomach, an empty cooler and a fresh reason to call the Hogs next fall.

Lacey says he can keep the biscuit recipe. Bubba says he would rather keep the score.

My call: Auburn Tigers 29, Arkansas Razorbacks 19.

Oklahoma State vs Kansas State prediction, spread and over/under for Saturday: I have Kansas State Wildcats +3.5 and Over 62.5, with Oklahoma State Cowboys 32, Kansas State Wildcats 31 as my final. Kickoff is 1:00 PM ET at Bill Snyder Family Stadium, and downtown Manhattan spends the weekend on its Holiday Open House, the biggest shopping days of the year along Poyntz Avenue.

Dusty Lockridge explains football like a rodeo clock. "Eight seconds, Hattie. Drew Mestemaker has 2,649 yards and 25 touchdown throws. We score 41.1 a game. Caleb Hawkins ran for 194 yards at Iowa State."

Hattie Brandvold does not look up from her notes. "And you lost that game 49-51, Dusty. You give up 27.1 a game. We give up 21.9, and we won the last two meetings, 14-6 and 42-20."

Here is why I take the points. Oklahoma State scores, but it has not closed on the road: 32-35 at Houston and 49-51 at Iowa State, both one-score losses. Kansas State's defense is the best in this game by a wide margin, and Jayden Bryant has 4 sacks. The worry for the Wildcats is the quarterback picture. Avery Johnson leads the team with 1,301 yards, but Jacob Knuth threw the most at Arizona State and Blake Barnett threw the most at Colorado, with 3 touchdowns in a 24-27 overtime loss. My 32-31 is a one-point Cowboys win, well inside the 3.5. DraftKings opened Oklahoma State −6.5, and it has come down to 3.5.

The risk is that Oklahoma State is simply better at throwing it. The Cowboys beat Oregon 39-31 and Colorado 57-24, and Justin Bowick has 731 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Kansas State has lost three of its last four.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 60.5 and it is up to 62.5. Mestemaker threw 5 touchdowns at Iowa State, and Kansas State scores 31.8 a game, with Rodney Fields Jr. at 487 rushing yards. My 32 and 31 make 63, half a point over 62.5. That is the slimmest call on the board, and I know it.

The room agrees on the side and splits on the over/under. The Formula has Oklahoma State 32-29 and takes Kansas State +3.5 with the Under. Next Man Up has Kansas State 33-31, takes the Wildcats +3.5, and likes the Over. In The Trenches sees a split in the run game, so no side, and it reads sides only with no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "I have the home team winning it, partner. You're both being polite."

The Formula: "Three points of disagreement. That is a field goal, not a philosophy."

Hattie wants to walk Poyntz Avenue after the game and do her holiday shopping early. Dusty says he will come along if Sunday's card show at Manhattan Town Center has an old Cowboys card worth framing. Hattie says it will be cheaper than the four quarters he is about to sit through.

Oklahoma State Cowboys 32, Kansas State Wildcats 31. Kansas State Wildcats cover the 3.5. Over 62.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Oklahoma State Cowboys vs Kansas State Wildcats prediction for Saturday, November 7: downtown Manhattan is throwing its Holiday Open House this weekend, the biggest shopping days of the year on Poyntz Avenue, and Dusty Lockridge has decided that a man from Stillwater can shop and gloat at the same time.

Hattie Brandvold has decided otherwise.

"You can buy a scarf," she told him outside a boutique. "You cannot buy a road win."

Dusty grinned under his hat. He is an ag-econ grad who explains offense with rodeo timing, and he thinks this whole thing comes down to eight seconds of nerve. "Drew Mestemaker has thrown for 2,649 yards," he said. "Twenty-five touchdowns. We score 41.1 points a game, Hattie. That is not a team. That is a stampede."

Hattie is an agronomy grad, and she explains defense with crop rotation. You plant one thing, you let the field rest, you plant another, and you never let the soil get lazy. "A stampede runs out of grass," she said. "We give up 21.9 points a game. You give up 27.1. And you lost 49-51 at Iowa State last week."

That was a wild one. Mestemaker threw 5 touchdowns in Ames. Caleb Hawkins ran for 194 yards. Justin Bowick caught 7 balls for 124 yards and 2 scores. And the Cowboys still lost by two. A week before that they put 57 on Colorado. Two weeks before that they lost 32-35 at Houston. Oklahoma State is 5-3, and almost every Saturday ends with somebody's scoreboard operator needing a nap.

"We beat Oregon," Dusty said. "Thirty-nine to thirty-one. Remember that?"

"I remember 14-6," Hattie said. "Last year. And 42-20 the year before."

Kansas State has won the last two meetings. Over the last ten, it is 5-5, which tells you how stubborn this series is. Neither side gets to keep the bragging rights for long.

The Wildcats have their own worries, and Hattie does not hide from them. They are 4-4. They lost 24-27 in overtime at Colorado last week, and 17-28 at Arizona State the week before. Avery Johnson leads the team with 1,301 yards through the air, but Jacob Knuth threw the most at Arizona State, and Blake Barnett threw the most in Boulder, with 3 touchdowns. Three different quarterbacks have led the way in three weeks.

"Crop rotation," Hattie said. "We are resting the field."

"You are guessing," Dusty said.

What she trusts is the defense. Jayden Bryant has 4 sacks. Logan Bartley has 54 tackles from the back of it. Rodney Fields Jr. has 487 rushing yards and 5 touchdowns, and when Fields gets going, Manhattan gets loud. Hattie wants the Wildcats to run the ball, keep Mestemaker on the sideline and make this an afternoon game in the old Bill Snyder way: patient, physical and a little bit mean.

Dusty wants the opposite. He wants tempo. He wants Hawkins, who has 906 rushing yards, to get the Wildcats back on their heels, and then he wants Bowick, with 731 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns, running free behind them. "Rodeo timing," he said. "You let the bull think he's winning, then you ride him for eight."

Hattie said that is not how bulls work. Dusty said that is exactly how bulls work. They let it go.

Here is how it shakes out. Mestemaker gets his yards, because he always does, and the Cowboys put up points in bunches. But Kansas State runs it, Fields finds room late, and the home crowd keeps this thing tight into the fourth quarter. It comes down to one more drive, and Oklahoma State gets it. Barely. Dusty celebrates like he roped a calf. Hattie says she has seen this movie, and that the ending changes in Stillwater next year.

Sunday, the Flint Hills Card Show sets up at Manhattan Town Center. Dusty wants to look for an old Cowboys card. Hattie says she will help him, as long as he pays for lunch.

My call: Oklahoma State Cowboys 32, Kansas State Wildcats 31.

Goldie did not even blink. She is a marine biology grad, and she explains defense like tide charts: what comes in, goes out. "Let it be known," she said, "that you are 2-7."

Winnie lowered the plate. It is true. Old Dominion beat Norfolk State in the opener and won 10-3 at App State in October, and the rest of the fall has been rough. The Monarchs lost 17-20 to East Carolina, 10-42 at Georgia State, 0-26 at Louisiana Tech and 23-36 to Marshall last week. They score 16.3 points a game and give up 27.8.

"Our quarterback room has range," Winnie said.

"Your quarterback room has a revolving door," Goldie said.

That is fair too. Quinn Henicle, Ryan Huff and Jaxon Potter have all led the Monarchs in throws in a game this season. Potter threw for 329 yards against Marshall, which sounds great until you remember the 3 interceptions. Henicle leads the team with 656 yards. Winnie likes to say the next one is always around the corner. Goldie likes to say that is the problem.

What Winnie does have is a defense with some bite. Lucas Struck has 70 tackles from the safety spot. Javen Gibson has 5 sacks. Old Dominion held App State to 3 points on the road, and Winnie brings that up roughly every eleven minutes. "Three points," he said. "In Boone. You could not do that."

Coastal could not. The Chanticleers lost 32-35 to App State at home in October, and that one still stings. Coastal is 3-5, and the losses have mostly been close: 24-31 at West Virginia, 24-31 to Georgia Southern, 32-35 to App. Goldie calls them low tides. They always come back in.

And they came back in last week. Coastal won 31-20 at Georgia State, Deuce Bailey threw for 297 yards and 3 touchdowns, and Clayton Coppock Jr. caught 6 balls for 100 yards and 2 scores. Bailey has 1,935 yards and 19 touchdowns on the season. Dominic Lee-Knicely has 484 rushing yards. Marcellius Pulliam has 74 tackles, and Ibrahim Diawara has 5 sacks. Goldie lists them in order, like a reef survey.

"Last year was last year," she said. "Your team scored 47 on us and I still came to Homecoming."

Winnie had no answer for that, which is rare for a town crier.

Here is how Goldie sees the afternoon. Bailey gets time, finds Coppock deep once or twice, and the home crowd gets loud early. Old Dominion hangs around because Struck and Gibson make some plays, and because Potter will hit a long one sooner or later. But the Monarchs do not score enough to keep up for four quarters. Coastal pulls away a little in the second half, the student section is loud, and the alumni stay late.

Winnie thinks his defense keeps it close. He might be right for a while. He usually is, for about a half.

The rest of the weekend is all Coastal. The Alumni Association brunch is Sunday, and Goldie already RSVP'd for both of them. Winnie says he will go if he can make a toast. Goldie says he can toast the Chanticleers or he can toast nothing.

Up the road, the South Carolina UFO Festival lands at the Conway Sports and Fitness Center on Saturday too. Winnie wants to know if anybody there has seen a Monarchs touchdown drive lately. Goldie says that is the kind of thing only the faithful ever see.

My call: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 27, Old Dominion Monarchs 19.

Georgia State Panthers vs App State Mountaineers prediction for Saturday, November 7: this is the App State Heroes Day Game, a celebration of military members, veterans and their families, and Zeb Whitlock has been up since dawn getting the Heroes Day Tailgate ready on the McKinney Alumni Center patio.

Malik Odom drove up from Atlanta with a thermos and a long memory.

"Ten years," Malik said, stepping out of the car into the mountain air. "Ten meetings. Zero wins. I am here to end that today."

Zeb handed him a cup of coffee. Zeb makes his coffee strong enough to stand a spoon in, and he explains football like the weather on the Blue Ridge: you respect it, you dress for it, and you never assume it will stay nice. "You said that last year," he said. "It was 41-20."

It was. App State has won all 10 meetings since 2016. Some were close, like 17-13 in 2020 and 33-26 in 2024. Most were not. The Mountaineers won 56-27 in 2019 and 45-16 in 2021. Malik remembers every one.

But this fall feels a little different to him, and he has reasons.

Georgia State scores 33.9 points a game. Cameran Brown has 14 touchdown throws. He threw 6 against Old Dominion in a 42-10 win. Rodshaun Dorsey has 459 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns. Qwantavius Wiggins has 446 rushing yards. And Xavier Esqillion has 7 sacks, which is the kind of number that keeps a quarterback awake at night.

"We beat Kennesaw State 31-17 on the road," Malik said. "We beat Northern Illinois. We can play."

Zeb nodded. He does not argue with facts. He just adds more.

"You also lost three in a row," he said. "Twenty-two to forty-nine at James Madison. Thirty-two to thirty-eight at Arkansas State. Twenty to thirty-one to Coastal last week."

That is the other part. Georgia State is 4-4. Brown led the Panthers in throws for the first six games, and Ayden Pereira led them the last two. Malik says the Panthers can win with either. Zeb says that is what people say when they are not sure.

App State has its own fog to drive through. The Mountaineers are 5-3, but they managed 3 points at home against Old Dominion in October and 3 points at Georgia Southern last week. Malachi Singleton has 1,915 yards through the air and threw for 331 against Charlotte, but he went 5 for 23 against Old Dominion. Sam Pickett III has 560 receiving yards. Jaquari Lewis has 8 rushing touchdowns. On defense, Colton Phares has 63 tackles and Caleb Sandstrom has 5 sacks.

"When we are good, we are really good," Zeb said. "We beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. We won 35-32 at Coastal."

"And when you are bad," Malik said, "you score 3."

Zeb poured himself more coffee. He did not answer that one.

Here is how it shakes out. Georgia State comes out loose and scores early, and for a while Malik looks like a man about to make history. Esqillion gets home a couple of times. But App State settles down, Lewis finds the end zone, Pickett makes a big grab on third down, and the home crowd carries the Mountaineers through a tight fourth quarter. It is close all afternoon, closer than most of the last ten. App State hangs on.

Malik will drive home with an eleventh story to tell. Zeb says he is welcome back next year, same patio, same coffee.

Before kickoff, they both stand with the veterans and their families at the tailgate. On Heroes Day, the series can wait for a few minutes. Then it is back to football, and back to ten years and counting.

My call: App State Mountaineers 30, Georgia State Panthers 27.

Texas A&M Aggies vs South Carolina Gamecocks prediction for Saturday, November 7: Columbia wakes up to Palmetto Luna Arts' Day of the Dead Celebration on Boyd Plaza at the Columbia Museum of Art, and by afternoon Williams-Brice is the loudest place in the state.

Colt Brazos walked into Beau Ravenel's tailgate like he owned the lot. He is a big man with a bigger voice, and he has no use for indoor volume.

"Gig 'em!" he called. "Eight of the last ten, Beau. Eight of ten!"

Beau Ravenel was flipping shrimp on a grill and did not turn around. "And we won the last three games this year, Colt. Florida, Tennessee, Oklahoma. Have a shrimp."

Colt had a shrimp. Then he had four.

The history really is on the Aggies' side. Texas A&M won 8 of the last 10 meetings, including 48-3 in 2020 and 44-14 in 2021. South Carolina won 44-20 in 2024, but last year the Aggies took it 31-30, and Colt has the replay saved on his phone. He shows it to people who have not asked.

This year feels different to Beau, and he has a quarterback to prove it. LaNorris Sellers has 1,849 yards through the air and 16 touchdowns. He has also run for 603 yards and 6 more scores. Last week in Norman, he threw for 301 yards and ran for 96, and South Carolina won 42-25. Mazeo Bennett Jr. caught 4 balls for 107 yards in that one. The Gamecocks score 36.9 points a game.

"He is the best player on this field," Beau said. "And everybody in this stadium knows it."

Colt does not argue about Sellers. He argues about defense.

Texas A&M gives up 18.9 points a game. The Aggies shut out Missouri State and The Citadel, held Arkansas to 7 and beat Arizona State 48-20. Ray Coney has 40 tackles, and Marco Jones has 2.5 sacks. Colt's theory is simple: if the Aggies can keep Sellers in the pocket and make him throw sideways, the crowd goes quiet.

"You gave up 49 at Alabama," Colt said.

"You scored 6 at LSU," Beau said.

That one hurt. The Aggies have struggled on offense away from home. They lost 6-35 at LSU, 6-27 at Missouri and 20-31 at Alabama. Marcel Reed has 1,390 yards, 8 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. KJ Edwards has 360 rushing yards. Texas A&M is 4-4 and has not played since Oct 24, so Colt is hoping the week off cleared some heads.

Beau's team is 5-3, and three of those losses were close or ugly: 34-41 to Mississippi State, 18-49 at Alabama, 34-35 in overtime to Kentucky. Since then, the Gamecocks have found their legs. Beau credits Justin Okoronkwo, who has 62 tackles, and Tomiwa Durojaiye, who has 4 sacks. Colt credits the schedule. They let that one go too.

Here is how it shakes out. The Aggies come out angry after the week off, and the defense keeps Sellers in check for a half. Reed makes a couple of plays, and Colt gets loud. But Sellers is Sellers. He breaks one with his legs in the third quarter, hits Bennett deep in the fourth, and Williams-Brice shakes. The Aggies answer and keep it close to the end, which is exactly what this series does. South Carolina gets the last word this time.

Before any of that, Beau is walking Colt over to Boyd Plaza. The Day of the Dead Celebration is free, with music, art and family altars, and this is its 15th year in Columbia. Beau's grandmother used to say you should always remember the people who brought you to the game. Colt says he will remember 31-30 for the rest of his life. Beau says that is not what she meant.

My call: South Carolina Gamecocks 28, Texas A&M Aggies 26.

display.fanatic_story:
UL Monroe Warhawks vs Arkansas State Red Wolves prediction for Saturday, November 7: Arkansas State is calling this one USA 250 Day, and it is also Heroes Day, Ag Day and Paragould Day, with the ROTC Hall of Heroes, an in-game commissioning ceremony and the 30th anniversary of the Ring of Honor. Darla Pickens says it is the busiest Saturday in Jonesboro since she can remember.

Remy Thibodeaux drove up from Monroe with a cooler of boudin and a grudge he has carried for a decade.

"One," he said, holding up a finger as he walked into Darla's tailgate. "One time we beat y'all in ten years. And it was last year. Twenty-eight to sixteen."

Darla runs a family farm outside town, and she explains football the way she explains soybeans: you plant, you wait, you harvest. "And nine times," she said, "we beat you."

That part is true. Arkansas State won 9 of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025. Some of them were wild. The Red Wolves won 67-50 in 2017 and 48-41 in 2019. Remy remembers both. He wishes he did not.

This fall has been hard for the Warhawks. UL Monroe is 1-7. It lost 13-62 at Mississippi State, 35-52 at South Alabama and 0-24 to Louisiana Tech. It scores 20.2 points a game and gives up 37.0. Remy does not hide from it. He just points to the one bright spot.

"We won at Troy," he said. "Twenty-one to fourteen. On the road. Aidan Armenta threw 2 touchdowns."

Darla gave him that one. Armenta has 1,323 yards and 10 touchdowns, with only 3 interceptions. Marcellus Jackson caught an 83-yard score last week against Southern Miss. Noah Flemmings has 75 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has 3 sacks. Remy calls Flemmings the bayou bouncer, because nobody gets past him without paying.

Arkansas State is 4-4, and Darla says the record does not tell the whole story. The Red Wolves lost 20-23 at Louisiana and 49-56 to South Alabama, and either of those could have gone the other way. Since then, they won 23-13 at Southern Miss and 38-32 over Georgia State. They have also had a week off to rest.

Trey Owens is the reason Darla sleeps well. He has 1,940 yards and 11 touchdowns. He threw for 418 against South Alabama and 309 against Georgia State. Jaylen Bonelli caught 7 balls for 150 yards in that last one. Joe Drew has 74 tackles from the safety spot. Solomon Baggett leads the team on the ground with 306 yards.

"Our defense gives up some," Darla admitted. "But your defense gives up more."

Remy had boudin in his mouth and could not argue.

Here is how it shakes out. Arkansas State comes out rested and loud, Owens finds Bonelli early, and the Red Wolves go up two scores before the first quarter ends. Armenta keeps UL Monroe in it for a while with some long throws, and Flemmings makes a dozen tackles, because he always does. But the Warhawks cannot slow Owens for four quarters. Arkansas State pulls away in the second half, and Darla's grill stays busy until dark.

The best part of the day happens before kickoff. The ROTC Hall of Heroes welcomes new names, and young officers take their oath right on the field in the commissioning ceremony. Darla has watched that ceremony for years, and she still tears up every time. Remy takes his hat off and stands for every word.

"That part," he said, "I can cheer for."

Then kickoff comes, and he goes right back to hollering for the Warhawks.

If the game gets out of hand, Darla says there is always the NEAVAL Art Show and Sale at the Harlan Henry Center that morning. Remy says he will go if they have a painting of the 2025 game.

My call: Arkansas State Red Wolves 37, UL Monroe Warhawks 19.

Pete Marchetti waves a Blue Hens towel like a semaphore flag. "Nick Minicucci threw for 414 at Western Kentucky. Sean Wilson caught 9 for 183. We've won two in a row."

Delaware has also rotated quarterbacks: Minicucci, Braden Streeter, EJ Archield Jr. and Tyler Bell have each led in throws. My 27-26 is a one-point Owls win at home. display.fanatic_story:
Delaware Blue Hens vs Kennesaw State Owls prediction for Saturday, November 7: it is Homecoming at Kennesaw State and the Mental Health Awareness game, Taste of Kennesaw takes over downtown from 11 in the morning until 6 at night, and Tasha Greer has a full plan for the day.

Pete Marchetti flew down from Wilmington and did not bring a plan. He brought a towel.

"Blue Hens!" he hollered at the tailgate, swinging the towel over his head. "Two in a row! Four hundred fourteen yards at Western Kentucky!"

Tasha is a nurse, and she has seen louder men calmed down by quieter words. "Pete," she said, "you're 4-4."

Pete stopped swinging. She was right. Delaware opened by beating Merrimack 42-7, then lost 26-35 at Vanderbilt and beat Coastal Carolina 22-14. After that it fell apart for a stretch: 3-42 at Virginia, 14-30 to Liberty, 30-33 at Middle Tennessee. Then the Blue Hens woke up. They beat Missouri State 61-38 and won 35-21 at Western Kentucky.

Nick Minicucci is the reason. He has 1,477 yards and 14 touchdowns with only 4 interceptions. He threw 5 touchdowns against Missouri State and 4 more at Western Kentucky, where he went 32 for 38 for 414 yards. Sean Wilson caught 9 balls for 183 yards in that one, and he has 591 on the year. Blake Matthews has 4.5 sacks. Gavin Moul has 53 tackles.

"He is a different quarterback now," Pete said. "You'll see."

Tasha has watched her own team fight through a long fall. Kennesaw State is 2-6, and almost all of it has been heartbreak. The Owls lost 14-17 at Arkansas State, 26-27 to Jacksonville State and 21-24 at Missouri State. Every one of those came down to the last few minutes. Tasha says she aged a year in October.

But last week was different. Kennesaw State went to Middle Tennessee and won 44-28. Rickie Collins went 16 for 19 with 3 touchdowns. Boogie Woods III ran for 2 more scores. Dylan Gary caught 2 balls, and both went for touchdowns. Tasha watched it twice.

"Middle Tennessee beat you," she reminded Pete. "Thirty-three to thirty. We beat them by 16."

Pete thought about that for a while. Football does not work that way, he said. Tasha said she knows, but it felt good to say.

The Owls have pieces. Collins has 1,632 yards through the air. Woods has 358 rushing yards and 6 touchdowns. Javon Rogers has 397 receiving yards. Ugonna Nwoha has 5 sacks up front, and Tywon Christopher has 62 tackles. Tasha thinks Nwoha is the key. If he gets to Minicucci early, the Blue Hens cannot get comfortable.

Homecoming also matters to her for another reason. This is the Mental Health Awareness game, and Tasha has spent her career in hospitals. She talks about checking on friends the way some people talk about stretching before a run. Pete got quiet when she said it. Then he said that was the best thing anybody had said at a tailgate all year, and he meant it. Tasha told him the best part of Homecoming is seeing who shows up for each other, win or lose, and that a towel-waving Blue Hens fan counts too.

Here is how it shakes out. Delaware moves the ball, because Minicucci is playing as well as anybody in this conference right now. Wilson gets loose once. But the home crowd is huge, Nwoha gets home a couple of times, and Woods grinds out the tough yards in the fourth quarter. It comes down to the last drive, like everything does with this Owls team. This time it goes their way.

After the game, if there is anything left at Taste of Kennesaw, Tasha wants a funnel cake and some live music. Pete says the towel comes too.

My call: Kennesaw State Owls 27, Delaware Blue Hens 26.

Hollis is a retired band director from Tuscaloosa, and he hears football like music: tempo, rhythm, a big finish. Remy-Jean is a Baton Rouge lawyer, and she argues football like a closing statement. They have been doing this for years.

"Eight of the last ten," Hollis said. "We won 20-9 last year. We won 42-13 the year before that."

"And we won 46-41 in 2019," Remy-Jean said. "And 32-31 in 2022. In overtime. I was there. You were there. You cried."

Hollis did not deny it.

This year, both teams are 6-2, and both of them can score. Alabama puts up 38.2 points a game. LSU puts up 40.1. The difference is defense. LSU gives up 16.0 a game, the fewest in this matchup by a lot. Alabama gives up 21.2.

"Keelon Russell," Hollis said, counting it out on his fingers like a downbeat. "Two thousand fifty-seven yards. Fifteen touchdowns. Five interceptions. He threw for 365 against South Carolina and 311 against Texas A&M."

The Tide have only stumbled twice. They lost 17-20 to Georgia and 10-26 at Tennessee. Lotzeir Brooks has 488 receiving yards. Rico Scott caught 6 balls for 156 yards against the Aggies. Caleb Woodson has 63 tackles, and Yhonzae Pierre has 3.5 sacks.

Remy-Jean let him finish. Then she began her closing.

"Sam Leavitt," she said. "Two thousand one hundred seventy-three yards. Seventeen touchdowns. He went 32 for 45 for 388 yards at Auburn. Jackson Harris caught 9 for 178 that day. Dilin Jones has 657 rushing yards. And Princewill Umanmielen has 8.5 sacks."

"Eight and a half," Hollis said quietly.

"Eight and a half," she repeated, like a verdict.

LSU's two losses came on the road: 24-32 at Ole Miss and 34-35 in overtime at Kentucky. At home, the Tigers have been a wall. They beat Clemson 51-10, Texas A&M 35-6 and Mississippi State 31-0. Remy-Jean says Tiger Stadium does that to people.

Hollis says Alabama has been to Tiger Stadium before.

Here is how it shakes out. Russell comes out sharp, Brooks gets behind the defense once, and the Tide quiet the crowd for a few minutes. But Leavitt answers, Jones runs hard, and Umanmielen gets home at the worst possible moment for Alabama. It is a shootout into the fourth quarter, the kind both of them will talk about for years. Alabama has the ball late with a chance, and Hollis is on his feet. LSU makes one more stop.

Hollis will say the band was better. Remy-Jean will say that is not how scoring works.

Before any of that, she is taking her nieces to the Mike's Kids Club Tailgate in the Fan Zone. There is a meal package for kids, and there are STEM tables where you can build things and break things. Hollis says that sounds like an Alabama practice. Remy-Jean says he can come along if he keeps the crimson zipped under a jacket.

He agrees, mostly because the jambalaya is that good. By the time they reach the PMAC, he has helped two kids build a paper bridge and lost an argument with a little girl about who has the better mascot. Remy-Jean says that is the only argument he will lose all day. Hollis says the day is young.

Cincinnati Bearcats vs Houston Cougars prediction for Saturday, November 7: Houston is hosting its 13th Annual AfriFest across town at The KBC Houston Event Center, with music, food and culture from 11 in the morning until 7 at night, and Marisol Treviño has already told everybody she is going.

Gus Bellweather flew down from Cincinnati with a Bearcats hoodie and a list.

"Five of the last six," he said, unfolding the list at Marisol's tailgate. "Thirty-four to nothing in 2024. Twenty-four to fourteen in 2023. Thirty-five to twenty in 2021. Shall I go on?"

Marisol is a Houston engineer, and she builds her arguments the way she builds bridges: load first, then style. "You can go on," she said. "Or you can look at what happened last Saturday."

Gus folded the list back up.

Last Saturday, Cincinnati lost 25-49 to Utah at home. Cole Tabb ran for 131 yards and a touchdown, but the defense could not stop anything. That has been the story of the Bearcats' fall. They are 5-3, they score 34.1 points a game and they give up 29.2. They lost 7-34 at Arizona and 42-45 at West Virginia. They also beat Kansas State 31-26 and Texas Tech 37-24, so they are dangerous on any given day.

"Cole Tabb," Gus said, recovering. "Seven hundred fifty-two yards. Ten touchdowns. JC French IV has 13 touchdown throws and 3 interceptions. We do not give the ball away."

That is true, and Marisol knows it. French is careful, and JV Gibson has 461 receiving yards. Jonathan Thompson has 63 tackles, and Patrick Bauer has 3.5 sacks.

Houston is 6-2, and Marisol thinks it is the best Cougars team she has seen in years. Conner Weigman has 2,053 yards, 20 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions. He threw 5 touchdowns in a 35-32 win over Oklahoma State and 4 more in a 35-16 win at Kansas State. Amare Thomas has 620 receiving yards. Makhi Hughes has 516 rushing yards. The defense gives up 21.0 points a game, and Kentrell Webb has 46 tackles from the back of it.

"You lost at Utah too," Gus said.

"Thirteen to twenty-one," Marisol said. "And then we had two weeks to think about it."

Houston has not played since Oct 24, so the Cougars come in rested. Marisol thinks a rested Weigman is the most dangerous player on the field. Gus says Tabb has fresher legs than anybody, because he runs so fast nobody touches him. Marisol says that is not how legs work.

Here is how it shakes out. Tabb breaks a long one early, and for a quarter Gus looks like a man about to add another entry to his list. But Houston settles in. Weigman starts finding Thomas on third downs, Hughes grinds out the tough yards, and the Cougars build a lead before halftime. Cincinnati keeps scoring, because it always does, but the defense cannot get off the field. Houston pulls away in the fourth quarter.

Gus will fly home with his list a little shorter. Marisol says she will mail him a new one. He says he will frame it next to the old one, because a Bearcats fan never throws away proof of the good years. She tells him the good years are a lot like Houston weather in November: pleasant while they last, and gone before you notice.

In the morning, she is taking him to AfriFest. The Nigerian American Multicultural Council hosts it every year, and Marisol says it is the best food in Houston for one day. Gus says he will try everything once. Marisol says he should start with the jollof rice and work from there.

My call: Houston Cougars 37, Cincinnati Bearcats 24.

Oregon Ducks vs Ohio State Buckeyes prediction for Saturday, November 7: Ohio State has called this one Scarlet the Shoe, every fan in the Horseshoe is asked to wear scarlet, and Bud Kowalczyk has been laying out sweaters on his tailgate table since dawn.

Ingrid Halvorsen showed up in green. Of course she did.

"You know what today is," Bud said.

"I know what today is," Ingrid said. "It is the day my Ducks come into your house and remind you about USC."

Bud winced. He is a retired steelworker from Youngstown, and he explains football like a mill shift: you show up, you work, you go home tired. He did not enjoy last Saturday. Ohio State lost 18-30 at USC, and Luke Fahey led the Buckeyes in throws that day instead of Julian Sayin. Bud does not want to talk about why. Ingrid did not ask.

"We are 6-2," he said. "We give up 15.5 points a game. We lost by a point at Texas and we lost at USC. That is it."

That is it. Ohio State beat Illinois 42-19, Iowa 31-14, Maryland 45-16 and Indiana 19-15. Sayin has 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Jeremiah Smith has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns. Bo Jackson has 637 rushing yards. Earl Little Jr. has 43 tackles, and Kenyatta Jackson Jr. has 3 sacks. The Buckeyes score 36.6 points a game.

"Jeremiah Smith," Bud said, "is the best player in America. Write that down."

Ingrid wrote nothing down. She is a software designer from Portland, and she thinks about football like a product launch: the version you ship matters more than the version you planned.

Oregon has shipped a few versions this year. Dante Moore led the Ducks in throws early, including 378 yards against Boise State. Dylan Raiola took over and threw for 289 in a 41-27 win at USC. Brock Thomas led them in throws against Nebraska. Now Raiola is back, and last week he went 22 for 31 for 336 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 34-26 win over Northwestern. Dakorien Moore caught 7 balls for 128 yards and 2 scores in that one.

"We beat USC by 14," Ingrid said. "You lost to USC by 12. Math."

Bud said football does not work that way. Ingrid said it worked fine for her.

Oregon is 5-3, and the losses have been close and frustrating: 31-39 at Oklahoma State, 15-17 to UCLA, 10-21 at Illinois. Jordon Davison has 439 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. Matayo Uiagalelei has 6.5 sacks, and Koi Perich has 53 tackles. The Ducks give up 21.4 points a game.

Here is how it shakes out. Oregon comes out fast, Uiagalelei gets into the backfield early, and for a few minutes the Horseshoe is very quiet. But Ohio State settles in. Smith makes a catch that nobody else in the country makes, Bo Jackson pounds away in the third quarter, and the Buckeyes' defense keeps Raiola from finding Moore deep. Oregon scores enough to keep Ingrid hopeful into the fourth quarter. Ohio State pulls away late.

Bud will celebrate the way he always does, by hugging people he does not know. Ingrid will say the next meeting is in Eugene, and she will mean it as a warning.

Before kickoff, Bud holds out a scarlet sweater. Ingrid looks at it for a long time. She agrees to wear it for exactly one photo, for Scarlet the Shoe, and then the green comes right back on. Bud frames the photo anyway. He says it will hang in his garage next to his old ticket stubs, the ones he never lets anybody touch. Ingrid says she will send him a green frame for it. Bud says he would sooner wear the sweater to Eugene. She says that can be arranged.

My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 31, Oregon Ducks 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Penn State Nittany Lions vs Washington Huskies prediction for Saturday, November 7: Penn State is coming to Husky Stadium for the first time in 105 years, and Washington made sure the welcome party is Homecoming. Vangie Tollefsrud says she has been waiting for this since she was a freshman on the water at dawn, and Luann Kessler says she has been waiting since 1921, which is not true but she said it with a straight face.

Here's the deal. The last time Penn State played on Montlake was the final game of the 1921 season. It was the seventh game ever played at Husky Stadium. This time the Huskies are calling it the Purple Reign Game, and it opens with the Blanket Parade, when former Washington letterwinners stand along the field to welcome the team back out. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET.

"A blanket parade," Luann says. "That's sweet. In Happy Valley we just call that November."

Vangie sets down her third coffee of the morning. "Luann, the blankets are for you. We're polite people. We figured you'd be cold."

The Nittany Lions brought company. Penn State's alumni group booked its first-ever Sailgate, a cruise on Lake Washington aboard the Spirit of Seattle with the Pep Band trumpets, the cheerleaders and the Nittany Lion himself, and it sold out. Washington parents are coming in too, since it doubles as UW Family Weekend, complete with a family section and a scarf.

"Penn State fans on a boat on my lake," Vangie says. "I rowed that lake in the rain for four years. You people get a buffet."

"We get a buffet and a trumpet section," Luann says. "Try to keep up."

Now the football, because these two came to argue.

Luann goes first. Rocco Becht has thrown for 1,839 yards with 13 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Chase Sowell is the go-to guy with 34 catches for 510 yards. Carson Hansen leads the ground game with 374 yards, but the back everybody in State College is talking about this week is Cam Wallace, who ran 22 times for 135 yards in the 31-17 win over Purdue. And then there's Tony Rojas, the linebacker who leads the team in sacks with 5 and tackles with 57. Penn State scores 29.0 a game and gives up 18.6.

"Linebacker U," Luann says. "Rojas is the Peachy Paterno of linebackers. Sweet on the outside, and then he takes your quarterback home."

Vangie takes the floor. Demond Williams Jr. has thrown for 1,495 yards and 9 touchdowns, but Elijah Brown has been the guy taking most of the throws in the last three games, including 19 of 30 for 136 yards in the 17-10 win at Nebraska. Chris Lawson made that day happen with 12 catches for 155 yards, and he has 44 catches for 638 yards this season. Alex McLaughlin leads the defense with 56 tackles, and Jacob Manu has 2.5 sacks. Washington scores 26.5 a game and allows 21.1.

"Lawson against Nebraska was a coxswain calling the stroke," Vangie says. "Every catch right on the beat."

"Seventeen to ten," Luann says. "Very rhythmic. Very low."

"We won in Lincoln in November," Vangie says. "Nobody scores in Lincoln in November. You lost 18-21 at Michigan."

Luann does not respond to that. She looks out the window at the drizzle like it owes her money.

Both teams have been through it. Penn State dropped four straight in the middle of the season, including 20-24 to Wisconsin, 23-31 to USC and that 18-21 loss in Ann Arbor, before getting right against Purdue. Washington lost three in a row too, to Minnesota, at USC and to Iowa, then won at Purdue and at Nebraska.

"We have both been to the dark place," Luann says.

"Ours has better coffee," Vangie says.

There's one more thing Luann wants on the record. The last time these two met, in 2024, Penn State won 35-6.

"That was in State College," Vangie says. "Rain doesn't count when it's yours."

Here's how it plays out on Montlake. The Blanket Parade gets the place loud early, and the Washington defense, led by McLaughlin, keeps the Penn State run game honest in the first half. Becht and Sowell find a rhythm before halftime, and Wallace grinds out the hard yards. Brown looks for Lawson every time Washington needs a first down, and Rojas makes the Husky backfield miserable at least twice. Nobody gets away. It comes down to one last Washington drive and a kick that splits the uprights while the rain gets heavier.

Vangie leaps out of her seat and nearly spills her coffee. Luann says Linebacker U doesn't cry, then cries a little, then buys a Washington scarf anyway because it's cold.

My call: Washington Huskies 24, Penn State Nittany Lions 23.

Charlotte vs UAB prediction: our pick is Charlotte 49ers +11.5, we're on the Over 47.5, and the final we're calling is UAB Blazers 33, Charlotte 49ers 22. Kickoff is 3:30 PM ET Saturday at Protective Stadium in Birmingham, and this spread has moved a point and a half toward UAB since it opened at −10.

UAB is wearing gray jerseys with the names of kids from Children's Harbor on the back, and the Blazers have not lost at Protective this year. Priya Halloran, who prices risk for a bank in uptown Charlotte, says that is exactly why the market got greedy.

"The 49ers are a distressed asset," Priya says. "Distressed assets are where you get paid."

Ozella Birchfield does not like the word distressed in her town. "Birmingham was built on things people wrote off, honey. Steel doesn't care about your spreadsheet."

Why Charlotte with the points: the 49ers are 1-7, and they give up 40.2 a game, so nobody wants them. But the offense changed when Conner Harrell took over the throws. He has 831 yards, 5 touchdowns and 2 interceptions, he won 38-31 at Temple, and he took Tulane to overtime in a 31-38 loss. Henry Rutledge ran 22 times for 121 yards in that Tulane game. UAB is not built to run away from anybody. The Blazers score 21.6 a game, and they just lost 10-30 at South Florida with Ryder Burton going 13 of 27 for 149 yards. Eleven and a half is a lot of points for an offense like that to clear.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 51.5 and it has come down to 47.5. We're on the Over 47.5. Charlotte's defense is the reason: 40.2 allowed per game is an open door, and UAB's Rod Robinson II and CJ Smith, who has 21 catches for 403 yards, should walk through it. Harrell and Jaden Barnes, with 48 catches, can put up enough on the other end.

The room is split on the side but not on the over/under. The Formula likes the 49ers getting 11.5 and has it UAB 31-23. Next Man Up likes UAB −11.5 and has it UAB 35-20. In The Trenches has no side this week. The Formula likes the Over. Next Man Up likes the Over too. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

UAB's defense has teeth with Marlin Dean at 7.5 sacks and Muaaz Byard at 76 tackles, so Harrell will take some hits. That's why we have UAB winning by 11 and not by 3.

"Forged, not given," Ozella says.

"Priced, not guessed," Priya says.

display.fanatic_story:
Charlotte 49ers vs UAB Blazers prediction for Saturday, November 7: Protective Stadium turns into Kids Takeover, the Blazers wear gray jerseys with 99 children's names on the back, and Ozella Birchfield has already ironed her gray sweater twice. Priya Halloran drove down from uptown Charlotte with a spreadsheet, a thermos and the calm face of a woman who has watched her team go 1-7.

Here's the deal. Saturday is the 10th annual Children's Harbor Game. Since the first one in 2017, UAB players have swapped their own names off the backs of their jerseys for the names of kids facing serious medical challenges, and each child gets the jersey worn in their honor after the game. More than 400 tickets and parking tickets were bought for the families. Fans are asked to wear gray. The Blazers are 8-1 in these games.

"I'm going to cry before kickoff," Ozella says. "Then I'm going to yell. In that order. Every year."

Priya nods. "That's a beautiful tradition. I'm still wearing teal. I'll clap in teal."

There's also a display in Blazer Village this week called "Derail the Niners." Priya has seen it.

"Derail," she says. "Clever jab. We already derailed ourselves in September. You can't derail a train that's in the shop."

"Forged, not given, honey," Ozella says. "Birmingham was a train town before it was anything. We know what a derailment looks like."

Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET, and before that the Blazer Walk brings the team through Uptown with the Marching Blazers. UAB is 4-0 at Protective this season, which Ozella will tell you about whether you ask or not.

Now the football.

Priya goes first, and she goes first because she has the better story to tell, even at 1-7. Charlotte's season turned when Conner Harrell took over at quarterback. He has 831 yards with 5 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions, and in his three games the 49ers won 38-31 at Temple and took Tulane to overtime before losing 31-38. Henry Rutledge leads the ground game with 452 yards, and he ran 22 times for 121 yards against Tulane. Jaden Barnes has 48 catches for 462 yards. Gavin Willis leads the defense with 65 tackles.

"The first five games were a write-down," Priya says. "Since then we're a turnaround story. I'd hold."

Ozella takes the floor. Ryder Burton has thrown for 1,333 yards. Rod Robinson II has 450 rushing yards. CJ Smith is the big-play guy with 21 catches for 403 yards, which is a lot of yards for not many catches. Then there's the defense. Marlin Dean has 7.5 sacks, and Muaaz Byard leads the team with 76 tackles.

"Marlin Dean is a blast furnace," Ozella says. "You open the door, you get burned."

"Your team lost 10-30 at South Florida last week," Priya says.

"And we beat Navy 24-20 in September," Ozella says. "Furnaces have off days. The fire doesn't go out."

Charlotte scores 20.6 a game and gives up 40.2. UAB scores 21.6 and allows 25.2. Ozella keeps reading the 40.2 out loud like it's a hymn.

"I know that figure," Priya says. "I put it in red. It has been in red since September."

The recent history is even. Going back to 2017, they've split four meetings, two apiece. Charlotte won the last one, 29-27 in 2024, and Priya remembers the Thanksgiving weekend drive home like it was a victory lap at Charlotte Motor Speedway.

"Two and two," Ozella says. "Somebody breaks it Saturday."

"Somebody always does," Priya says.

Here's how it plays out under the Birmingham sky. The building is gray and loud early, and the Blazers come out flying in those jerseys. Robinson gets UAB rolling on the ground, and Smith catches a long one over the top that makes Ozella stand on her chair. Charlotte stays in it longer than anybody in Uptown wants, with Harrell finding Barnes on third downs and Rutledge running hard. But Dean gets home a couple of times in the second half, and Byard is everywhere. UAB pulls away in the fourth quarter, and the kids on the jerseys get the afternoon they deserve.

Ozella hugs a stranger in gray. Priya opens a spreadsheet tab called "Write-Downs," adds one more row, and then shuts the laptop and claps for the kids anyway, in teal.

My call: UAB Blazers 33, Charlotte 49ers 22.

Temple vs Navy prediction: our pick is Temple Owls +7.5, we're on the Under 53.5, and the final we're calling is Navy Midshipmen 30, Temple Owls 23. Kickoff is 3:30 PM ET Saturday in Annapolis, where the spread opened at Navy −7.5 and has not moved off it.

Navy is 2-6 and so is Temple, which makes this a game for people who love football and nobody else. Teddy Fiorella, who has never left North Philly without a gym bag, is fine with that. Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather is not.

"Seven and a half is a lot of hook for a team that just lost by 22 to Notre Dame," Teddy says.

"Notre Dame is not Temple, Theodore," Annabel says. "Adjust your heading."

Why Temple with the points: last year's game was decided by one point, 32-31, and the last nine meetings split five for Navy and four for Temple. These programs play close. Navy gives up 29.9 a game, and it lost 39-49 at home to North Texas and 34-38 at UTSA in back-to-back weeks. Temple has Ajani Sheppard, who has 1,245 yards with 8 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions, though all three came in the 9-17 loss at East Carolina. Keveun Mason has 564 rushing yards, so Temple can grind a little too. A team that can run the ball and shorten the game is how you stay inside a touchdown and a hook.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 52.5 and it is up a point to 53.5. We're on the Under 53.5. Navy's offense is Jackson Gutierrez running the ball, with 979 yards and 13 touchdowns on the ground. That keeps the clock moving. He also has 717 yards through the air, mostly on a handful of throws a game. Temple only scores 23.6 a game. Both teams want long drives, and long drives eat the second half.

The room splits both ways. The Formula lands on Temple +7.5 without backing it hard and has it Navy 30-24. Next Man Up lands on Navy −7.5 without backing it hard and has it Navy 30-21. In The Trenches has no side this week. The Formula lands on the Over without backing it hard. Next Man Up lands on the Under without backing it hard. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Curly Ordonez has 77 tackles for Temple, and he is going to see a lot of Gutierrez. Navy's Coleman Cauley has 63 tackles and MarcAnthony Parker has 4 sacks. Neither defense is going to shut the other down. That is why we think Navy wins by a touchdown and not by more.

"Ya gotta take a punch, Commander," Teddy says.

"Then keep your guard up, Theodore," Annabel says.

Navy Midshipmen 30, Temple Owls 23. Temple Owls cover the 7.5. Under 53.5.

Temple Owls vs Navy Midshipmen prediction for Saturday, November 7: both teams walk into Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium at 2-6, and Teddy Fiorella says that makes it the most honest game in America. Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather says it makes it a game where somebody gets to stop the bleeding, and she has a chart showing which way the current runs.

Here's the deal. Kickoff in Annapolis is 3:30 p.m. ET. Before that, the Navy Football Brotherhood sets up its tailgate at Gate 5 and Taylor Avenue at noon, and the Naval Academy classes of 2011, 2016 and 2021 are back for their 15th, 10th and 5th reunions. This is also the season the stadium is marking the 100th anniversary of Navy's 1926 national championship team.

"Nineteen twenty-six," Teddy says. "In Philly we were busy inventing everything else."

"In Annapolis we were busy winning a national title, Theodore," Annabel says. "Note it in the log."

The stadium got new food this year too, including cream of crab soup and coffee from Travelin' Tom's in Annapolis. And in the southwest corner of the stadium, fans can take photos with a Blue Angel and a Marine Corps Harrier.

"Cream of crab soup," Teddy says. "Fancy. Where's the cheesesteak?"

"In Philadelphia," Annabel says. "Where you left it."

Teddy is wearing a Temple hoodie and running shoes. He jogged the steps at the stadium twice before anybody else showed up. Annabel watched him from the parking lot with a coffee and said nothing, which is the most frightening thing she can do.

Now the football.

Teddy goes first, because he is louder. Ajani Sheppard has 1,245 yards with 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions, and yes, all three interceptions came in the 9-17 loss at East Carolina last week. Keveun Mason is the workhorse with 564 rushing yards. Colin Chase leads the receivers with 330 yards. And then there's Curly Ordonez, the linebacker, who leads the team with 77 tackles and 2 sacks.

"Ordonez is a Philly guy in spirit," Teddy says. "He'll hit you, then help you up, then hit you again."

Annabel takes the floor. Jackson Gutierrez runs the Navy offense, and he does it on the ground. He has 979 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns, plus 717 yards through the air on very few throws. Jordan Collins, the tight end, has 212 receiving yards on just 6 catches. Coleman Cauley leads the defense with 63 tackles, and MarcAnthony Parker has 4 sacks.

"Gutierrez is a destroyer escort," Annabel says. "Low profile. Hard to stop. Keeps coming."

"Your team gave up 49 to North Texas," Teddy says.

"Steady as she goes," Annabel says. "And your team lost to Charlotte."

Teddy does sit-ups on the spot. Out of spite.

The numbers say these two belong together. Temple scores 23.6 a game and gives up 26.6. Navy scores 27.6 and gives up 29.9. Over the last nine meetings, Navy won five and Temple won four. Last year Navy won 32-31.

"One point," Teddy says. "One point, Commander."

"A point is a point," Annabel says. "Ask anyone who has docked a ship."

Both teams are coming off a bad week. Temple lost at East Carolina. Navy lost 13-35 to Notre Dame. Navy also dropped close ones at UTSA, 34-38, and at UAB, 20-24.

Here's how it plays out on the Severn. Navy keeps the ball for long, grinding drives, and Gutierrez carries it over and over. Temple answers with Mason on the ground and a couple of big throws from Sheppard to Chase. Ordonez makes a big stop in the third quarter that makes Teddy run up and down his row like it's the art museum steps. But Navy's running game wears on Temple in the fourth quarter, and Cauley gets the stop the Midshipmen need. It's a one-score game until late.

Annabel rings an imaginary ship's bell and says "Anchors aweigh." Teddy says you gotta take a punch, takes the punch, and asks where the cream of crab soup stand is.

My call: Navy Midshipmen 30, Temple Owls 23.
