Marshall Thundering Herd vs Georgia Southern Eagles prediction for Saturday, November 7: it's Homecoming in Statesboro, it's Military Appreciation Day at Paulson Stadium, and Royce Ogeechee has been at the Bishop Alumni Center since before the coffee was ready. Mercy Holderby drove down from Huntington in a green sweater, green socks and, she swears, green earrings she was born wearing.

Here's the deal. Georgia Southern is rolling Homecoming and Military Appreciation Day into one, and the alumni tailgate at the Bishop Alumni Center runs from noon until 3 p.m. as a Salute to Service tailgate for active-duty service members, veterans and military families. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET.

And this one has history. Saturday is the 11th all-time meeting between these two schools. They played six times from 1989 to 1996, back when both were two of the most famous programs in I-AA, and then picked it back up when Marshall joined the Sun Belt in 2022.

"I-AA," Royce says, and his eyes get wet. "The option. The buses. Beautiful Eagle Creek. Mercy, those were the days."

"Those were our days too, Royce," Mercy says. "Huntington remembers every one of those games."

"So does Statesboro," Royce says. "Every single snap."

Mercy lets that one sit. She's a nurse. She has patience, and she has a long memory.

The last three meetings were decided by a combined 11 points. Marshall won 38-33 in 2023. Georgia Southern won 24-23 in 2024 and 24-19 last year in Huntington.

"Five points, one point, five points," Royce says. "Y'all keep making me nervous."

"Good," Mercy says.

Now the football.

Royce goes first, because it's his house. Max Johnson has thrown for 1,924 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against App State last week he went 36 of 47 for 327 yards in a 19-3 win. Alex Taylor is his go-to guy, with 34 catches for 435 yards, and he caught 10 against App. On defense, Anthony Bynum has 5 sacks, and Brandon Tyson leads the team with 39 tackles. Georgia Southern gives up 20.5 a game.

"Our defense held App to 3," Royce says. "Three. That's a peanut-sized number, and I know peanuts."

Mercy takes the floor. Marshall is 5-3, and the Herd won 36-23 at Old Dominion last week. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson has 1,107 passing yards, and Zion Turner has taken his share of snaps too. Judah Price leads the ground game with 319 yards and ran for 82 at Old Dominion. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 372 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns. Caleb Clark-Glover leads the defense with 59 tackles, and Kelvon McBride has 3 sacks.

"We are 5-3," Mercy says. "Say it with me. Five and three."

"Y'all also lost 0-45 at Penn State," Royce says.

"September," Mercy says. "That was September. We are a November team."

Marshall scores 23.5 a game and gives up 29.8. Georgia Southern scores 23.8 and gives up 20.5. Mercy reads the Marshall defense figure, then closes her eyes like she's checking a pulse.

"It's going to be fine," she says. "It's always fine. We rebuild. That's what we do."

Royce takes his hat off for that one. Everybody in Statesboro knows what Marshall means when it says that.

Here's how it plays out in Statesboro. The Homecoming crowd is loud, and the veterans honored before kickoff get the biggest cheer of the day. Johnson gets the Eagles moving early with Taylor on short throws, and Georgia Southern punches in a couple of scores before halftime. Marshall stays in it with Price running hard and Turner-Bradshaw making a big catch down the sideline. But Bynum gets home on a third down in the third quarter, and the Eagles turn it into points. The Herd fights to the end, the way the Herd always does, but Georgia Southern pulls away late.

Royce cracks a bag of boiled peanuts and hugs a veteran at the tailgate. Mercy hums "We Are" all the way to the car, sniffles once, and promises Royce that Huntington will remember this.

My call: Georgia Southern Eagles 31, Marshall Thundering Herd 19.

Western Kentucky Hilltoppers vs Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders prediction for Saturday, November 7: it's Homecoming at Floyd Stadium, it's the Hall of Fame Game, and Opal Stonebriar brought two casseroles, one for her people and one for Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt, because she's going to feed you before she corrects you. Tops drove down from Bowling Green with a hot towel still slung over one shoulder from his last customer.

Here's the deal. This is Middle Tennessee's first November Homecoming since 2008, and the Blue Raiders are making a whole day of it. It's also Youth Sports Day and Blue Raider Kids Club Day, so kids walk in the Homecoming parade and form the high-five tunnel when the team runs out. Kickoff is 3:30 p.m. ET in Murfreesboro.

"A high-five tunnel," Tops says. "Very sweet. We'll wave on our way through."

"Thurman, the children will remember your manners," Opal says. "Mind them."

Floyd Stadium opened in 1933. It holds 27,303 people. The Blue Raiders are 55-29-2 all-time on Homecoming, and 21-9-2 in Homecoming games played in November. Opal has those figures written inside the lid of her casserole dish.

"I didn't need to know that," Tops says.

"Everybody needs to know that," Opal says.

But this is a rivalry, and Tops has his own figures. Western Kentucky leads the all-time series 39-35-1. The Hilltoppers have won 7 in a row and nine of the last ten. Last year was 42-26. In Murfreesboro, though, Middle Tennessee leads 21-17-1, which is the one fact Opal holds onto like a hymnal.

"Seven straight," Tops says, polishing an imaginary razor. "That's a lot of fresh haircuts, Opal."

"Aren't you sweet for counting," Opal says. "Now count to 21-17-1."

Now the football.

Tops goes first, unhurried, like he has all afternoon. Brock Glenn is the guy for Western Kentucky. He has 887 passing yards, and he leads the team in rushing with 451 yards and 5 touchdowns. Against Delaware he ran 17 times for 129 yards. Jonathan Stafford Jr. leads the receivers with 46 catches for 433 yards. On defense, Jaylen Lewis has 62 tackles and Westen Ard has 2.5 sacks.

"Glenn is a straight-razor quarterback," Tops says. "Smooth, quick, and you don't see him coming."

Opal takes the floor. Roman Gagliano has thrown for 1,587 yards with 12 touchdowns. Cam'ron Lacy is his go-to target, or as Opal calls him, "my boy," with 45 catches for 510 yards. Antonio Martin leads the ground game with 586 yards, and he ran for 106 against Kennesaw State. Korey Smith leads the defense with 73 tackles.

"Korey Smith is the deacon of that defense," Opal says. "He keeps everybody in their pew."

"You gave up 44 to Kennesaw State last week," Tops says.

"We did," Opal says, setting down the casserole spoon very carefully. "And you gave up 35 to Delaware. Hand me the rolls."

Both teams have had a tough fall. Western Kentucky is 3-5 and gives up 31.1 a game. Middle Tennessee is 4-4 and gives up 29.6. Both offenses can score. Both defenses have had rough weeks.

"So it's a shootout," Tops says.

"It's a homecoming," Opal says. "Different thing. More casseroles."

Here's how it plays out in Murfreesboro. The kids give the Blue Raiders a loud send-off through the high-five tunnel, and Middle Tennessee comes out swinging with Gagliano hitting Lacy early. Glenn answers with his legs, breaking a long run that makes Tops stand up in the visitors' section. It goes back and forth all afternoon. Martin grinds out tough yards in the fourth quarter, Korey Smith makes a stop on WKU's last real chance, and the Homecoming crowd gets to sing on the way out.

Opal hugs every Hall of Famer she can find. Tops sits quietly with his hot towel over his face for a full minute, then says, "Good game, Opal. Next year you're coming to my shop."

My call: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 28, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 27.

"Rock Chalk," Fitz says. "Wait, it's FOOTBALL season?"

"It has been since September, Fitz," Knox says. "Your team is 3-5."

"In basketball we'd still be undefeated," Fitz says.

Here's the deal. Saturday is Kansas' Salute to Service game and its "Beak the Stigma" game, and it's the fifth home game of the season at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium. Kickoff is 3:45 p.m. ET. Kansas is 3-1 at home this year, and the last time the Jayhawks played there, they beat Baylor 25-24 on Homecoming on Oct. 24, coming back from 11 points down in the fourth quarter.

"Eleven points in the fourth quarter," Knox says. "That's a launch coaster. Zero to sixty."

"I watched the end of that one," Fitz says. "Somebody told me it was on."

Knox has his own coaster story. UCF beat BYU 39-31 in overtime on Oct. 24. Then the Knights went home against Baylor and lost 9-41. Up the lift hill, then straight down.

"That's not a ride," Fitz says. "That's a malfunction."

"It's a lesson in physics," Knox says. "What goes up comes down hard."

Fitz insists on giving Knox the full tour. He points out every concession stand, especially the one where he plans to spend most of the second quarter.

"You know there's a game going on during all this," Knox says.

"I've heard rumors," Fitz says. "Somebody said there's a scoreboard and everything."

"There is," Knox says. "And it counts by sevens, not twos."

Now the football.

Knox goes first, flipping through his clipboard. Keyone Jenkins has thrown for 1,181 yards and 11 touchdowns. Duke Watson leads the ground game with 597 yards. Josh Derry has 37 catches for 428 yards. UCF scores 29.8 a game. On defense, Tackett Curtis leads with 48 tackles and Isaiah Nixon has 2.5 sacks.

"Jenkins is a smooth operator," Knox says. "When he's on, it's a ten-car train with no wobble."

"Against Baylor he threw for 82 yards," Fitz says.

"Every coaster has a maintenance day," Knox says.

Fitz takes over, confused but loyal. Isaiah Marshall has 1,506 passing yards with 11 touchdowns. Cole Ballard threw for 285 at TCU last week, though Kansas lost 16-22. Dylan Edwards leads the backs with 573 yards. Nik McMillan has 466 receiving yards on just 25 catches, which Fitz says is like a guard who only shoots threes. Trey Lathan has 55 tackles. Leroy Harris III has 3.5 sacks.

"McMillan's a sharpshooter," Fitz says. "Catch, go, gone."

"That's a good ratio," Knox says. "I respect the engineering."

Kansas scores 29.1 a game and gives up 23.8. UCF gives up 25.2. Knox notes that these teams have met before. Kansas won 51-22 in 2023 and 27-20 last year.

"Two straight," Fitz says. "Is that good in football?"

"It's good in anything, Fitz," Knox sighs.

Here's how it plays out in Lawrence. The Salute to Service crowd fills the stands early, and Kansas comes out fast with Marshall finding McMillan deep. UCF answers, because Jenkins and Watson are too good to stay quiet. It's a back-and-forth game, a real wooden coaster, all rattle and noise. Edwards grinds out the clock in the fourth quarter, and Lathan makes the stop that ends UCF's last drive.

Knox folds up his clipboard and says it was a good ride. Fitz checks his phone to see when basketball starts.

My call: Kansas Jayhawks 29, UCF Knights 25.

Rice Owls vs North Texas Mean Green prediction for Saturday, November 7: Odalys Chen-Moreau, a Rice PhD student who carries a notebook full of footnotes, has driven up to Denton for Homecoming, and Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, a Denton jazz drummer, is tapping out a beat on the hood of her car before she has even parked.

"Is that a samba?" Odalys asks.

"It's the Mean Green fight tempo," Grady says. "Very fast. You'll see."

Here's the deal. This is the 80th annual Homecoming at North Texas. The Mean Green have held a Homecoming every season since 1946. This is just the third time Rice has been the Homecoming opponent. North Texas is 53-25-1 all-time on Homecoming and has won 7 of its last 9. Kickoff is 4:00 p.m. ET at DATCU Stadium.

"Eighty years," Odalys says. "Now that's a sample size I respect."

"You hear that?" Grady says. "She respects something."

Odalys reminds him that Rice has its own Homecoming crowd back in Houston, and that the Marching Owl Band would turn this whole parade into a skit. Grady says he would pay good money to see that, and he means it, and he would bring his own snare drum to join in.

Now the football.

Grady goes first, drumming on a cooler lid. Tayven Jackson has thrown for 2,577 yards with 22 touchdowns and only 5 interceptions. Last week he threw for 404 yards in a 48-41 win over Florida Atlantic. Jahiem White has run for 1,054 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he went for 193 against the Owls from Boca. Justin Stevenson has 50 catches for 781 yards and 8 touchdowns. North Texas scores 43.8 a game.

"That's bebop," Grady says. "Four hundred yards. A drum solo every drive."

"Correlation is not causation," Odalys says. "But I admit that's a lot of yards."

Odalys flips open her notebook. Jacurri Brown leads Rice with 669 rushing yards and has thrown for 478. But the headline is Gael Ochoa. At Florida Atlantic, Ochoa ran 12 times for 259 yards and 4 touchdowns. Rice lost that one 49-51, which Odalys describes as "statistically devastating." Jordan Clark leads the receivers with 257 yards. AJ Brown has 59 tackles, and Chibby Nwajuaku has 2 sacks.

"Twelve carries, 259 yards," Odalys says. "N is too small. But it's a very exciting N."

"That's a great solo," Grady says. "But can he play a full set?"

Here's the honest part. Rice is 1-7. North Texas is 6-2. The Mean Green give up 31.9 a game, so Rice can score. But the Owls give up 31.8, and North Texas has been scoring in bunches. Last year North Texas won 56-24, and the Mean Green are 7-1 against Rice since 2016.

"Seven and one," Grady says. "That's a pretty steady groove."

"Eight games," Odalys says. "Still small. I'm writing it down anyway."

Zakye Barker has 62 tackles for North Texas, and Davion Rhodes has 4 sacks. Grady says Barker plays like a bass player, never flashy, always there.

Here's how it plays out in Denton. The Homecoming crowd is loud early, and Jackson hits Stevenson for a long score in the first quarter. White adds two short touchdowns. Rice answers with Ochoa and Brown running hard, and the Owls hang around for a while. But North Texas just keeps pushing the tempo, and by the fourth quarter the Mean Green are playing in double time. Barker makes a stop on fourth down to end Rice's last real drive.

Odalys closes her notebook and admits the sample is getting bigger. Grady hands her a pair of drumsticks and tells her to count it off.

My call: North Texas Mean Green 42, Rice Owls 24.

"What does that mean?" Nola asks.

"It means we're ready," Tessa says. "Tested all week. No bugs."

"Out on the farm we'd call that ready for harvest," Nola says.

Here's the deal. Saturday is Parent & Family Weekend at San José State. There's a Brew & Vine pregame tasting, and the Spartans are holding a Military & First Responders Salute to Service with Veterans Day coming up. Kickoff is 4:00 p.m. ET, which is 1:00 in the afternoon in San José, and the gameday is presented by Webcor. Students get in free with their Tower ID.

"Free with an ID card," Nola says. "Back home we'd charge them in sweet corn."

Tessa's parents are coming in for Family Weekend, and she has already promised them a win. Nola says her grandpa used to say not to count your bushels until the combine is in the shed.

Now the football.

Nola goes first, and she's honest about it. Northern Illinois is 0-8. The Huskies score 16.2 a game and give up 37.6. But they lost only 24-31 at UNLV last week, and they have real players. Taron Dickens has thrown for 1,617 yards. DeAree Rogers has 64 catches for 633 yards. Telly Johnson Jr. has 574 rushing yards. Jack Murray leads the defense with 58 tackles.

"Knee-high by the Fourth of July," Nola says. "We were a little late planting this year. But the crop is coming."

"That's a long sprint cycle," Tessa says, kindly. "But I've shipped worse code than an 0-8 roster. Every team gets a hotfix eventually."

"We're due," Nola says. "My grandpa always said the late corn is the sweetest."

Tessa takes over, scrolling through her laptop. Luke Weaver has thrown for 1,810 yards and 11 touchdowns. Carson Clark leads the receivers with 55 catches for 642 yards. Jabari Bates has 649 rushing yards. On defense, Jayland McGlothen has 6 sacks, and Dylan Lee leads the team with 78 tackles. San José State gives up only 22.3 a game.

"McGlothen is our firewall," Tessa says. "Six sacks. Nothing gets through."

"And your offense?" Nola asks.

Tessa winces. San José State scores 19.9 a game, and the Spartans lost 16-21 to New Mexico last week. Weaver has 8 interceptions this season.

"Some days you push to production and it breaks," Tessa says. "Rollback, patch, try again."

The two teams haven't played each other since 2016, so neither side has fresh bragging rights. Nola says that's fine, because DeKalb people don't brag anyway, they just show up on time.

But the Spartans defense takes over in the second half. Bates grinds out yards, Lee makes stop after stop, and San José State pulls away.

Nola shakes Tessa's hand and says there's always next season's harvest. Tessa closes her laptop and says the release went fine, then invites Nola to dinner with her parents, who want to hear all about the corn.

"Gold?" Clementine asks.

"It's Homecoming, mija," Lourdes says. "And Military Appreciation. Everybody wears gold. Even the visitors, if they have manners."

Here's the deal. Saturday is Homecoming at FIU, and it's also Military Appreciation day, with the whole crowd asked to wear gold. Kickoff is 4:00 p.m. ET in Miami. Lourdes grew up in Sweetwater, a short drive from campus, and she says this is the one game a year her whole family shows up for, cousins included.

"How many cousins?" Clementine asks.

"Enough to fill a section," Lourdes says. "Abuela keeps the list."

Clementine pulls on the gold shirt over her fleece vest, which Lourdes says is a crime against the Miami weather. Clementine says she's dressed for a river in November, not a stadium in Florida.

Now the football.

Clementine goes first, the way she reads a river: calm, patient, looking for where it runs fast. Henry Belin IV took over at quarterback for Missouri State in October and has 1,071 passing yards and 8 touchdowns. His big target is Isaiah Myers, who has 41 catches for 873 yards and 8 touchdowns. Jared Lloyd leads the defense with 86 tackles, and Josh Lukusa has 2.5 sacks. Last week the Bears beat Sam Houston 24-3.

"Myers is the rapids," Clementine says. "You see him coming and you still can't stop him."

"We'll see," Lourdes says, pouring two tiny cups of cafecito.

Lourdes takes over. JJ Kohl has thrown for 1,801 yards and 11 touchdowns. Maguire Anderson leads the receivers with 41 catches for 596 yards. Devonte Lyons has 435 rushing yards. On defense, DeeJay Holmes Jr. has 5 sacks and DeAndre Boykins leads with 45 tackles. FIU gives up only 20.4 a game.

"Our defense is like Abuela's kitchen," Lourdes says. "You don't get through without permission."

Then Lourdes admits the hard part. FIU has lost three in a row, including 10-49 at Liberty last week. The Panthers score only 18.9 a game. Kohl has 9 interceptions.

"That's a muddy stretch of river," Clementine says, gently.

"It's a bad week," Lourdes says. "Every family has one. But we're 3-1 at home."

Clementine has one more thing. Missouri State won this matchup 28-21 last year. Lourdes says she does not remember that game, and her cousins don't either, and if anybody brings it up at the tailgate, they'll be cut off from the cafecito.

Both teams are 3-5. Missouri State scores 24.4 a game and gives up 30.9. These are two teams looking for a good afternoon, and only one of them will get it.

Here's how it plays out in Miami. The gold crowd is loud, the cousins fill their section, and the veterans in the stands get the biggest cheer of the day on Military Appreciation day. Myers catches a long one early, and Clementine stands up in her fleece. But Holmes Jr. gets after Belin IV, and the FIU defense settles in. Kohl finds Anderson for a touchdown before halftime, Lyons runs hard in the second half, and Boykins makes the stop that ends Missouri State's last drive.

Lourdes pours one more cafecito for Clementine and says she can come back next year, as long as she wears gold again. Clementine says she'll bring a lighter vest.

My call: Florida International Panthers 26, Missouri State Bears 21.

Louisiana Tech Bulldogs vs Troy Trojans prediction for Saturday, November 7: Booker "Champ" Tullos, a former Louisiana Tech fullback who grows peaches in Ruston, has driven across three states with a crate of the last fruit of the season, and Marlo Pickens, who long-snapped at Troy, meets him downtown with a sack of boiled peanuts and a seat on the parade route.

"Peaches in November?" Marlo asks.

"Preserves," Champ says. "Same spirit."

Here's the deal. It's Homecoming in Troy, and the theme this year is "Flight 1887," a nod to the university's founding in 1887. The parade rolls through downtown Troy at 10 a.m., presented by the Pike County Chamber of Commerce. The alumni tailgate starts at 11:30 at the Alumni House, with Hooks Bar-B-Q doing the cooking. From 11 to 1, there's "Pipers in the Park" at Janice Hawkins Cultural Arts Park. The Homecoming queen is crowned at halftime, and Troy Mayor Jason Reeves is among the Alumni of the Year. Kickoff is 4:00 p.m. ET.

"Bagpipes, barbecue and a parade," Champ says. "Y'all don't do anything halfway."

"Wait until you hear the Sound of the South," Marlo says. "That band will rattle your peaches."

Champ says he'll take the barbecue first and the bagpipes second. Marlo says that's the right order.

Now the football.

Champ goes first, standing up like he's still in the backfield. Louisiana Tech is 6-2. The Bulldogs score 32.6 a game and give up only 20.9. Blake Baker has thrown for 1,327 yards with 13 touchdowns and just 1 interception. Jalen Mickens leads the receivers with 43 catches for 618 yards. And then there's Alonzo Jackson Jr., who has 7 sacks and 57 tackles.

"Jackson is a wrecking ball," Champ says. "I'd have loved to block for a guy like that. Or better, not block against him."

"One interception all year?" Marlo asks.

"One," Champ says. "Baker takes care of the ball like I take care of my peach trees."

Last week the Bulldogs won 35-20 at South Alabama. Champ has the box score folded in his shirt pocket.

Marlo takes over, cracking a peanut. Troy is 4-4, but the Trojans just won 24-21 in overtime at James Madison with Tucker Kilcrease at quarterback. Goose Crowder has 1,162 passing yards on the season. Gavin Griffin leads the backs with 436 yards. TK Keyes has 282 receiving yards. On defense, Donnie Smith has 7 sacks, and Keno Jones leads with 65 tackles. Troy scores 23.0 a game and gives up 24.4.

"Donnie Smith has as many sacks as your guy," Marlo says.

"He does," Champ admits. "That's a fair fight."

"And Troy is 3-1 at home," Marlo adds, and Champ nods along.

These two teams haven't met since 2016, so there is no fresh grudge. Champ says that's good, because he'd rather make friends over barbecue.

Here's how it plays out in Troy. The parade crowd fills Veterans Memorial Stadium, the Sound of the South plays the Trojans onto the field, and Troy comes out with energy. Smith gets to Baker once early, and the Homecoming crowd goes wild. But Baker is patient, and he finds Mickens for two big gains before halftime. The queen is crowned at the break with Louisiana Tech in front. Troy fights back in the second half, Griffin running hard and Jones making stops, but Jackson Jr. comes up with a sack on Troy's final drive.

Marlo hands Champ the last of the boiled peanuts. Champ hands Marlo a jar of peach preserves. Both of them agree it was a good day in Troy.

My call: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs 27, Troy Trojans 22.

Vanderbilt vs Mississippi State prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Homecoming in Starkville: Mississippi State has spent the week of Nov. 1 through Nov. 8 telling everybody There's No Place Like State, and the Saturday payoff is a 4:15 PM ET kickoff at Davis Wade Stadium with the crowd asked to wear maroon. My side is Mississippi State Bulldogs −3, my call on points is Over 48.5, and my score is Mississippi State Bulldogs 32, Vanderbilt Commodores 23.

Pippa Ashcroft has the economist's case for the Commodores. "We're 3-5, but Junior Sherrill has 706 receiving yards, and Jared Curtis threw for 247 and two scores at Kentucky. We score 22.8 a game. Dogs that bark late can still get bit."

Wade Pettus answers from the feed-store notebook he keeps in his jacket. "Vandy is 0-5 in the league and gives up 30.2 a game. Ole Miss hung 52 on y'all. Homecoming crowd, maroon everywhere, and we have Fluff Bothwell with 563 rushing yards and Anthony Evans III with 666 receiving."

Here is why I lay the three. Both teams are sliding, but Vanderbilt's slide has more holes in it. The Commodores have lost five in a row, giving up 21, 38, 52, 31 and 34 along the way, and Curtis has 8 interceptions to go with his 8 touchdown throws. Mississippi State's offense has gone quiet over the last month, with 0 at LSU and 3 at Texas, and Kamario Taylor has not been the Bulldog with the most throws in any of the last three games. Still, the Bulldogs scored 62, 38, 41 and 31 when they had their footing in September, and this is the softest defense they have seen since then.

The risk is plain. If the quarterback spot stays unsettled, a 15-23 day like the one against Oklahoma is on the table, and Vanderbilt has enough throwing game to sneak out of town. DraftKings opened Mississippi State −3 and it has not moved.

display.fanatic_story:
Vanderbilt vs Mississippi State prediction for Homecoming in Starkville: the cowbells come out Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium at 4:15 PM ET, and the whole town has been told what to wear. Maroon. Head to toe, if you can manage it, because Mississippi State has spent Homecoming week reminding everybody that There's No Place Like State.

I asked two people who see this one from opposite porches to walk me through it.

Pippa Ashcroft studies economics in Nashville and hums country hooks under her breath when she is nervous. She was humming before I finished saying hello. Wade Pettus has a poultry-science degree from Mississippi State and keeps the Bulldogs' throwing game charted on feed-store receipts, folded into a stack in his shirt pocket.

"Y'all have the theme down," Pippa said. "No place like State. I'll give you that. It's the only place in the league where I can hear my own heartbeat over a cowbell."

Wade grinned. "That's the point. Homecoming week ran from the first of the month through the eighth. Friday night the Diamond Dawg Classic is out at Dudy Noble Field, with Will Clark and Rafael Palmeiro managing. Then the True Maroon Trek. Breakfast with Royalty had chicken biscuits. We do the week right."

"Chicken biscuits," Pippa said. "You would bring up chickens."

He shrugged. "Professional pride."

Here is where the two of them landed on football, and it is a matchup of two teams trying to remember how September felt.

Vanderbilt won its first three, then lost five in a row. The Commodores are 3-5 and 0-5 in league play, scoring 22.8 points a game and giving up 30.2. The losses read Auburn 15-21, Georgia 14-38, Ole Miss 17-52, Arkansas 21-31 and Kentucky 17-34.

"The Auburn game still hurts," Pippa said. "Six points. Then Georgia, then the Ole Miss game I won't talk about. But look at Jared Curtis at Kentucky. Twenty-seven of thirty-six for 247 and two touchdowns. He is figuring it out."

Curtis has 1,489 yards this year with 8 touchdowns and 8 interceptions, and that even split is the whole Vanderbilt story in one stat. Junior Sherrill is the reason the throwing game works at all, with 706 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns, and he had 8 catches for 78 at Kentucky. Sedrick Alexander leads the rushing with 274 yards and 5 scores. On defense, CJ Heard has 60 tackles and Nick Rinaldi has 3.5 sacks.

Wade pulled out a receipt. "Now mine. We were 4-0. Beat UL Monroe 62-13, won at Minnesota, won at South Carolina 41-34, beat Missouri 31-24. Kamario Taylor was throwing it all over the yard."

"And then?" Pippa asked, sweetly.

"And then Alabama, 23-56. LSU, 0-31. Oklahoma, 15-23. Texas, 3-31." He folded the receipt back up. "Rough month."

Mississippi State is 4-4, scoring 26.6 and allowing 28.1. Taylor has 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns and only 4 interceptions, but Parker Puckett took the most throws at LSU and against Oklahoma, and AJ Swann did at Texas, going 12 of 15 for 97. Fluff Bothwell has 563 rushing yards, Anthony Evans III has 666 receiving yards, Tyler Lockhart has 48 tackles and Jaray Bledsoe has 3.5 sacks.

"So who is your quarterback Saturday?" Pippa asked.

"Whoever it is, he gets to throw against a defense that gave up 52 to Ole Miss," Wade said. "That changes the whole night. The last month we played four ranked-looking giants. Vanderbilt is a different kind of Saturday."

Pippa sang a verse of something about a dirt road and a broken heart. Then she said, "Your last two in this series were 24-17 and 45-6. I know. I looked it up so you wouldn't get to tell me."

"I was going to tell you anyway."

The way I see it, the game turns on whether Mississippi State's offense wakes up in front of its own people. Four straight weeks against Alabama, LSU, Oklahoma and Texas would flatten anybody. Vanderbilt's defense is the softest group the Bulldogs have faced since September, and a Homecoming crowd in maroon is going to be loud from the opening kick.

Vanderbilt can score enough to keep it honest. Curtis and Sherrill will make plays. But the Commodores have not stopped anybody in five weeks, and I don't see that changing in Starkville with the cowbells going.

Pippa said she would hum the Commodores home on the drive back up the Natchez Trace whatever happens. Wade said he would save her a chicken biscuit.

My call: Mississippi State Bulldogs 32, Vanderbilt Commodores 23.

Rutgers vs Wisconsin prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Heroes Day at Camp Randall: Wisconsin opens its doors to veterans at 4:15 PM ET in Madison, and the Badgers are laying a big number to a Rutgers team that just played Michigan to a touchdown. My side is Rutgers Scarlet Knights +17.5, my call on points is Over 45.5, and my score is Wisconsin Badgers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 18.

Vinny Scolari drove in from Exit 9 and grades trenches the way he grades boardwalk arm-wrestlers, by who blinks first. "Seventeen and a half? We just lost 21-28 to Michigan. We won 37-30 at Maryland. KJ Duff has 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Nobody blinks first here."

Lars 'Brat' Ellefson played fullback for the Badgers and still wears the cheese wedge to every home game. "Wisconsin gives up 17.1 a game. We went to Happy Valley and won 24-20. We beat USC 24-7. And we've won the last four of these, 31-17, 52-3, 24-13 and 42-7."

Both of them have a point, and that is why I want the points. Wisconsin's offense has been a sometime thing. The Badgers were shut out 0-30 at Iowa and scored 7 at UCLA, and Colton Joseph has thrown for 66, 58 and 90 yards in three of his last four games. He leads the team in both throwing yards at 1,346 and rushing at 371. That is a defense-first team that wins 24-20 and 24-7, not one that wins by three scores every week.

Rutgers has warts. The Scarlet Knights give up 32.6 a game and lost 15-47 to Indiana and 14-42 at Northwestern. But they score 27.8, Antwan Raymond has 733 rushing yards, and Duff can flip a game on one catch. Against Michigan, AJ Surace hit only 3 of 12 throws and they still had a chance late.

On points, my 33 and 18 add to 51, past 45.5. Wisconsin's scoring defense is the reason the Over is not easy, but Rutgers has allowed 28 or more in seven of its eight games, and the Badgers have hit 31 or more three times.

The room is in agreement on the side. The Formula has Wisconsin 32-19, takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes the Over. Next Man Up has Wisconsin 34-17, takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches takes Rutgers +17.5 and likes it, and it reads sides only with no score this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Vinny says Jersey guys do not need three touchdowns of cushion, just three hours of stubborn. Brat says the cheese wedge has seen worse.

display.fanatic_story:
Rutgers vs Wisconsin prediction for Heroes Day at Camp Randall: Saturday at 4:15 PM ET, Madison turns its home game into a salute to veterans, and Rutgers walks into the middle of it carrying a long trip and a short memory of last week.

Camp Randall carries that weight well. There is a free Salute to Veterans Tailgate at Camp Randall Memorial Park, with replica gear on loan from the Wisconsin Veterans Museum, and the new Camp Randall Veterans Memorial Plaza is open for people to walk through before kickoff.

I sat down with two guys who could not be more different if they tried.

Vinny Scolari is from off Exit 9 of the Turnpike. He grades blockers the way he grades arm-wrestling on the boardwalk, by watching who blinks. Lars Ellefson, who everybody calls Brat, played fullback for the Badgers and owns a foam cheese wedge older than some of the current roster.

"Heroes Day is a good day," Vinny said. "My uncle did twenty years. I'll be at the tailgate looking at the old helmets. Then I'll be in the stands looking at us get no respect."

Brat laughed. "You get respect. You just don't get wins in Madison. Four meetings, four Wisconsin wins. 31-17, 52-3, 24-13, 42-7."

"Fifty-two to three was 2021. Different guys."

That is true. This Rutgers team is 2-6, and it is a strange 2-6. The Scarlet Knights score 27.8 points a game and allow 32.6. They lost 21-37 to UMass, which hurts to type, and 21-28 at Boston College. Then they gave USC everything in a 35-42 loss, beat Howard 58-7, got run over 15-47 by Indiana, won 37-30 at Maryland, lost 14-42 at Northwestern and then played Michigan close in a 21-28 loss last Saturday.

"The Michigan game is the one," Vinny said. "AJ Surace went 3 for 12 and we still almost had it. Jourdin Houston caught one ball and took it 80 yards for a score. That's Jersey. One shot."

Dylan Lonergan leads the team with 1,066 throwing yards and 10 touchdowns, and Surace has taken the most throws in three of the last four games. Antwan Raymond is the workhorse with 733 rushing yards and 6 scores, and he ran for 85 against Michigan. KJ Duff is the guy you build the night around, with 774 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns. Sekou Kromah has 3 sacks and Chris Joines leads with 41 tackles.

Brat had his own list. "Wisconsin is 5-3. We give up 17.1 a game. We won 24-20 at Penn State. We beat USC 24-7. We beat Michigan State 31-3."

"And Iowa?" Vinny asked.

Brat looked at the cheese wedge for a while. "Zero to thirty. We don't discuss it."

The Badgers score 23.6 a game, which tells you everything about how they win. Colton Joseph is the whole offense. He has 1,346 throwing yards and 11 touchdowns, and he is also the leading rusher at 371 yards. Tyrell Henry is the top receiver at 397. The defense is the real show, with Cooper Catalano at 75 tackles and Sebastian Cheeks at 6 sacks.

"Here's my problem," Vinny said. "Joseph threw for 66 at UCLA and 58 against USC and 90 at Iowa. You can't throw it? We'll put nine guys in the box and make you."

"We beat USC throwing for 58," Brat said. "That's the Wisconsin way. Run it, hit you, run it again."

I asked them about the veterans plaza. Both of them got quiet. Brat said he walked through it on a weeknight and stayed longer than he planned. Vinny said his uncle would have liked the replica gear more than the football.

So here is how I see the game. Wisconsin's defense should win the day. Rutgers has allowed 28 or more in seven of eight games, and the Badgers at home on a big emotional Saturday will be ready. But the Wisconsin offense does not blow anyone out unless the other side hands it over. Raymond will move the chains some, Duff will get a couple of shots, and Rutgers will score enough to make the fourth quarter mean something.

Vinny promised to stay for the whole thing. Brat promised to lend him a cheese wedge if it gets cold.

My call: Wisconsin Badgers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 18.

South Alabama vs Louisiana prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Saturday at Cajun Field: Louisiana Salutes night in Lafayette kicks off at 5:00 PM ET, and the Ragin' Cajuns are laying more than a touchdown to a South Alabama team that has a habit of leaving this building happy. My side is South Alabama Jaguars +9.5, my call on points is Over 58.5, and my score is Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 35, South Alabama Jaguars 26.

Azalea Fairhope-Grice builds Mardi Gras floats in Mobile and coached volleyball long enough to know a team that is about to crack. "We won 24-22 the last time we came to Lafayette, and 20-17 the time before. Nine and a half is a lot of float to push uphill."

Amélie 'Mimi' Fontenot keeps the books for half the dance halls in Acadiana and two-steps when she is right. "Honey, no. We won 31-22 last year, and this series since 2016 is 8 to 2 for us. Lunch Winfield has 470 rushing yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. You do not stop that man in our house."

Here is why I take the points. South Alabama scores 33.2 a game, and it has put up 52 on UL Monroe and 56 at Arkansas State. Keenan Phillips has 576 rushing yards and 6 touchdowns, and Jared Hollins has 1,195 throwing yards with only 4 interceptions. The Jaguars have lost two in a row, 13-20 at Marshall and 20-35 to Louisiana Tech, but even the bad nights have not been blowouts outside the 21-45 trip to Kentucky.

Louisiana is 5-3 and better on defense, allowing 21.2 a game. The Cajuns score 30.1 and beat Troy 33-6 and Charlotte 34-7. But their three losses came 30-49 at USC, 31-32 at Louisiana Tech and 31-35 at Southern Miss, and their wins over UAB and Arkansas State were 21-14 and 23-20. This is not a team that buries people.

The Over is the cleaner half for me. South Alabama allows 32.8 a game, and the 2018 meeting in this series ended 48-38. My 35 and 26 make 61, past 58.5.

The room is split on the side. The Formula has Louisiana 34-25, with South Alabama +9.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has Louisiana 36-26, sides with the Cajuns −9.5 and likes the Over. Azalea says she has seen floats tip and keep rolling. Mimi says the band will be playing in Lafayette long after the Jaguars head home.

South Alabama vs Louisiana prediction for Louisiana Salutes night in Lafayette: the Ragin' Cajuns honor military members, veterans and first responders at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, with a 5:00 PM ET kickoff, and South Alabama shows up as the one visitor in the league that seems to like it here.

The Jaguars have won their last two trips to Lafayette. They won 24-22 in 2024, and in 2022 they won 20-17 on a field goal at the very end. That is the part Mobile people bring up first. The part they bring up second, if you push, is that they are 2-5 all time at Cajun Field. Saturday is the 15th meeting between the two.

I got the two sides together on a phone call that ran long.

Azalea Fairhope-Grice builds Mardi Gras floats in Mobile and used to coach high school volleyball, which means she can spot a rotation breaking down from the cheap seats. Amélie Fontenot, Mimi to everyone, is an accountant in Lafayette who will tell you about zydeco whether you asked or not, and then she will show you the steps.

"I want to talk about 2022," Azalea said before I could ask anything.

"Of course you do," Mimi said. "One kick. Everybody in Mobile has it framed."

"We have two, actually. 2024 too. 24-22."

"And last year we won 31-22 and nobody in Mobile mentions it."

They are both right, and that is the fun of this one. Over the ten meetings from 2016 to 2025, Louisiana won eight and South Alabama won two. But the Jaguars' two came in the last four years, and both came in this building.

This South Alabama team is 4-4 and plays wide open. The Jaguars score 33.2 a game and allow 32.8. They beat Ohio 41-36, beat UL Monroe 52-35 and won a 56-49 shootout at Arkansas State. Then the month went sideways, with a 13-20 loss at Marshall and a 20-35 loss to Louisiana Tech last Saturday.

"The Marshall game was a volleyball match where nobody could serve," Azalea said. "Jared Hollins went 12 for 33. That is not him."

Hollins has 1,195 throwing yards with 9 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Keenan Phillips is the lead back with 576 yards and 6 scores, Brendan Jenkins leads the receivers at 451 yards, and Cole Blaylock leads the defense with 46 tackles. Against Louisiana Tech, Anthony Eager caught 7 balls for 102 yards and 2 touchdowns, so there are weapons.

Mimi waited politely and then went to work. "Lunch Winfield."

That is the whole Louisiana argument in two words. Winfield has thrown for 1,452 yards and leads the team on the ground with 470 yards and 9 rushing touchdowns. The Cajuns are 5-3, scoring 30.1 a game and allowing just 21.2, with Jake St. Andre at 60 tackles.

"We lost by one at Louisiana Tech, 31-32," Mimi said. "We lost 31-35 at Southern Miss. Close ones. At home we beat Troy 33-6 and Arkansas State 23-20. Home is home."

"Home is also where you lost to us twice," Azalea said.

Mimi did a little two-step in her kitchen. I could hear it over the phone.

What about the salute? Both of them liked it. Azalea's father was a firefighter in Mobile, and she said a night that honors first responders hits her harder than any rivalry. Mimi said Lafayette does these nights right, with the crowd on its feet for every service member they bring onto the field.

Here is how I see the game. Louisiana's defense is the better group on the field, and Winfield is the best player in it. At home, with the crowd up for Louisiana Salutes, the Cajuns should take control by the third quarter. But South Alabama scores too much to go away. Phillips will find room, Hollins will hit enough shots, and the Jaguars will keep it a two-score game into the fourth.

Azalea says she has seen floats lose a wheel and still finish the parade. Mimi says she will be dancing on the way out either way.

My call: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 35, South Alabama Jaguars 26.

display.fanatic_story:
Boise State vs Colorado State prediction for Saturday at Canvas Stadium: the Broncos bring a sea of blue to Fort Collins for a 6:00 PM ET kickoff, and the Rams get one more chance to prove their best night this season was not a fluke.

Boise State's schedule card for this road game says it in two words: Wear Blue. The Boise State alumni association is running a free Bronco Bash on South College Avenue before kickoff, from 3 to 5:30 PM ET, with music, game day swag and a drawing for a football signed by Coach Danielson for those who registered by Nov. 3. Colorado State, for its part, lists tailgating on the game page, and the parking office has event hours running all day out of the lots on West Pitkin Street.

I found two people to argue it out.

Thatcher Bluestem is from the Treasure Valley and has blue in every shade. Blue jacket, blue hat, blue socks. He says the blue turf is a lifestyle. Ansel Rimrock lives in Fort Collins and runs trails before work, which might explain why nothing seems to bother him.

"You know what I like about this trip?" Thatcher said. "We've been coming here forever and we've won almost every time. Eight of nine since 2016."

"The one we won was 31-30 in 2023," Ansel said. "I was there. I ran home."

"You ran home?"

"It was a good night. I had energy."

The series tilts hard to Boise, and last year's game was a 49-21 Broncos win. But this Colorado State team is a strange, fun mess. The Rams are 3-5 and score 35.5 points a game while allowing 42.4. They opened with a 35-13 win over Wyoming and a 58-24 win over Southern Utah. Then came four straight losses, including 45-59 at UTSA, 26-56 to Oregon State and 27-66 at Texas State. Then they turned around and beat San Diego State 56-49.

"That San Diego State game," Ansel said. "Hauss Hejny went 24 of 31 for 333 and 3 touchdowns. When he plays, we are a different team."

Hejny has 1,138 yards with 14 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions, and when he has taken the most throws the Rams have scored 35, 58, 56 and 14. Mel Brown leads the rushers with 454 yards, RJ Vick leads the receivers with 425, and Oumar Diomande is all over the field with 76 tackles.

"And the 14?" Thatcher asked.

"Utah State. Cold night. We don't talk about it."

Thatcher's turn. Boise State is 7-1 and ranked 20th. The Broncos score 35.9 a game and allow 23.6. The only loss was the opener, 27-34 at Oregon, and since then it has been seven wins in a row.

"Maddux Madsen has thrown 1 interception all year," Thatcher said. "One. In eight games. He has 1,681 yards and 15 touchdowns. And Dylan Riley has 1,049 rushing yards."

Riley has 9 rushing touchdowns, Rasean Jones leads the receivers with 554 yards, and Boen Phelps has 49 tackles. Jones had a monster night against Texas State last week with 9 catches for 117 yards and 3 touchdowns.

"About that Texas State game," Ansel said gently. "46-45."

Thatcher shrugged. "A win is a win."

"Texas State put 66 on us. They put 45 on you. That's not nothing."

He has a point. Boise won that one by one at home. The defense that gave up 23.6 a game over the season gave up 45 in a single afternoon. That is the opening Colorado State needs.

I asked Ansel what Fort Collins does on a game Saturday. He said the town walks to the stadium, the tailgates go all day, and the mountains sit right there to the west watching. Thatcher said he would be the guy in blue in the middle of it, being friendly about it.

So here is how I see it. Boise State is the better team, and Riley is going to run for a lot of yards against a defense that has given up 41 or more five times. Madsen will not give the ball away. The Broncos should be in control by halftime. But Colorado State scores too much at home to get run out of its own building, and Hejny will keep hitting Vick and Brown in the second half. The Rams keep it to a little over two scores.

Ansel says he will run home either way. Thatcher says he will wave from the bus.

My call: Boise State Broncos 44, Colorado State Rams 28.

Kentucky vs Tennessee prediction, pick against the spread and over/under for Homecoming at Neyland Stadium: Knoxville has spent the week telling everybody All Roads Lead to Tennessee, and at 6:15 PM ET the road brings in a 7-1 Kentucky team ranked No. 8 against a 6-2 Tennessee team ranked No. 16. My side is Tennessee Volunteers −6.5, my call on points is Over 50.5, and my score is Tennessee Volunteers 30, Kentucky Wildcats 23.

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle grew up on a horse farm a short ride from Keeneland and reads a football game like a past-performance page. "Look at the form. Kentucky won two overtime races in a row, 35-34 at South Carolina and 35-34 over LSU, then went to Norman and won 21-13. Kenny Minchey has 1,755 yards, 14 touchdowns and 1 interception. That horse does not throw a shoe."

Earl 'Rocky Top' Haskew snapped for the Vols and tunes his banjo during commercials. "Form is fine. Class is different. We give up 16.2 a game. We held Alabama to 10. Tyree Weathersby has 7 sacks, and DeSean Bishop has 957 yards and 11 touchdowns. And we beat y'all 56-34 last year."

Rhett's past-performance read is honest, and so is the trouble in it. Kentucky's two overtime wins were by one point each, and the one time the Wildcats ran against a top-class field at home they lost 17-45 to Alabama. Tennessee's two losses came 17-20 to Texas and 24-27 at South Carolina. Nobody has handled the Vols by more than a field goal.

The Tennessee case is the defense and the ground game. Bishop ran 32 times for 120 at South Carolina, and the Vols have held Auburn to 14, Arkansas to 17 and Alabama to 10 in the last month and a half. George MacIntyre does not need to win this game with his arm, and he has 728 throwing yards. He needs to hand it off and avoid mistakes.

Kentucky can make that hard. Minchey's 1 interception all year is the reason the Wildcats have survived close finishes. Grant Godfrey has 72 tackles and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace has 5 sacks. If the Vols fall behind early, this is a closer race than I think.

On points, the series has gone big lately, with 56-34 last year and 45-42 in 2021. Kentucky scores 32.9 and Tennessee scores 32.2. My 30 and 23 make 53, past 50.5.

The room splits on the side but not on points. The Formula has Tennessee 29-24, sides with Kentucky +6.5 and likes the Over. Rhett says his horse has the cleaner form. Earl says Neyland is a longer track than it looks.

display.fanatic_story:
Kentucky vs Tennessee prediction for Homecoming in Knoxville: the theme this year is All Roads Lead to Tennessee, and on Saturday at 6:15 PM ET the road from Lexington ends at Neyland Stadium, where the Vols will be wearing their Dark Mode uniforms and the whole place will be loud.

Homecoming week has been busy. Monica Abbott is the grand marshal. The parade steps off Friday afternoon at 4 p.m. on Volunteer Boulevard and finishes at Neyland. The Europa and the Bull fountain on campus has been dyed orange, and there is Smokey's Howl on the schedule too. If you are a Kentucky fan, you are walking into an orange wall.

I got two old hands to talk it over.

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle grew up on a horse farm outside Lexington and still talks about football like a horseman sizing up a yearling. Earl Haskew, who everyone calls Rocky Top, was a long snapper for the Vols and brings a banjo to every tailgate he can find.

"Here's the thing nobody in Knoxville wants to hear," Rhett said. "We're 7-1. We're the better team on paper."

Earl plucked a string. "Paper doesn't play in Neyland."

Kentucky has been a story all fall. The Wildcats are 7-1, scoring 32.9 points a game and allowing 24.8. The only loss was 17-45 to Alabama back in September. Since then, it has been one escape after another. They won 35-34 in overtime at South Carolina, then 35-34 in overtime against LSU the next week. Then they went to Oklahoma and won 21-13, and beat Vanderbilt 34-17.

"Kenny Minchey has thrown one interception all year," Rhett said. "One. He has 1,755 yards and 14 touchdowns. He doesn't panic."

That is the heart of the Kentucky case. CJ Baxter leads the rushers with 487 yards and 8 touchdowns, Kenny Darby is the top receiver at 507 yards, Grant Godfrey has 72 tackles and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace has 5 sacks.

Earl put the banjo down for this part. "Tennessee is 6-2. We give up 16.2 a game. We held Alabama to 10 points at home. We lost to Texas by three and at South Carolina by three. That's it."

He's right about that. The two Tennessee losses were 17-20 to Texas and 24-27 at South Carolina. The Vols score 32.2 a game. DeSean Bishop is the engine, with 957 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, and he carried 32 times for 120 yards at South Carolina. Mike Matthews leads the receivers with 528. On defense, Tyree Weathersby has 7 sacks and Amare Campbell has 52 tackles.

"What about the quarterback?" Rhett asked.

George MacIntyre has taken over the throwing, with 728 yards. Faizon Brandon took the most throws in the first four games and MacIntyre has done it since.

"George doesn't need to be a hero," Earl said. "Hand it to Bishop. Let the defense work. That's how we beat Alabama 26-10."

Rhett had one more card to play. "Two overtime wins. You know what that tells me? We don't lose close games."

"You know what it tells me?" Earl said. "You're lucky."

Then there is the history, which Earl was happy to bring up. Over the ten meetings from 2016 to 2025, Tennessee won eight and Kentucky won two. Last year it was 56-34 for the Vols. In 2021 it was 45-42.

"2020," Rhett said. "34-7. I remember that one."

"Everybody remembers the one they won," Earl said, and started playing Rocky Top on the banjo.

So here is how I see it. Kentucky has the better season, and Minchey is not going to give the game away. But Tennessee at home, on Homecoming, in Dark Mode, with Bishop running behind that front, is a different animal. The Vols defense has not given up more than 27 all year. The Wildcats will move the ball some and Minchey will make a few big throws. But late in the game, Bishop carries it, the crowd sings, and Tennessee pulls away by a touchdown.

Rhett says Kentucky has earned some respect. Earl says Neyland hands it out one Saturday at a time.

My call: Tennessee Volunteers 30, Kentucky Wildcats 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Sam Houston vs Jacksonville State prediction for Homecoming in Jacksonville, Alabama: the theme on campus is Cocky Reigns Supreme, the parade comes first, and then the Gamecocks take Burgess-Snow Field at AmFirst Stadium against Sam Houston at 7:00 PM ET.

Jax State calls itself The Friendliest Campus in the South, and Homecoming is when it tries hardest to prove it. There are tailgates and reunions all day, including the Golden Gamecocks Reunion for the old grads. During the game, the school will recognize its 2026 Alumni of the Year winners along with the Homecoming Queen, King and Court. Cocky, the mascot, gets top billing for once.

I brought in two people who know their regions.

Lem Coxwell teaches history in Walker County, Texas, and will tell you a tall tale about Sam Houston the man before he will tell you anything about Sam Houston the football team. Burl Ashcraft-Neeley cooks barbecue in Calhoun County, Alabama, and has opinions about pork shoulder that he shares freely.

"I'll be honest with you," Lem said. "It has been a long fall in Huntsville."

It has. The Bearkats are 1-7. They score 18.0 points a game and allow 25.1. The only win was 59-0 over Nicholls in September. But it hasn't been all blowouts. They lost 21-24 at Troy to open the year, 17-23 to Tulsa and 24-30 to New Mexico State.

"Then the offense went cold," Lem said. "Three points at Liberty. Three against Western Kentucky. Three at Missouri State. I have told some tall tales in my classroom, and none of them were as hard to explain as that."

Landyn Locke leads the throwing with 1,653 yards and 12 touchdowns, though DJ Bailey took the most throws at Missouri State and went 20 of 35 for 258. Tim Burns Jr. leads the receivers with 392 yards, and Alton McCaskill leads the ground game with 232. The defense has been the steady part. Dean Ford has 47 tackles and Josh Alexander-Felton has 4 sacks.

Burl had a rib in one hand and a list in the other. "We're 6-2. We give up 19.9 a game. And we just went to Las Cruces and shut out New Mexico State, 24-0."

Jacksonville State scores 26.9 a game and wins tight. After a 7-33 loss at North Dakota State and a 49-7 win over Eastern Kentucky, the Gamecocks lost 27-29 in overtime at Ohio. Then they won five straight, by scores of 31-27, 23-13, 27-26, 27-24 and 24-0.

"Caden Creel," Burl said. "That's the show. He has 1,741 throwing yards and 713 rushing. He's like a good smoker. Steady heat."

Deondre Johnson leads the receivers at 438 yards, and Caleb Nix leads the defense with 54 tackles.

Lem pointed out the history. "We beat them 42-7 in 2021."

"And we won the last three," Burl said. "35-28, 21-11 and 29-27."

"All close."

"All ours."

That back-and-forth is the game in a nutshell. Jax State wins, but it rarely runs away from anybody. Sam Houston's defense is good enough to keep things from getting silly, but the Bearkats have to find some points from somewhere.

I asked Burl about Homecoming. He said the parade goes through campus, the families set up early, and the smell of smoke hangs over the whole place by noon. Lem said he has never been, but he figures any town that names its stadium field after two people instead of one has a story worth hearing.

Here is how I see it. Jacksonville State on Homecoming, with Creel running and throwing, should control this from the second quarter on. The Gamecocks' defense is coming off a shutout, and the Bearkats have scored 3 points in three of their last four. But this Jax State team has not blown many people out, and Sam Houston's defense will make it work for every score. Creel gets his yards, the Gamecocks pull clear in the second half, and the Bearkats get a couple of late scores to make it look respectable.

Lem says he will have a new tall tale either way. Burl says the shoulder will be ready at halftime.

My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Sam Houston Bearkats 15.

display.fanatic_story:
Georgia vs Ole Miss prediction for Saturday night in Oxford: the Rebels and Bulldogs meet at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium at 7:30 PM ET, and Ole Miss has already turned the whole week into a contest. It is called Beat Week, and it runs from Monday, Nov. 2, through Saturday, Nov. 7.

Here is how it works. Ole Miss and Georgia are racing to see which school can collect the most charitable gifts before kickoff. Every gift of $5 or more counts as one point, no matter the size, so a $5 gift counts the same as a $5,000 one. Georgia has the bigger alumni base, so Ole Miss is asking every fan to make three gifts to three things they love about the place, maybe a school, a scholarship and the Pride of the South Marching Band. Three gifts, three points. The school even pointed out that the Rebels beat Georgia in the Sugar Bowl in January and would like a second win over the Bulldogs this year.

I talked it through with two people who see this game in very different light.

Thad Okafor-Brandt is a DJ on a college station who plays indie records nobody else has heard of and spends his off nights watching defensive film. Langston Fairbanks lives in Oxford, wears seersucker well past the season for it and will quote Faulkner at you whether or not you have asked.

"I already made my three gifts," Langston said. "School of Law, a scholarship and the band. That's three points."

"That's very Oxford of you," Thad said.

"Faulkner said the past is never dead. It's not even past. That is this series."

He is not wrong. The last four meetings have swung back and forth. Ole Miss won 45-14 in 2016 and 28-10 in 2024. Georgia won 52-17 in 2023 and 43-35 last year.

Georgia comes in at 7-1 and ranked second in the country. The Bulldogs score 41.0 points a game and allow just 14.9. They beat Oklahoma 41-13, won 20-17 at Alabama and beat Florida 27-8 last Saturday. The one loss was 24-27 to Auburn.

"Watch the Georgia defense on film," Thad said. "It's like a perfect record with one scratch. Auburn found the scratch. Alabama almost did."

Gunner Stockton has 1,671 yards, 16 touchdowns and 4 interceptions, though he threw for only 101 against Florida. Dwight Phillips Jr. leads the rushers with 415 yards, Craig Dandridge leads the receivers with 349, and Raylen Wilson leads the defense in both tackles, with 51, and sacks, with 4.

Ole Miss is 6-2 and ranked 12th, scoring 37.1 a game and allowing 24.0. The Rebels opened by beating Louisville 41-38, then beat LSU 32-24 at home. They lost 28-52 at Florida and 27-34 at Texas. But at home they have been very good, beating Missouri 31-3 and Auburn 45-15 last week.

"Trinidad Chambliss is the whole thing," Langston said. "He has 2,189 yards and 18 touchdowns. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. When the Grove is full and the sun goes down, this place is a different stadium."

"Chambliss also has 8 interceptions," Thad said. "Three at Texas. Georgia's defense eats that up."

That's the matchup. Ole Miss throws it all over the place, and Georgia's defense is the best it has seen. The Rebels also have a defense with some bite, with Blake Purchase at 4.5 sacks and Keaton Thomas at 52 tackles.

I asked them both how they want Saturday to feel. Thad said he wants a game he can play back like a great record. Langston said he wants the Hotty Toddy to ring out under the lights at the end of the fourth quarter, with the Beat Week scoreboard settled too.

Here is how I see it. Georgia is the better team on paper, with the better defense and more depth. But this is a night game in Oxford, and Ole Miss has been very good at home. Chambliss will make big plays and a couple of mistakes. Stockton will be careful and get it done late. It comes down to one drive, and Georgia has the last one.

Thad says he will play the deep cuts all the way home. Langston says the ending will be long and close, like a Faulkner sentence.

My call: Georgia Bulldogs 31, Ole Miss Rebels 30.

Moss Feldstein studies physics in Boulder and does his best thinking in a hammock under the Flatirons. "Momentum is real. We beat Kansas State 27-24 in overtime, and Richard Young ran 24 times for 120 and 2 touchdowns. Joseph Williams has 732 receiving yards. We are finally moving."

Skylar Vanterpool is finishing a sports-science master's in Tempe and measures everything. "Measure this. You score 21.0 a game. We beat that same Kansas State team 28-17. Reed Harris has 804 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns, and Cardae Mack has 523 rushing yards. We won 42-17 last year."

The day begins with Sparky's Touchdown Tailgate at College Avenue and 6th Street, the free pregame party ASU throws before every home game. It opens 2.5 hours before kickoff, with games and live entertainment for the whole family. This week it doubles as a thank-you to service members, and it should be packed with parents in maroon and gold visiting their kids for the weekend.

I sat down with two people who could not be more different.

"I'm coming in hot," Moss said. "We just beat Kansas State in overtime. Momentum is a physical quantity. Look it up."

"I measure things for a living," Skylar said. "Your momentum is one game."

Colorado is 3-5. The Buffaloes score 21.0 points a game and allow 29.4. They won 14-13 at Georgia Tech to open the year and beat Weber State 52-21. Then came five losses in a row: 7-41 at Northwestern, 13-23 at Baylor, 7-29 to Texas Tech, 24-27 to Utah and 24-57 at Oklahoma State. Then the 27-24 overtime win over Kansas State.

"Richard Young ran 24 times for 120 yards and 2 touchdowns against K-State," Moss said. "That is a young man finding his orbit."

Isaac Wilson has handled the throwing since late September, with 1,164 yards, 7 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Joseph Williams is the go-to target with 732 receiving yards and 5 scores. On defense, Lamont Lester Jr. has 5 sacks, and Gideon Lampron leads the team with 81 tackles.

Skylar clicked the stopwatch. "Arizona State is 4-4. We score 29.5 and allow 29.5. Perfectly balanced, which I appreciate."

The Sun Devils have been up and down. They crushed Morgan State 70-7, lost 20-48 at Texas A&M, beat Kansas 24-17, lost 19-55 to Baylor, beat Hawai'i 30-12, lost 25-53 at Texas Tech, beat Kansas State 28-17 and lost 20-27 at BYU last week.

"Win, lose, win, lose," Moss said. "You're a sine wave."

"And this is a win week," Skylar said.

Cutter Boley leads the team with 1,360 throwing yards and 13 touchdowns, though Mikey Keene and Jake Fette have taken the most throws in the last three games. Reed Harris is the headliner with 804 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns. Cardae Mack leads the ground game with 523 yards, and Owen Long has 72 tackles.

Then there is the history, which is about as even as it gets. Over the eight meetings since 2016, each side has won four. Colorado won 27-24 in 2023. Arizona State won 42-17 last year.

"Forty-two to seventeen," Skylar said. "I timed the drive home. It felt short."

"That was a different team," Moss said. "We have Joseph Williams now."

I asked both of them about the weekend. Skylar said the family is flying in for Family Weekend, and the first stop is the tailgate. Moss said Boulder fans travel well to Tempe in November because nobody wants to miss a warm night.

Here is how I see it. Both defenses give up a lot, and both teams are capable of a big play on any snap. Colorado has real momentum, and Young gives the Buffaloes a ground game they did not have a month ago. But the Sun Devils at home, on a family night with the crowd behind them, have been a different team. Harris will make a couple of big catches, Mack will grind out the tough yards, and Arizona State pulls away late by a score.

Moss says momentum is conserved. Skylar says she has the stopwatch to prove otherwise.

My call: Arizona State Sun Devils 30, Colorado Buffaloes 24.

Louisville vs Georgia Tech prediction for Dodd After Dark: Georgia Tech is turning Saturday night into an event at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field, with a 7:30 PM ET kickoff, a halftime fireworks show presented by Georgia Power and the school's annual Military Appreciation Day all wrapped into one.

The Jackets are pulling out the stops for this one. Remaining tickets were marked down to half price, and there is a Buy One, Give One offer so fans can send local military personnel and veterans to the game. A wide range of events is planned to thank people who served. And then, at halftime, the sky over Midtown lights up.

I found two people to give me both sides.

Bianca Thornberry hosts a Kentucky Derby party every May in Louisville that people plan their springs around. She talks about football the way she talks about seating charts. Wendell Quist has an aerospace engineering degree from Georgia Tech and spends his free time tracking punt trajectories, which he will show you on his phone if you let him.

"I love a night game," Bianca said. "And I love fireworks. Georgia Tech is throwing a party, and Louisville is bringing the guests."

"That's generous," Wendell said. "Most guests don't score 52."

Louisville is 5-3 and the offense has been a joy to watch. The Cardinals score 40.4 points a game. They beat Villanova 59-13, SMU 41-31, Florida State 44-20, Syracuse 34-26 and Stanford 52-24 last week. But all three losses were heartbreakers: 38-41 to Ole Miss, 27-30 to Wake Forest and 28-31 at NC State.

"Every one of those was a coin flip," Bianca said. "That's the part that makes me crazy. We could be 8-0."

Lincoln Kienholz has 2,094 throwing yards, 12 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. Isaac Brown ran 9 times for 139 yards and 3 touchdowns against Stanford and has 707 rushing yards on the year. Tre Richardson leads the receivers with 633, and he caught 10 balls for 140 last week. On defense, Tyler Thompson has 5.5 sacks and T.J. Capers has 57 tackles.

Wendell pulled up his phone. "Our side of it is harder. We're 2-6."

Georgia Tech scores 24.8 a game and allows 30.8. The losses include a 13-14 heartbreaker to Colorado to open the year, 24-45 to Tennessee, 27-34 at Stanford, 24-34 at Virginia Tech, 27-49 to Boston College and 11-34 at Pitt last Saturday. The wins came over Mercer and Duke, 44-11 and 28-25.

"Alberto Mendoza threw for 81 at Pitt," Wendell said. "That's a bad trajectory. But he has 1,795 yards on the year. Justice Haynes has 548 rushing yards. Jordan Allen has 543 receiving."

Tae Harris leads the Tech defense with 50 tackles, and Noah Carter has 3 sacks.

The history is a fun one. The four meetings are split two and two. Georgia Tech won 66-31 in 2018 and 46-27 in 2020. Louisville won 39-34 in 2023 and 31-19 in 2024.

"Sixty-six," Wendell said. "I think about it often."

"I don't," Bianca said.

I asked them both about the night itself. Wendell said he has done the math on the fireworks and is pretty sure the Georgia Power folks know what they are doing. Bianca said any night with fireworks and a crowd honoring veterans is a good night, even if her team is in the other jersey. Both said they will stand for the military salute.

So here is how I see it. Louisville has the better offense, and Brown and Kienholz are going to find room against a Tech defense that has given up 34 or more in five games. But this Louisville team has not run away from many good teams, and the Cardinals defense gives up 27.0 a game. Georgia Tech at home under the lights, with a crowd that showed up for the fireworks, will make some plays. Mendoza and Haynes get the Jackets into the twenties. The Cardinals pull away late.

Bianca says every good party runs long. Wendell says he will be watching the fireworks trajectories at halftime no matter what the scoreboard says.

My call: Louisville Cardinals 38, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 25.

Miami vs Notre Dame prediction for Saturday night in South Bend: the Hurricanes, 8-0 and rolling, walk into Notre Dame Stadium at 7:30 PM ET against a 7-1 Irish team that has been waiting for this one since the summer of 2025.

Game day on campus has its rituals, and they start early. At 5:15 PM ET the team leaves the Basilica of the Sacred Heart for the Victory March, with the Band of the Fighting Irish playing along the route and the Notre Dame Bagpipe Band leading the players into the stadium. At 5:30 the Trumpets at the Dome play outside the Main Building, and the Glee Club sings on Library Quad. At 6:00 the band plays its Concert on the Steps of Bond Hall, and the gates open, 90 minutes before kickoff. Later the band marches out to the stadium from the Main Building.

I talked it over with two very different people.

Javi Castillo, who everybody calls The Breeze, played defensive back at The U and still dresses like it is always July in Coral Gables, all linen and sunglasses. He moves between English and Spanish depending on how excited he is. Declan Moriarty-Chen is a grad student at Notre Dame who wears a sweater vest every single day and can tell you the schedule from any season you name.

"Oye, I love this place," Javi said. "The bagpipes, the band. Very classy. And then we beat you."

"You beat us last year," Declan said. "27-24. In Miami. This is our house."

That 2025 game is still sitting with both of them. Miami won it 27-24, and the series before that had a 30-27 Notre Dame win in 2016 and a 41-8 Miami win in 2017. Miami has two of the last three.

Miami is unbeaten for a reason. The Canes score 47.6 points a game and allow 17.8. They won 45-6 at Stanford, 77-7 over Florida A&M, 41-13 at Clemson and 52-23 over Pitt. The last few have been closer, a 43-35 overtime win over Florida State and a 38-35 win at North Carolina last week.

"Darian Mensah," Javi said, taking off his sunglasses for emphasis. "2,425 yards. 25 touchdowns. One interception. Uno."

Malachi Toney has 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns, including 2 scores at North Carolina. Javian Mallory leads the rushers with 495. On defense, Marquise Lightfoot has 7 sacks and Mohamed Toure has 44 tackles.

Declan was ready. "Notre Dame is 7-1. We score 40.4 a game and allow 13.4. The only loss was 24-28 at BYU."

The Irish have been close to perfect otherwise. They beat Wisconsin 41-13, Rice 52-0, Purdue 49-10, Stanford 58-7 and Navy 35-13 last week. CJ Carr has 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns and 1 interception.

"Both quarterbacks have one interception," Declan said. "Somebody has to make the second one Saturday."

Nolan James Jr. leads the Irish ground game with 519 yards and 8 touchdowns. Jordan Faison is the top receiver at 497. Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks and Drayk Bowen has 45 tackles. Jerome Bettis Jr. had 78 receiving yards against Navy, which made Declan very happy.

"Florida State put 35 on you," Declan said. "North Carolina put 35 on you."

"And we still won," Javi said. "Así es."

I asked them about the night. Declan said the Victory March is the best part of any game day, and that walking behind the bagpipes with the crowd along the route makes the hair on his arms stand up. Javi said he would be there too, just to see it, even in the other team's colors. Then he said he was going to need a much warmer jacket than he brought.

Here is how I see it. Miami's offense is the best Notre Dame has seen, and Mensah is going to make his plays. But the Hurricanes defense has bent in the last three weeks, and the Irish at home at night, with James running behind that front and Carr protecting the ball, are a tough out. Notre Dame grinds out a couple of long drives in the second half, Miami answers with big plays, and the Irish hang on in the fourth quarter.

display.fanatic_story:
Michigan State vs Michigan prediction for Saturday night in Ann Arbor: the Spartans walk into a sold-out Michigan Stadium at 2-6, the Wolverines sit at 5-3, and Shay Kowalczyk says that just means Michigan has more to lose. Gus Hartwell says that is the kind of thing people say on the drive down from East Lansing.

Kickoff is 7:30 p.m. ET, and this is the fifth straight night game in the series. Michigan has made it a Blue Out and Military Appreciation Game. Fans are asked to wear blue. Big flags for the six military branches go on the field for the anthem, American flags fly on all 16 flag poles around the stadium, and more than 150 Michigan football alumni will stand along the field as the team runs out. The Michigan Marching Band does an extended pregame show featuring "The Cake," and the team does the Wolverine Walk a little over two hours before kickoff.

"Blue Out," Shay says. "So a hundred thousand people dressed like a bruise."

"A hundred thousand people dressed like winners," Gus says. "Wear green if you want to be easy to find."

Gus has been going to games at the Big House since he was old enough to sit still, and he still stands up for the band every single time. Shay has a green flannel she wears to every road game in this rivalry and has never washed it during the season. She says that is tradition. Gus says it is a health concern.

Now the football.

Shay goes first. Alessio Milivojevic runs the Spartan offense, and he takes care of the ball. He has 1,263 yards with 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Against Illinois he went 22 of 26 for 196 yards and 2 touchdowns, and Michigan State lost that one 37-38 in overtime. Against Northwestern it was 21-24. Jaziun Patterson leads the backs with 327 yards and 5 touchdowns. Chrishon McCray leads the receivers with 289 yards. On defense, Devin Vaught has 52 tackles and Eli Coenen has 3.5 sacks.

"We are not a 2-6 team," Shay says. "We are a team that lost close games to people who got lucky."

"You lost 3-31 at Wisconsin," Gus says.

"We don't talk about Madison," Shay says.

Gus takes his turn. Michigan has had two quarterbacks this year. Bryce Underwood leads the team with 924 yards, 5 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Tommy Carr took over the last two games, and at Rutgers he went 22 of 27 for 266 yards and a touchdown in a 28-21 win. JJ Buchanan is the big target with 38 catches for 611 yards and 5 touchdowns. Jordan Marshall leads the backs with 319 yards. The defense is the real story. Michigan gives up 16.4 points a game. Troy Bowles has 57 tackles and John Henry Daley has 4 sacks.

"Our defense held Penn State to 18," Gus says. "Iowa got 20. Indiana got 13 in overtime. Nobody runs on us."

"Nobody scores for you either," Shay says. "You beat Western Michigan 13-12. In your own house."

"A win is a win," Gus says.

"Tell that to the 16 flag poles," Shay says.

History helps Gus. In the ten meetings from 2016 to 2025, Michigan won seven and Michigan State won three. Michigan won 31-20 last year and 24-17 the year before. But Shay remembers 2021, when the Spartans won 37-33, and 2020, when they won 27-24 in Ann Arbor.

"Every few years the green shows up," Shay says. "That's the deal in this state."

"Every few years the green gets lucky," Gus says.

Here's how it plays out. Michigan rides the run early, and the Big House gets loud when the defense forces a three-and-out on the first drive. Milivojevic makes the Wolverines work, hitting McCray on a couple of quick throws and keeping the chains moving into the second quarter. Michigan State gets a field goal and later a touchdown, and Shay jumps so high in the visitors' section that she loses her hat. But the Michigan defense tightens up after halftime. Carr finds Buchanan for the big play that finally breaks it open, and Michigan grinds out the clock in the fourth quarter.

Gus sings "The Victors" all the way to the parking lot. Shay says it is two scores and not a blowout, and that the green flannel stays unwashed until next year.

My call: Michigan Wolverines 26, Michigan State Spartans 15.

display.fanatic_story:
Iowa vs Northwestern prediction for Saturday night in Evanston: two 6-2 teams, a brand-new stadium, and two insiders who have not agreed on anything since the first week of September.

Orrin Kalvelage has had Iowa season tickets for longer than some of these players have been alive. He brings the same thermos to every road game. Ezra Lindqvist lives a short walk from the lake and spent the last two years watching cranes swing over the old site, waiting for the new Ryan Field to open.

It finally did. The new 35,000-seat Ryan Field opened last month after 2 2/3 years of construction, and Saturday is Iowa's first look at it. It is also the first time these two have met since 2024. While the new place was being built, Northwestern played its home games at Northwestern Medicine Field at Martin Stadium, right on the lakefront. Kickoff Saturday is 7:30 p.m. ET.

"Nice building," Orrin says. "Shame about the football."

"The football is 6-2," Ezra says. "Same as yours. And we haven't lost at home."

That's true. Northwestern is 5-0 at home this season. Iowa is ranked No. 21 and walks in off a 30-0 shutout of Wisconsin.

Orrin goes first. The Iowa defense is the whole story. The Hawkeyes allow 12.5 points a game. Cam Buffington leads them with 70 tackles, and Joseph Anderson has 4 sacks. On offense, Hank Brown has been steady with 1,190 yards, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions, and against Wisconsin he went 20 of 24 for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns. Kamari Moulton leads the backs with 541 yards. Tony Diaz leads the receivers with 461 yards.

"We beat Michigan in their own house 20-19," Orrin says. "We'll be fine in a stadium that still smells like paint."

Ezra has heard this speech before. His turn. Aidan Chiles is having the year of his life. He has 1,898 yards, 13 touchdowns and just 1 interception. He also runs. At Oregon last week he had 93 yards on the ground to go with 281 through the air. Griffin Wilde caught 5 balls for 146 yards in that game and has 761 on the season. Caleb Komolafe leads the backs with 618 yards. Braydon Brus does everything on defense, with 67 tackles and 4 sacks.

"We scored 26 at Oregon," Ezra says. "You'd be lucky to score 26 against a high school."

"We scored 30 against Wisconsin and they scored zero," Orrin says.

"Wisconsin scores zero against everybody," Ezra says.

History is close, too. In the nine meetings since 2016, Iowa won five and Northwestern won four. Iowa won the last one 40-14 in 2024. But Northwestern won 21-20 in 2020, 14-10 in 2018 and 38-31 in 2016. Ezra lists every one of them from memory. Orrin says he has blocked those out.

"You can't block out 2020," Ezra says. "It was one point."

"I can block out anything," Orrin says. "I'm from Iowa. We're patient people."

Here's how it plays out. The new stadium is loud from the opening kick, and it gets louder when Chiles scrambles for a first down on the opening drive. Iowa answers the way Iowa always does. Moulton runs it, Brown hits Diaz on third down, and the Hawkeyes keep the ball for what feels like a full quarter. The Iowa defense gets after Chiles and forces a punt or two. It is tight at the half.

In the second half, Chiles finds Wilde deep, and the crowd by the lake finally gets the moment it has been waiting two years for. Iowa comes back with a long drive and makes it a three-point game. The Hawkeyes get the ball back one more time, but Brus gets home on a big third down, and Northwestern holds on.

Orrin pours what is left in the thermos and says the new stadium has bad karma for visitors. Ezra says that is called a home team.

My call: Northwestern Wildcats 24, Iowa Hawkeyes 21.
