Oklahoma vs Florida prediction for Saturday night in Gainesville: the Sooners come in at 4-4, the Gators are 5-3 and ranked No. 25, and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium will be rocking under the lights.

Savannah Redbird-Lowe has had Oklahoma season tickets since she was a student in Norman. She drives a crimson pickup with a Sooner Schooner sticker on the back window. Dax Marchetti grew up a short drive from the Swamp, owns three different orange-and-blue jerseys, and says the heat and noise in Gainesville can break anybody.

This one is the Saluting Those Who Serve game. Florida will honor members of the armed forces, veterans and local first responders, and a ticket gets donated to a local military hero. Outside the O'Connell Center at Gate 2, there's a free Fan Fest that opens three hours before kickoff. Kickoff is 7:45 p.m. ET.

"Fan Fest," Savannah says. "Do they have barbecue?"

"They have everything," Dax says. "Come early."

These two have met before, but not often. Florida won 24-14 in January 2009. Oklahoma won 55-20 in December 2020. Savannah brings up the second one. Dax brings up the first one.

"That was the big one," Dax says.

"That was seventeen years ago," Savannah says. "Ours was more recent."

Savannah goes first. John Mateer is the leader in Norman. He has 1,835 yards, 13 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Last week he went 26 of 43 for 244 yards and 2 touchdowns, but Oklahoma lost 25-42 to South Carolina. Isaiah Sategna III is the top receiver with 591 yards. Lloyd Avant leads the backs with 347 yards. On defense, Adepoju Adebawore has 4 sacks and Owen Heinecke has 63 tackles.

"We beat Texas," Savannah says. "27-24."

"We beat Texas too," Dax says. "27-24. In Austin."

"Same score?" Savannah says.

"Same score," Dax says. "Except ours was on their field."

Dax takes his turn. Florida has a first-year head coach in Jon Sumrall, and the Gators have been fun to watch. Aaron Philo threw for 1,367 yards before Tramell Jones Jr. took over the last two games. Against Texas, Jones went 22 of 35 for 155 yards and 2 touchdowns. Against Georgia, it was tougher. Florida lost 8-27. Jadan Baugh is the workhorse with 801 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. Dallas Wilson leads the receivers with 417 yards. On defense, Jayden Woods has 4.5 sacks and Myles Graham has 55 tackles.

"Baugh is going to run all night," Dax says.

"We'll be ready," Savannah says.

"You gave up 42 to South Carolina," Dax says.

"So did you," Savannah says. "Almost. You gave up 38."

Florida has put up big numbers at home. The Gators scored 66 on Florida Atlantic, 52 on Campbell and 52 on Ole Miss. They also lost 17-45 at Missouri and 19-38 to South Carolina at home. Oklahoma lost 13-41 at Georgia and 13-21 to Kentucky.

Here's how it plays out. The Swamp is loud from the opening kick. Florida gets the ball first and Baugh runs right at the Sooners. He breaks a long run, and the Gators score early. Mateer answers. He hits Sategna for a big gain, then runs it in himself. It is tied after the first quarter.

The game goes back and forth. Florida takes the lead at halftime on another Baugh touchdown. In the third quarter, Mateer leads a long drive, and Oklahoma kicks a field goal. Jones finds a receiver deep in the fourth quarter, and Florida pulls ahead by two scores. Oklahoma answers with a late touchdown, but the Gators recover the onside kick and run out the clock.

Dax says the Swamp is undefeated at night. Savannah says that is not true, and that she will be back.

My call: Florida Gators 28, Oklahoma Sooners 23.

Liberty vs New Mexico State prediction for Saturday night in Las Cruces: the Flames come in at 7-1 and rolling, the Aggies are 3-5 and limping, and it is Homecoming and Ag Day at Aggie Memorial Stadium. Gideon Fairweather says that is nice for the alumni. Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya says that is the whole point.

Gideon has followed Liberty since the program was a small school on a hill in Lynchburg. He knows the fight song by heart and sings it in the car. Esperanza grew up in the Mesilla Valley, eats green chile with every meal, and has a red-and-white Aggies scarf she has worn to every Homecoming since high school. Kickoff is 8 p.m. ET, which is 6 p.m. out in the desert.

"Homecoming," Gideon says. "Who scheduled the Flames for Homecoming?"

"Somebody who likes a challenge," Esperanza says.

This series has history. The two teams have met nine times in the previous eight seasons, which is a lot for two schools that are not close to each other. Liberty has won four straight, including the 49-35 win in the 2023 Conference USA Championship. But Esperanza remembers 2022, when the Aggies beat Liberty 49-14. And 2018, when they won 49-41. Last year it was close, a 30-27 Liberty win.

"Two of nine," Gideon says. "You got two."

"We got two big ones," Esperanza says. "We'll take a third."

Gideon goes first. Deshawn Purdie is the best player on the field, and it is not close. He has 1,453 yards, 10 touchdowns and only 1 interception. Against FIU last week he went 16 of 19 for 227 yards in a 49-10 win. Kam Davis leads the backs with 603 yards and 7 touchdowns. Makai Jackson is the deep threat with 626 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. On defense, Liberty allows 13.5 points a game. Derrell Farrar leads the team with 43 tackles, and Brenton Williams has 4 sacks.

"Our only loss was 13-20 at James Madison," Gideon says. "In the first week."

"You beat Gardner-Webb by one," Esperanza says. "Gardner-Webb."

"A win is a win," Gideon says.

Esperanza takes her turn, and she knows the Aggies have problems. The offense has struggled. Trey Hedden leads the team with 906 throwing yards, but Adam Damante has taken most of the snaps lately. Against Jacksonville State last week, Damante went 6 of 19 for 29 yards, and New Mexico State lost 0-24.

"Zero," Gideon says. "Your team scored zero."

"James Jones ran for 112," Esperanza says. "Look at that instead."

Jones is the real deal. He has 889 rushing yards on 139 carries this season. TK King leads the receivers with 307 yards. The defense has playmakers too. Gabe Peterson has 5.5 sacks, and Nick Session has 58 tackles.

The Aggies have shown what they can do. They beat Western Kentucky 34-13 and won 30-24 at Sam Houston. They also lost 18-42 to New Mexico, which still makes Esperanza angry.

"Don't bring up the Lobos," she says.

"I didn't," Gideon says.

"You were about to," Esperanza says.

Out in Las Cruces, the radio call is on 99.5 FM KXPZ, and Esperanza's grandfather will have it on in the garage, like he does every Homecoming.

Here's how it plays out. Liberty comes out fast. Purdie hits Jackson for a big gain on the first drive, and Davis punches it in. The Homecoming crowd goes quiet for a minute. Then the Aggies do what they do best. Jones runs it, and runs it again, and the Aggies grind out a long drive that ends with a field goal. Peterson gets to Purdie on a third down, and the crowd comes back to life.

In the second half, Liberty's defense makes it tough on the Aggie quarterback. The Flames add two more scores, but Jones keeps running hard into the fourth quarter, and the Aggies find the end zone late. Liberty wins it, but nobody in the stands goes home early.

Esperanza says she will remember every word Gideon said tonight. Gideon sings his fight song the whole way to the parking lot.

My call: Liberty Flames 31, New Mexico State Aggies 16.

West Virginia vs Texas Tech prediction for Saturday night in Lubbock: the Mountaineers come in at 5-3 off a win at TCU, the Red Raiders are 7-1 and ranked No. 13, and it is the Celebrate America Game at Galaxy Stadium.

Jolene Buckhannon grew up in the hills outside Morgantown and still sings "Country Roads" every time she crosses into a new state. Bodie Ratliff is a Lubbock lifer who has a tortilla in his pocket on every home Saturday and says the wind on the South Plains is just weather to him.

"Nice of you to fly out," Bodie says.

"Nice of you to have a stadium we can find," Jolene says. "There's nothing else out here."

Texas Tech calls this one the Celebrate America Game. The school will recognize each branch of the military and its campus military and veterans programs throughout the night. Before the game, fans pack Raider Alley in the Engineering Key, which is free and open to the public, with live music, food, family activities and the Goin' Band from Raiderland. Raider Alley has been part of game day in Lubbock since 1994. Kickoff is 9:30 p.m. ET.

"Raider Alley," Jolene says. "Do they have pepperoni rolls?"

"They have better," Bodie says.

"Nothing is better," Jolene says.

Jolene goes first. West Virginia can score. The Mountaineers put up 35.9 points a game. Michael Hawkins Jr. has 1,598 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Cincinnati, he went 25 of 33 for 464 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 45-42 win. Cam Cook is a workhorse with 923 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns. DJ Epps is the big-play receiver with 556 yards on just 22 catches. On defense, Isaiah Patterson leads the team with 48 tackles.

"We beat TCU 24-20 on the road last week," Jolene says. "We're hot."

"You lost 31-52 to Arizona at home," Bodie says.

"Arizona was a bad day," Jolene says. "Everybody has a bad day."

Bodie takes his turn. Texas Tech is 7-1, and the only loss was 24-37 at Cincinnati. Will Hammond has led the team with 1,561 throwing yards, but Thomas Castellanos took the most snaps last week against Arizona and threw for 144 yards and 2 touchdowns in a 34-26 win. J'Koby Williams ran wild in that game with 175 yards. He has 794 on the season. Kenny Johnson leads the receivers with 548 yards. The defense is the real reason Texas Tech is ranked. A.J. Holmes Jr. has 7.5 sacks, and Austin Romaine has 66 tackles.

"Holmes is going to live in your backfield," Bodie says.

"Hawkins runs," Jolene says. "Good luck catching him."

The long history is close, but lately it has been all Texas Tech. In the ten meetings since 2016, Texas Tech won six and West Virginia won four. Last year Texas Tech won 49-0. The year before that it was 52-15.

"Forty-nine to nothing," Bodie says. "Remember that one?"

"I've moved on," Jolene says. "That was a different team."

"It was last year," Bodie says.

"Different team," Jolene says.

Jolene does have some old wins to point to. West Virginia won 48-17 in 2016, 46-35 in 2017 and 42-34 in 2018. She has those scores memorized and says them like a prayer.

Here's how it plays out. Galaxy Stadium is loud and the flags are out for Celebrate America. Texas Tech gets the ball first and Williams breaks a long run to set up the opening score. West Virginia answers right away. Hawkins finds Epps deep, and Cook finishes the drive. It is a shootout in the first half, and Jolene is on her feet in the visitors' section yelling about every flag.

Then Holmes takes over. He gets to Hawkins twice in the third quarter, and Texas Tech turns those stops into points. The Red Raiders pull away in the fourth. West Virginia keeps scoring, though, and Cook gets a late touchdown that makes Jolene feel a little better on the long drive home.

Bodie says the Red Raiders are headed somewhere special. Jolene says she will be singing "Country Roads" all the way home anyway.

My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 41, West Virginia Mountaineers 24.

display.fanatic_story:
Fresno State vs Utah State prediction for Saturday night in Logan: the Bulldogs come up from the Central Valley at 5-3, the Aggies are 3-5 but just beat Colorado State, and it is going to be cold on the hill at Maverik Stadium.

Roz Ayala has been going to Fresno State games since she was a kid, back when she sat on her dad's shoulders. She wears a red hoodie to every game, no matter how hot or cold it is. Hyrum Tolleson grew up in Cache Valley and walks to the stadium. He says anyone who needs a hoodie in November has never lived in Logan.

Saturday's game is about more than football. Utah State is honoring all military members and first responders. Kickoff is 9:30 p.m. ET, which is 7:30 p.m. in Logan, on Merlin Olsen Field at Maverik Stadium. Current Utah State students can get a free ticket, so the student section should be packed.

"Free tickets," Roz says. "That's the only way you can fill the place."

"We fill it fine," Hyrum says. "Just wait until you hear it."

Roz goes first. Fresno State's offense runs through Jayden Mandal. He has 1,595 throwing yards with 10 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Sacramento State he went 23 of 26 for 316 yards. Last week against Oregon State, he went 11 of 17 for 202 yards and 2 touchdowns in a 38-22 win. Bryson Donelson ran for 108 yards in that game and has 407 on the season. Josiah Freeman leads the receivers with 533 yards and caught 2 touchdowns last week. On defense, K'vion Thunderbird leads with 66 tackles, and Dylan Hampsten has 5 sacks.

"We beat Oregon State by 16," Roz says. "Oregon State scores a ton."

"You lost 0-39 at USC," Hyrum says.

"USC is USC," Roz says. "That was the first game."

Hyrum takes his turn, and he knows the Aggies have been up and down. Utah State has used two quarterbacks this year. Grady Brosterhous leads the team with 1,120 yards, 7 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. But McCae Hillstead took over last week and looked sharp. He went 17 of 22 for 173 yards in a 31-14 win over Colorado State. He also ran for 79 yards and a touchdown. Anthony Garcia was the hero of that game with 11 catches for 121 yards. Javen Jacobs leads the backs with 491 yards. Eli Wood leads the receivers with 479 yards and 5 touchdowns. On defense, Brevin Hamblin has 62 tackles, and Jordan Pendleton has 2.5 sacks.

"We lost to Washington by two," Hyrum says. "On the road. We beat Washington State by one. We lost to Texas State by three. We play everybody close."

"You lost to Idaho State," Roz says.

"We don't talk about that," Hyrum says.

History is pretty even. In the five meetings since 2016, Utah State won three and Fresno State won two. Utah State won 28-17 last year, and Hyrum has the program from that game framed in his basement. Fresno State won 37-32 in 2023 and 35-16 in 2020.

"Three to two," Hyrum says. "We're ahead."

"Not for long," Roz says.

Here's how it plays out. It is cold and the wind is blowing off the mountains. Fresno State gets the ball first, and Mandal hits Freeman on a quick throw to get the Bulldogs moving. The drive stalls and they kick a field goal. Utah State answers with Hillstead. He runs for a first down and then finds Garcia for a big gain. The Aggies kick a field goal of their own.

The game stays tight. Neither team can run away with it. Donelson breaks a long run in the third quarter to give Fresno State the lead. Hillstead finds Wood in the end zone to get Utah State back within two. The Aggies get one more chance late, but Thunderbird makes a big stop, and Fresno State holds on.

Roz takes off her hoodie and waves it over her head in the cold. Hyrum says she will regret that in the morning.

My call: Fresno State Bulldogs 21, Utah State Aggies 19.

"Different player," Neto says.

Juniper Ostrowski grew up in the Willamette Valley, has had the same seats at Reser Stadium for years, and wears a bright orange rain jacket no matter what the sky says.

"First meeting," Yesenia says. "We're making history."

"You're making a long flight home," Juniper says.

Corvallis is ready for the newcomers. Before kickoff, the OSU Alumni Association runs Tailgate Town at the CH2M HILL Alumni Center from 4:30 p.m. until kickoff at 7:30 p.m. Pacific, which is 10:30 p.m. ET. There's barbecue from Pacific Northwest pitmasters, indoor games, photo spots and appearances from OSU Cheer and the OSU Marching Band.

"Barbecue," Yesenia says. "In Oregon."

"Pacific Northwest pitmasters," Juniper says. "It's good."

"I'm from Texas," Yesenia says. "I'll be the judge."

Yesenia goes first. Texas State can score. The Bobcats put up 38.1 points a game. Brad Jackson has 1,933 yards, 18 touchdowns and 5 interceptions. Last week he threw for 327 yards and 4 touchdowns at Boise State, and Texas State lost 45-46. Torrance Burgess Jr. has 922 rushing yards. Chris Dawn Jr. leads the receivers with 467 yards. On defense, Jayden Bradley has 56 tackles, and Tymere Jackson has 3.5 sacks.

"We lost by one at Boise," Yesenia says. "One point. On the blue turf."

"You lost 7-59 at Texas," Juniper says.

"Everybody loses at Texas," Yesenia says.

"We didn't play Texas," Juniper says.

"Lucky you," Yesenia says.

Juniper takes her turn, and she has a lot to work with. Braden Atkinson is putting up huge numbers. He has 2,977 yards, 25 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. Against Colorado State he went 31 of 34 for 427 yards and 5 touchdowns. Against San Diego State it was 409 yards and 5 more touchdowns. Jesse Legree has 1,110 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns. AJ Newberry leads the backs with 465 yards. On defense, Takari Hickle has 6 sacks and Aiden Sullivan has 60 tackles.

"Atkinson is the best quarterback nobody talks about," Juniper says.

"You lost 22-38 at Fresno State last week," Yesenia says.

"Fresno State is tough at home," Juniper says.

The Beavers scored 66 on San Diego State and 56 at Colorado State. Texas State scored 66 on Colorado State and 63 on Incarnate Word. These teams can both put up points in a hurry.

"Sixty-six," Juniper says. "We did it first."

"We did it too," Yesenia says. "So it doesn't count."

Here's how it plays out. It is a cool night at Reser. Oregon State gets the ball first, and Atkinson finds Legree deep for a touchdown on the opening drive. Texas State answers right away. Jackson hits Dawn for a big gain, and Burgess runs it in. That's how the whole first half goes. Score, answer, score, answer.

In the second half, Hickle gets to Jackson on a big third down, and Oregon State gets a field goal out of it. Atkinson finds Legree again early in the fourth quarter to stretch the lead. Texas State keeps fighting. Jackson throws a late touchdown to make it a one-score game, but the Beavers get the ball back and run out the clock.

Juniper says Corvallis made a good first impression. Yesenia says the Bobcats want a rematch someday, in San Marcos, where Juniper can leave the rain jacket at home.

My call: Oregon State Beavers 38, Texas State Bobcats 32.

"Hughes runs like a bull," Colter says. "You'll need three guys to bring him down."

"He also throws interceptions," Monroe-Kalani says. "Seven of them."

"He throws touchdowns too," Colter says.

"Five," Monroe-Kalani says.

Monroe-Kalani takes her turn. Jackson Arnold runs the UNLV offense, and he has been sharp. He has 1,655 yards, 13 touchdowns and 4 interceptions.
